There was a moderate correlation between autoCPAP pressure and OSA (obstructive sleep apnoea) severity (AHI r = 0.34, p = 0.02; oxygen desaturation index (ODI (oxygen desaturation index)) r = 0.48, p < 0.001).

Overall, individuals with OSA (obstructive sleep apnea) had increased VO2max when compared to the normalized US (ultrasound) Air Force data (p<.001). Patients with an apnea-hypopnea index of greater than 20 demonstrated a decreased VO2max as compared to normalized values (p<.001). No differences in VO2max were observed after either medical or surgical therapy for OSA (obstructive sleep apnea).

To provide insight into the factors by which obesity in itself may directly lead to early arterial damage, we aimed to determine early sonographic markers of obesity-related vascular dysfunction in young obese males.
results.reference: In this population, neither BMI nor neck circumference nor waist circumference is predictive of autoCPAP pressure. Therefore, the previously derived algorithm does not adequately predict the fixed CPAP pressure for subsequent clinical use in these obese individuals. In addition, some subjects without OSA generated high autoCPAP pressures, and thus, the correlation between OSA severity and autoCPAP pressure was only moderate.

results.question: Does the clinical presentation of a prior preterm birth predict risk in a subsequent pregnancy?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that the risk of recurrent preterm birth varies based on the clinical presentation of a prior spontaneous preterm birth. Specifically, women with a history of advanced cervical dilatation had a significantly higher rate of recurrent preterm birth and shorter cervical length compared to those with prior PPROM or preterm labor. This supports the idea that the clinical presentation of a prior preterm birth can predict risk in a subsequent pregnancy.

yes
contexts: The objective of the study was to determine whether risk of recurrent preterm birth differs based on the clinical presentation of a prior spontaneous preterm birth (SPTB (spontaneous preterm birth)): advanced cervical dilatation (ACD (advanced cervical dilatation)), preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM (premature rupture of membranes)), or preterm labor (PTL (preterm labor)).

This retrospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies from 2009 to 2014 complicated by a history of prior SPTB (spontaneous preterm birth). Women were categorized based on the clinical presentation of their prior preterm delivery as having ACD (advanced cervical dilatation), PPROM (premature rupture of membranes), or PTL (preterm labor). Risks for sonographic short cervical length and recurrent SPTB (spontaneous preterm birth) were compared between women based on the clinical presentation of their prior preterm birth. Log-linear regression was used to control for confounders.
To determine the ability of early sonogram to predict the presentation of twin A at birth.

Of 522 patients included in this study, 96 (18.4%) had prior ACD (advanced cervical dilatation), 246 (47.1%) had prior PPROM (premature rupture of membranes), and 180 (34.5%) had prior PTL (preterm labor). Recurrent PTB occurred in 55.2% of patients with a history of ACD (advanced cervical dilatation) compared with 27.2% of those with PPROM (premature rupture of membranes) and 32.2% with PTL (P = .001). The mean gestational age at delivery was significantly lower for those with a history of ACD (34.0 weeks) compared with women with prior PPROM (37.2 weeks) or PTL (37.0 weeks) (P = .001). The lowest mean cervical length prior to 24 weeks was significantly shorter in patients with a history of advanced cervical dilation when compared with the other clinical presentations.

We linked two provincial administrative databases containing records on in-patient deliveries and ED (emergency department) visits. The study sample included women who delivered a live singleton baby between April 2003 and March 2004. Pregnant women who made at least one ED (emergency department) visit for asthma were counted as cases and the rest of the women as control subjects. We performed a multivariable analysis using logistic regression to model the risk of having an ED (emergency department) visit for asthma, with fetal gender being one of the predictors. In addition, a series of multivariable logistic regressions were also constructed separately for cases and controls for the following adverse delivery outcomes: low birth weight baby, preterm delivery, and delivery via Caesarian section.
results.reference: Patients with a history of ACD are at an increased risk of having recurrent preterm birth and cervical shortening in a subsequent pregnancy compared with women with prior preterm birth associated PPROM or PTL.

results.question: Is the Distance Worth It?
results.answer:
The evidence suggests that traveling longer distances to high-volume centers is associated with better outcomes, including higher lymph node yield, more neoadjuvant chemoradiation, and lower short-term and overall mortality compared to staying local at low-volume centers. Although travel burden is a concern, the improved survival and treatment quality indicate that the distance may be justified for rectal cancer patients.

yes
contexts: Distance to provider might be an important barrier to timely diagnosis and treatment for cancer patients who qualify for Medicaid coverage. Whether driving time or driving distance is a better indicator of travel burden is also of interest.

A total of 18,605 patients met inclusion criteria; 2067 patients were in the long-distance/high-volume group and 1362 in the short-distance/low-volume group. The median travel distance was 62.6 miles for the long-distance/high-volume group and 2.3 miles for the short-distance/low-volume group. Patients who were younger, white, privately insured, and stage III were more likely to have traveled to a high-volume center. When controlled for patient factors, stage, and hospital factors, patients in the short-distance/low-volume group had lower odds of a lymph node yield ≥12 (OR = 0.51) and neoadjuvant chemoradiation (OR = 0.67) and higher 30-day (OR = 3.38) and 90-day mortality (OR = 2.07) compared with those in the long-distance/high-volume group. The short-distance/low-volume group had a 34% high risk of overall mortality at 5 years compared with the long-distance/high-volume group.

Of the 361 patients invited, 267 (74%) refused participation. These refusers were more restricted in their mobility, lived further away from the location of the intervention, and had a partner more often than did the participants. No differences were found in level of education, age or gender. The main reasons given by respondents for refusing to participate were lack of time, travel distance, and transport problems.
It is unclear whether traveling long distances to high-volume centers would compensate for travel burden among patients undergoing rectal cancer resection.

The vertical distance between the tibial tuberosity and tibial cut averaged 24.7 ± 4 mm. The average vertical distance from tibial tuberosity to proximal and to distal PCL footprint was found to be 22 ± 4.4 and 16 ± 4.4 mm, respectively. Five knees were considered at 50% risk of an entire PCL removal after CR TKA (total knee arthroplasty).
results.reference: Our results indicate that when controlled for patient, tumor, and hospital factors, patients who traveled a long distance to a high-volume center had improved lymph node yield, neoadjuvant chemoradiation receipt, and 30- and 90-day mortality compared with those who traveled a short distance to a low-volume center. They also had improved 5-year survival. See Video Abstract at http://links.lww.com/DCR/A446.

results.question: Aripiprazole: a new risk factor for pathological gambling?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that aripiprazole may be a new risk factor for pathological gambling, as the probability that pathological gambling is due to aripiprazole was considered "possible" in 7 out of 8 cases analyzed. These cases involved patients with a history of addictive disorders and gambling prior to aripiprazole prescription, suggesting a potential causal link.

yes
contexts: It is commonly accepted that pathological gambling results from the interaction of multiple risk factors. Among these, dopamine replacement therapy (DRT (dopamine replacement therapy)) prescribed for Parkinson disease can be cited. Another dopamine agonist, aripiprazole, could be a new risk factor. We decided to explore this potential adverse drug reaction (ADR (adverse drug reaction)).

The patients involved were schizophrenic or bipolar, mostly young men with a history of addictive disorders and regular gambling prior to the prescription of aripiprazole. For each one of them, the causality of aripiprazole was considered, using an algorithm. The probability that pathological gambling is actually due to aripiprazole is "possible" in 7 cases out of 8, and "doubtful" in one.
Based on a cohort of 166 pathological gamblers starting treatment in our department, data of each of the 8 patients treated by aripiprazole at inclusion were analyzed.

Most participants (73.5%) wandered; all showed PNA (physically nonaggressive agitation) behaviors. Factor analyses yielded an one-factor solution for wandering (explained variance = 43.66%) and a two-factor solution for PNA (explained variance = 53.45%). Overall wandering correlated significantly with PNA (physically nonaggressive agitation) Factor 1 (df =179, r = 0.68, p<0.001) and Factor 2, but at a lower value (df = 179, r = 0.26, p<0.01).

To examine the representativeness of a randomized controlled trial (RCT (randomized controlled trial)) sample versus one obtained by consecutive new case ascertainment, for subjects with child bipolar I disorder.
results.reference: Adverse drug reactions were confronted with other already published case reports. Dopamine partial agonist mechanism of aripiprazole could explain the occurrence of pathological gambling.

results.question: Immune suppression by lysosomotropic amines and cyclosporine on T-cell responses to minor and major histocompatibility antigens: does synergy exist?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that lysosomotropic amines such as chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine suppress T-cell responses to minor histocompatibility antigens (MiHC) and that when combined with cyclosporine, there is a synergistic suppression of T-cell proliferative responses to MiHC. Similar synergy is also observed in responses to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) antigens. Therefore, the evidence supports the existence of synergy between lysosomotropic amines and cyclosporine in immune suppression of T-cell responses to both minor and major histocompatibility antigens.

yes
contexts: Using murine models, we have shown that the lysosomotropic amine, chloroquine, is effective in the prevention of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD (graft-versus-host disease)) mediated by donor T cells reactive with recipient minor histocompatibility antigens (MiHCs (minor histocompatibility antigens)). Because lysosomotropic amines can suppress major histocompatibility complex (MHC (major histocompatibility complex)) class II antigen presentation, their mechanism of action is potentially different from current immune suppressant drugs used to control GVHD (graft-versus-host disease) such as cyclosporine.

We investigated the use of cyclosporine and the lysosomotropic amines chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine in combination for additive or synergistic immunosuppression on T-cell responses in vitro to MiHC and MHC (major histocompatibility complex) in mice.

We found that similar concentrations of chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine suppress the T-cell response to MiHC in mice (C57BL/6 anti-BALB.B) and that lysosomotropic amines in combination with cyclosporine result in synergistic suppression of a proliferative response to MiHC. Similar suppression and synergy appear to be present in an alloreactive response (C57BL/6 anti-BALB/c). Direct inhibition by chloroquine of T-cell proliferative responses induced by anti-CD3epsilon in the absence of antigen-presenting cells is present at higher concentrations than that required to suppress responses to MiHC or MHC (major histocompatibility complex). Chloroquine appears to induce decreased T-cell viability at high concentrations. This effect does not appear to be due to decreased T-cell production of interleukin-2 or interferon-gamma. At lower concentrations (<25 microg/ml), chloroquine can also decrease the ability of antigen-presenting cells to stimulate an a C57BL/6 anti-BALB/c T-cell response and can inhibit MHC (major histocompatibility complex) class II expression after activation with lipopolysaccharide.
The aim of this study was to analyze the properties of the immune cell microenvironment of regional lymph nodes (LNs (lymph nodes)) positive for lung cancer.

A 10-year-old boy developed very severe aplastic anemia (VSAA (very severe aplastic anemia)) after being admitted to our hospital with a fulminant hepatic failure of unknown origin. A chest computed tomography scan revealed multiple lung nodules and a biopsy of a pulmonary lesion showed all the signs of AFOP (acute fibrinous and organizing pneumonia). Infectious workup remained negative. We started immunosuppressive therapy with antithymocyte globulin and cyclosporine to treat VSAA (very severe aplastic anemia). Subsequent chest computed tomography scans showed a considerable diminution of the lung lesions but the VSAA (very severe aplastic anemia) did not improve until we performed hematopoietic stem cell transplantation 5 months later.
results.reference: Lysosomotropic amines in combination with cyclosporine appear to be synergistic in the suppression of T-cell proliferation to MiHC and MHC. Use of chloroquine in combination with cyclosporine may result in improved control of GVHD.

results.question: Does induction chemotherapy have a role in the management of nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that induction chemotherapy was given to a subset of patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma, particularly those with Stage IV disease, and was associated with improved 5-year overall survival (68% vs. 56%), freedom from relapse (64% vs. 37%), and local control (86% vs. 56%) compared to those who did not receive induction chemotherapy. This suggests that induction chemotherapy has a beneficial role in the management of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

yes
contexts: To assess the outcomes of patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC (nasopharyngeal carcinoma)) whose treatment was determined by computerized tomography (CT (computerized tomography)) and/or magnetic resonance imaging staging and to analyze the impact of induction chemotherapy and accelerated fractionated radiotherapy.

The analysis is based on 122 of 143 previously untreated patients with NPC (nasopharyngeal carcinoma) treated with radiation therapy at The University of Texas M. D. Anderson Cancer Center between 1983 and 1992. Excluded were 4 patients treated with palliative intent, 4 children, 12 patients not staged with CT (computerized tomography), and 1 patient who died of a cerebrovascular accident prior to completion of treatment. The stage distribution was as follows: AJCC Stage I-2, Stage II-7, Stage III-12, Stage IV-101; Tl-15, T2-33, T3 (triiodothyronine)-22, T4 (thyroxine)-52; N0-32, N1-10, N2-47, N3-32, Nx-1. Fifty-nine (48%) patients had squamous cell carcinoma; 63 (52%) had lymphoepitheliomas, undifferentiated NPC (nasopharyngeal carcinoma) or poorly differentiated carcinoma, NOS (UNPC (undifferentiated npc or poorly differentiated carcinoma, nos)). Sixty-seven patients (65 with Stage IV disease) received induction chemotherapy. Fifty-eight patients (24 of whom had induction chemotherapy) were treated with the concomitant boost fractionation schedule. The median follow-up for surviving patients was 57 months.

Few studies have assessed whether the advantage chemotherapy has been shown to have in treating advanced non-small lung carcinoma in clinical trials is transferrable to normal health care activity. This could explain the skepticism of a large number of pneumologists towards this treatment. The objective of our study was to analyze prognostic factors related to survival and to see whether cytostatic treatment was an independent predictor.

The overall actuarial 2- and 5-year survival rates were 78 and 68%, respectively. Forty-nine patients (40%) had disease recurrence. Thirty-three (27%) had local regional failures; 19 at the primary site only, 8 in the neck and 6 in both. Local failure occurred in 31% of patients staged T4 (thyroxine) compared to 13% of T1-T3 (p = 0.007). Sixteen patients failed at distant sites alone. Among Stage IV patients the 5-year actuarial rates for patients who did and did not receive induction chemotherapy were as follows: overall survival: 68 vs. 56% (p = 0.02), freedom from relapse: 64 vs. 37% (p = 0.01), and local control: 86 vs. 56% (p = 0.009). The actuarial 5-year distant failure rate in patients with UNPC (undifferentiated npc or poorly differentiated carcinoma, nos) who were treated with induction chemotherapy and controlled in the primary and neck was 13%. In patients who did not receive chemotherapy, the actuarial 5-year local control rates for patients treated with concomitant boost or conventional fractionation were 66 and 67%, respectively.
The present study aims to evaluate benefit of adding surgery to chemoradiotherapy alone in management of carcinoma esophagus.
results.reference: While not providing conclusive evidence, this single institution experience suggests that neoadjuvant chemotherapy for Stage IV NPC patients improves both survival and disease control. Recurrence within the irradiated volume was the most prevalent mode of failure and future studies will evaluate regimens to enhance local regional control.

results.question: Treatment of contralateral hydrocele in neonatal testicular torsion: Is less more?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that managing contralateral hydrocele in neonatal testicular torsion solely through a scrotal approach, without inguinal exploration, is safe and effective. None of the patients treated this way developed clinical hydrocele or hernia after long-term follow-up, supporting a less invasive approach.

yes
contexts: Treatment of neonatal testicular torsion has two objectives: salvage of the involved testicle (which is rarely achieved) and preservation of the contralateral gonad. The second goal universally involves contralateral testicular scrotal fixation to prevent the future occurrence of contralateral torsion. However, there is controversy with regards to management of a synchronous contralateral hydrocele. It has been our policy not to address the contralateral hydrocele through an inguinal incision to minimize potential injury to the spermatic cord. Our objective in this study was to determine whether the decision to manage a contralateral hydrocele in cases of neonatal testicular torsion solely through a scrotal approach is safe and effective.

Thirty-seven patients were identified as presenting with neonatal torsion. Age of presentation averaged 3.5 days (range 1-14 days). Left-sided pathology was seen more commonly than the right, with a 25:12 distribution. All torsed testicles were nonviable. Twenty-two patients were noted to have a contralateral hydrocele at presentation. All hydroceles were opened through a scrotal approach at the time of contralateral scrotal fixation. No patient underwent an inguinal exploration to examine for a patent process vaginalis. None of the patients who presented with a hydrocele have developed a clinical hydrocele or hernia after an average 7.5 years (range 4.3-11.2) follow-up.

We reviewed all cases of neonatal testicular torsion occurring at our institution between the years 1999 and 2006. Age at presentation, physical examination, ultrasonographic and intraoperative findings were recorded. Patients were followed after initial surgical intervention to determine the likelihood of developing a subsequent hydrocele or hernia.

There is controversy surrounding the optimal management of the testicular remnant associated with the vanishing testes syndrome. Some urologists advocate the need for surgical exploration, whereas others believe this is unnecessary. These differing opinions are based on the variable reports of viable germ cell elements found within the testicular remnants. To better understand the pathology associated with this syndrome and the need for surgical management, we reviewed our experience regarding the incidence of viable germ cell elements within the testicular remnant.

Fifty-six patients underwent removal of the testicular remnant. Patient age ranged from 11 to 216 months. In 8 of the specimens (14%), we identified viable germ cell elements. In an additional 4 patients (7%), we identified seminiferous tubules without germ cell elements.
results.reference: We have demonstrated that approaching a contralateral hydrocele in cases of neonatal testicular torsion solely through a scrotal incision is safe and effective. Inguinal exploration was not performed in our study and our long-term results demonstrate that such an approach would have brought no additional benefit. In avoiding an inguinal approach we did not subject our patients to unnecessary risk of testicular or vasal injury. Contralateral hydrocele is commonly seen in cases of neonatal testicular torsion. In our experience this is a condition of minimal clinical significance and does not warrant formal inguinal exploration for treatment. This conservative management strategy minimizes the potential of contralateral spermatic cord injury in the neonate. The aims of the study were met.

results.question: Are normally sighted, visually impaired, and blind pedestrians accurate and reliable at making street crossing decisions?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that normally sighted and visually impaired pedestrians are accurate and reliable in their street crossing decisions when using vision plus hearing or vision only. However, blind pedestrians are less accurate under the hearing only condition, though they remain reliable. Overall, the evidence supports that these groups are generally accurate and reliable in making street crossing decisions when visual information is available.

yes
contexts: We found that normally sighted and visually impaired pedestrians were accurate and reliable in their street crossing decision-making ability when using either vision plus hearing or vision only (P>0.05). Under the hearing only condition, all subjects were reliable (P>0.05) but inaccurate with their street crossing decisions (P<0.05). Compared to either the normally sighted (P = 0.018) or visually impaired subjects (P = 0.019), blind subjects were the least accurate with their street crossing decisions under the hearing only condition.

The purpose of this study is to measure the accuracy and reliability of normally sighted, visually impaired, and blind pedestrians at making street crossing decisions using visual and/or auditory information.

Using a 5-point rating scale, safety ratings for vehicular gaps of different durations were measured along a two-lane street of one-way traffic without a traffic signal. Safety ratings were collected from 12 normally sighted, 10 visually impaired, and 10 blind subjects for eight different gap times under three sensory conditions: (1) visual plus auditory information, (2) visual information only, and (3) auditory information only. Accuracy and reliability in street crossing decision-making were calculated for each subject under each sensory condition.

The 56 participants were originally recruited for a prospective study on driving and community re-integration post-stroke; the study population consisted of moderately impaired stroke survivors without severe communication disorders who had been referred for a driving assessment. The driving records of the 56 participants for the 5 years before study entry and the 1-year study period were acquired with written consent from the Ministry of Transportation of Ontario (MTO (ministry of transportation of ontario)), Canada. Self-reports of collisions and convictions were acquired via a semistructured interview and then compared with the MTO (ministry of transportation of ontario) records.

Neuropsychological test measures, including the visual reproduction, digit span, and logical memory subtests of the Wechsler memory scale (revised), the Trail Making test, Wisconsin Card Sorting test, Hopkins Verbal Learning test, Controlled Oral Word Association, and the Galveston Orientation and Amnesia test (GOAT (galveston orientation and amnesia test)).
results.reference: Our data suggested that visually impaired pedestrians can make accurate and reliable street crossing decisions like those of normally sighted pedestrians. When using auditory information only, all subjects significantly overestimated the vehicular gap time. Our finding that blind pedestrians performed significantly worse than either the normally sighted or visually impaired subjects under the hearing only condition suggested that they may benefit from training to improve their detection ability and/or interpretation of vehicular gap times.

results.question: Is it Crohn's disease?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts discuss colorectal cancer, celiac disease, Hirschsprung's disease, and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), but none mention Crohn's disease or provide information related to it. Therefore, there is no evidence in the given context to support or refute the question about Crohn's disease.

no
contexts: The incidence of colorectal cancer in young patients is increasing. It remains unclear if the disease has unique features in this age group.

Celiac disease (CD (celiac disease)) is an autoimmune enteropathy characterized by villus atrophy and malabsorption of essential nutrients. Vitamin D deficiency has been described in autoimmune diseases, but its status in prepubertal children with CD (celiac disease) has not been adequately studied.

The correlation between radiographic transition zone on contrast enema in Hirschsprung's disease and the total length of aganglionosis is known to be inaccurate. The aim of our study was to analyse this correlation more precisely to improve preoperative planning of the corrective surgery.

Celiac disease (CD (celiac disease)) is believed to be a permanent intolerance to gluten. A number of patients, however, discontinue the gluten-free diet (GFD (gluten-free diet)) without developing symptoms or signs. The aim of our study was to investigate whether CD (celiac disease) patients are capable of developing tolerance to gluten.

A cross sectional study of 38 patients fulfilling the classification criteria for SLE. The patients visited a rheumatology outpatient clinic in Switzerland between January 2002 and December 2004. The last assessment during this period was used for the study. The assessment included, besides demographic data, the measurement of disease activity using the BILAG index, the measurement of disease damage using the SLICC/ACR damage index (SDI (slicc/acr damage index)), as well as the patient's self assessed health status using the patient's questionnaire Medical Outcome Survey Short Form 36 (SF-36).
results.reference: Granulomatous myelotoxicity and enteritis developed in a 21 year old female within 3 weeks of initiating sulfasalazine for rheumatoid arthritis. Following a short course of corticosteroids, the patient had resolution of her cholestatic hepatitis, rash, eosinophilia, and gastrointestinal symptoms with no residual manifestations at 7 months follow-up. Although severe reactions to sulfasalazine are rare and unpredictable, practicing physicians should be aware of unusual clinical presentations of toxicity when prescribing sulfasalazine.

results.question: Is Chaalia/Pan Masala harmful for health?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that a large majority of children using Chaalia and Pan Masala consider these substances harmful for health (96% for Chaalia and 60% for Pan Masala). Additionally, knowledge about established harmful effects was assessed and found to be variable but generally high among users, suggesting recognized health risks associated with these substances.

yes
contexts: To determine the practices and knowledge of harmful effects regarding use of Chaalia and Pan Masala in three schools of Mahmoodabad and Chanesar Goth, Jamshed Town, Karachi, Pakistan.

A total of 370 students were interviewed over a period of six weeks, of which 205 (55.4%) were boys. The ages of the students were between 10 and 15 years. Thirty one percent of the fathers and 62% of the mothers were uneducated. The frequency of use of any brand of Chaalia was found to be 94% and that of Pan Masala was 73.8%. Eighty five percent of them were regular users. A large majority (88%) procured the substances themselves from near their homes. Ninety five percent of the children had friends with the same habits. Eighty four percent were using the substances in full knowledge of their families. Chaalia was considered harmful for health by 96% and Pan Masala by 60%. Good taste was cited as a reason for continuing the habit by 88.5% of the children and use by friends by 57%. Knowledge about established harmful effects was variable. Knowledge about harmful effects was high in both "daily" and "less than daily users".

To achieve the objective a cross-sectional design was used in three government schools of Mahmoodabad and Chanesar Goth, Jamshed Town, Karachi. Students of either gender drawn from these schools fulfilling the inclusion and exclusion criteria were interviewed using a pre-coded structured questionnaire. Along with demographic data, questions regarding frequency of Chaalia and Pan Masala use, practices of this habit in friends and family and place of procurement of these substances, were inquired. Knowledge was assessed about harmful effects and its source of information. In addition, practices in relation to that knowledge were assessed.

The strategic use of PMS (performance measurement systems) in health care organizations directly and significantly (p < 0.001) enhances performance in terms of improved processes. Perceived managerial discretion is positively and significantly (p < 0.001) affected by the strategic use of PMS (performance measurement systems), whereas the mediation effect is non-significant.

A comparative survey of information held on the Child Health Computing System (CHCS (child health computing system)) and the Northern Ireland Cerebral Palsy Register (NICPR (northern ireland cerebral palsy register)) in one Health and Social Services Board in Northern Ireland was carried out. The sample comprised children with cerebral palsy aged 5-9 years.
results.reference: The frequency of habits of Chaalia and Pan Masala chewing, by school children in lower socio-economic areas is extremely high. The probable reasons for this high frequency are taste, the widespread use of these substances by family members and friends, low cost and easy availability.

results.question: Does multi-modal cervical physical therapy improve tinnitus in patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus?
results.answer:
The provided study shows that multimodal cervical physical therapy significantly decreased tinnitus severity (TFI scores) and neck complaints (NBQ scores) in patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus. Additionally, 53% of patients experienced substantial improvement immediately after treatment, supporting the effectiveness of this therapy for tinnitus in these patients.

yes
contexts: To investigate the effect of a multimodal cervical physical therapy treatment on tinnitus complaints in patients with CST (cervicogenic somatic tinnitus).

Tinnitus can be related to many different aetiologies such as hearing loss or a noise trauma, but it can also be related to the somatosensory system of the cervical spine, called cervicogenic somatic tinnitus (CST (cervicogenic somatic tinnitus)). Case studies suggest a positive effect of cervical spine treatment on tinnitus complaints in patients with CST (cervicogenic somatic tinnitus), but no experimental studies are available.

Patients with a combination of severe subjective tinnitus (Tinnitus Functional Index (TFI): 25-90 points) and neck complaints (Neck Bournemouth Questionnaire (NBQ (neck bournemouth questionnaire)) > 14 points).
All patients received cervical physical therapy for 6 weeks (12 sessions). Patients were randomized in an immediate-start therapy group (n = 19) and a 6-week delayed-start therapy group (n = 19).

In all patients (n = 38) TFI and NBQ (neck bournemouth questionnaire)-scores decreased significantly after treatment (p = 0.04 and p < 0.001). NBQ (neck bournemouth questionnaire)-scores remained significantly lower after follow-up (p = 0.001). Immediately after treatment, 53% (n = 38) experienced substantial improvement of tinnitus. This effect was maintained in 24% of patients after follow-up at six weeks.
results.reference: Cervical physical therapy can have a positive effect on subjective tinnitus complaints in patients with a combination of tinnitus and neck complaints. Larger studies, using more responsive outcome measures, are however necessary to prove this effect.

results.question: Detailed analysis of sputum and systemic inflammation in asthma phenotypes: are paucigranulocytic asthmatics really non-inflammatory?
results.answer:
The data show that paucigranulocytic asthmatics have increased sputum eosinophils and elevated absolute blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects, indicating the presence of inflammation despite the paucity of granulocytes. Therefore, paucigranulocytic asthma cannot be considered truly non-inflammatory based on these findings.

no
contexts: The technique of induced sputum has allowed to subdivide asthma patients into inflammatory phenotypes according to their level of granulocyte airway infiltration. There are very few studies which looked at detailed sputum and blood cell counts in a large cohort of asthmatics divided into inflammatory phenotypes. The purpose of this study was to analyze sputum cell counts, blood leukocytes and systemic inflammatory markers in these phenotypes, and investigate how those groups compared with healthy subjects.

The total non-squamous cell count per gram of sputum was greater in mixed granulocytic and neutrophilic phenotypes as compared to eosinophilic, paucigranulocytic asthma and healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Sputum eosinophils (in absolute values and percentages) were increased in all asthma phenotypes including paucigranulocytic asthma, compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Eosinophilic asthma showed higher absolute sputum neutrophil and lymphocyte counts than healthy subjects (p < 0.005), while neutrophilic asthmatics had a particularly low number of sputum macrophages and epithelial cells. All asthma phenotypes showed an increased blood leukocyte count compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005), with paucigranulocytic asthmatics having also increased absolute blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Neutrophilic asthma had raised CRP (C reactive protein) and fibrinogen while eosinophilic asthma only showed raised fibrinogen compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005).

We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study on 833 asthmatics recruited from the University Asthma Clinic of Liege and compared them with 194 healthy subjects. Asthmatics were classified into inflammatory phenotypes.

We hypothesized that if the inflammation of the airway wall influences to some extent and in some way the PD (perception of dyspnea) in asthma patients, ICSs (inhaled corticosteroids) reverse the effect of airway inflammation on the PD (perception of dyspnea).

Some of the disagreements on the perception of dyspnea (PD (perception of dyspnea)) during bronchoconstriction in asthma patients could depend on the interrelationships among the following: (1) the influence of baseline airflow obstruction on the patient's ability to detect any further increase in airway resistance; (2) the effect of eosinophilic inflammation on the airway; (3) bronchial hyperresponsiveness (BHR (bronchial hyperresponsiveness)); and (4) the effect of inhaled corticosteroids (ICSs (inhaled corticosteroids)).
results.reference: This study demonstrates that a significant eosinophilic inflammation is present across all categories of asthma, and that paucigranulocytic asthma may be seen as a low grade inflammatory disease.

results.question: Is HIV/STD control in Jamaica making a difference?
results.answer:
The data indicate that the HIV/STD control program in Jamaica has had a positive impact, as evidenced by only a marginal increase in AIDS incidence rates, stable low HIV prevalence in the general population, declines in syphilis rates and congenital syphilis cases, and significant increases in condom use across various groups. These findings suggest that the control efforts are contributing to controlling the epidemic.

yes
contexts: To assess the impact of the comprehensive HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/STD (sexually transmitted disease) Control Program established in Jamaica since the late 1980s on the HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) epidemic.

The annual AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) incidence rate in Jamaica increased only marginally in the past three years from 18.5 per 100000 population to 21.4 in 1997. HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) prevalence in the general population groups tested has been about 1% or less. Among those at high risk, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) prevalence rates have risen to 6.3% (95% confidence interval 5.0-8.0) in STD (sexually transmitted disease) clinic attenders, around 10% and 21% in female prostitutes in Kingston and Montego Bay respectively and approximately 30% among homosexuals. Syphilis rates and congenital syphilis cases have declined. The proportion of men aged 15-49 years reporting sex with a non-regular partner declined from 35% in 1994 to 26% in 1996 (P<0.001). Women ever having used condoms increased from 51% in 1988 to 62.5% in 1992 and 73% in 1994 and 1996 (P<0.001), while condom use with a non-regular partner increased from 37% in 1992 to 73% in 1996 (P= 0.006). Condom use among men was high over the period: around 81% had ever used condoms and 77% used them with non-regular partners. Gay men, inner-city adults and adolescents aged 12-14 years all reported increases in condom use while condom sales and distribution increased from around 2 million in 1985 to 10 million in 1995.

AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) case reports, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) testing of blood donors, antenatal clinic attenders (ANC (antenatal clinic attenders)), food service workers, sexually transmitted disease (STD (sexually transmitted disease)) clinic attenders, female prostitutes, homosexuals and other groups were used to monitor the HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) epidemic. Primary and secondary syphilis and cases of congenital syphilis were also monitored. National knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP (knowledge, attitude and practice)) surveys were conducted in 1988, 1989, 1992, 1994 and 1996.

To determine whether the OraQuick® HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-1/2 Assay (OraSure Technologies, Inc., Bethlehem, PA, USA) in sputum is a valid tool for HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) surveillance among TB (tuberculosis) patients.

The number of new diagnoses of HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) infection is rising in the northwestern hemisphere and it is becoming increasingly important to understand the mechanisms behind this trend.
results.reference: HIV/STD control measures appear to have slowed the HIV/AIDS epidemic in Jamaica, however a significant minority of persons continue to have unprotected sex in high risk situations.

results.question: Is Panton-Valentine leucocidin associated with the pathogenesis of Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia in the UK?
results.answer:
The data show that only a very small proportion (1.6%) of Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia isolates in the UK and Ireland were PVL-positive, and these were all methicillin-susceptible strains. No PVL-positive isolates were found among methicillin-resistant strains, and the clinical significance of PVL in these bacteraemia cases remains uncertain. Therefore, the evidence does not support a strong association between PVL and the pathogenesis of S. aureus bacteraemia in this setting.

no
contexts: The morbidity and mortality associated with Panton-Valentine leucocidin (PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin))-positive Staphylococcus aureus suggest that this toxin is a key marker of disease severity. Nevertheless, the importance of PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin) in the pathogenesis of primary bacteraemia caused by S. aureus is uncertain. We have determined the prevalence of PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-encoding genes among isolates of S. aureus from bacteraemic patients.

Consecutive bacteraemia isolates of S. aureus (n=244) from patients hospitalized in 25 centres in the UK and Ireland during 2005 were screened for PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin) and mecA genes. PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive isolates were characterized by toxin gene profiling, PFGE, spa-typing and MIC determinations for a range of antimicrobials.

Four out of 244 isolates (1.6%) were PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive and susceptible to oxacillin [methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA)]. Eighty-eight out of 244 (36%) were oxacillin-resistant (methicillin-resistant S. aureus), but none was PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive. The four patients (two males: 30 and 33 years; two females: 62 and 80 years) had infection foci of: skin and soft tissue, unknown, indwelling line, and surgical site, and were located at one centre in Wales, one in England and two in Ireland. One of four PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive isolates was resistant to penicillin and fusidic acid, the remainder were susceptible to all antibiotics tested. Genotypic analyses showed that the four isolates represented three distinct strains; the two isolates from Ireland were related.

Adoption and implementation of evidence-based measures for catheter care leads to reductions in central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI (central line-associated bloodstream infection)) rates in the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit). The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether this rate reduction is sustainable for at least 1 year and to identify key determinants of this sustainability at the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) of the Floating Hospital for Children at Tufts Medical Center.

Infection control rate was 31% in retention and 59% in the removal group after initial surgical treatment, and 81% and 91% at latest followup, respectively. Treatment duration was shorter in the retention group and there was no difference in number of additional surgeries and length of hospital stay. Type of treatment (retention versus removal) was the only factor associated with infection control; subgroup analysis in the retention group showed Staphylococcus aureus infection and polyethylene nonexchange as contributing factors for failure of infection control.
results.reference: We found that 1.6% of S. aureus (all MSSA) from bacteraemic patients were PVL-positive. This low incidence suggests that PVL-positive S. aureus are of no particular significance as causative agents of S. aureus bacteraemia.

results.question: Are even impaired fasting blood glucose levels preoperatively associated with increased mortality after CABG surgery?
results.answer:
The study in abstract [4] shows that non-diabetic patients with impaired fasting glucose (IFG) had higher relative risks of 30-day and 1-year mortality after CABG compared to those with normal fasting blood glucose, although the confidence intervals are wide and include 1 for some comparisons. This suggests an association between even impaired fasting glucose levels preoperatively and increased mortality after CABG surgery.

yes
contexts: Impaired fasting glucose (IFG (impaired fasting glucose)) below the diagnostic threshold for diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)) is associated with macrovascular pathology and increased mortality after percutaneous coronary interventions. The study goal was to determine whether pre-operative fasting blood glucose (fB-glu) is associated with an increased mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting)).

The anesthetical-surgical procedure presented a mortality rate of 3.125% (1:32) and a morbidity rate of 6.25% (2:32). It was evidenced an initial mean blood glucose = 199.4 mg/dl and the end = 326.1 mg/dl. In spite of extended fasting (minimum of 2 hours for the absolute fasting and maximum of 8.5 hours for liquids, and 20.5 hours for solids) all animals presented at the end of the surgical procedure any gastric content and a blood glucose increase. Those with fasting for liquids and solids when compared to the quantity of solid gastric content, presented a moderate negative degree of correlation.

Both fasting and 2-hour plasma glucose levels were associated with higher Framingham risk score (fasting glucose: r(2) = 0.21; 2-hour glucose: r(2) = 0.24; P<0.001 for both), and insulin sensitivity with lower Framingham risk score (r(2) = 0.36; P<0.001). However, adjustment for insulin sensitivity and 2-hour glucose made the effect of fasting glucose non-significant (P = 0.060). Likewise, when adjusting for insulin sensitivity and fasting glucose, the association between 2-hour glucose and Framingham risk score disappeared (P = 0.143). In contrast, insulin sensitivity was still associated with Framingham risk score after adjusting for glucose levels (P<0.001). Body fat was not associated with Framingham risk score when taking insulin sensitivity into account (P = 0.550).

During 2001-03, 1895 patients underwent primary CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) [clinical DM (CDM (clinical dm)) in 440/1895; complete data on fB-glu for n=1375/1455]. Using pre-operative fB-glu, non-diabetics were categorized as having normal fB-glu (<5.6 mmol/L), IFG (5.6<or =fB-glu<6.1 mmol/L), or suspected DM (SDM (suspected dm)) (>or =6.1 mmol/L). fB-glu was normal in 59%. The relative risks of 30 day and 1 year mortality compared with patients with normal fB-glu was 1.7 [95% confidence interval (CI (confidence interval)): 0.5-5.5] and 2.9 (CI (confidence interval): 0.8-11.2) with IFG (impaired fasting glucose), 2.8 (CI (confidence interval): 1.1-7.2) and 1.9 (CI (confidence interval): 0.5-6.3) with SDM (suspected dm) vs. 1.8 (CI (confidence interval): 0.8-4.0) and 1.6 (CI (confidence interval): 0.6-4.3) if CDM (clinical dm), respectively. The receiver operator characteristic area for the continuous variable fB-glu and 1 year mortality was 0.65 (P=0.002).

In 60 middle-aged individuals without diabetes we studied the associations of fasting plasma glucose, 2-hour post oral glucose tolerance test plasma glucose, insulin sensitivity as well as body fat percentage with CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk. Insulin sensitivity was measured as the glucose infusion rate during a euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamp, body fat percentage was measured by dual X-ray absorptiometry, and CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk was estimated using the Framingham risk score. Associations of fasting plasma glucose, 2-hour plasma glucose, insulin sensitivity and body fat percentage with the Framingham risk score were assessed in linear regression models.
results.reference: The elevated risk of death after CABG surgery known previously to be associated with CDM seems also to be shared by a group of similar size that includes patients with IFG and undiagnosed DM.

results.question: Does positron emission tomography change management in primary rectal cancer?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that positron emission tomography (PET) scanning changed the management in 17% of patients with primary rectal cancer, including cancellation of surgery and changes in radiotherapy fields. Additionally, PET altered the overall tumor stage in 39% of patients, and follow-up confirmed the appropriateness of these PET-induced management changes. Therefore, PET does influence management decisions in primary rectal cancer.

yes
contexts: The influence of positron emission tomography in the management of recurrent rectal cancer is well established but its role in primary rectal cancer remains uncertain. This study therefore prospectively assesses the impact of position emission tomography scanning on the management of primary rectal cancer.

Forty-six patients with advanced primary rectal cancer referred for consideration of adjuvant preoperative therapy underwent position emission tomography scanning. The referring physicians prospectively recorded each patient's stage following conventional imaging and the proposed treatment plan prior to position emission tomography scanning. This was then compared with subsequent stage and actual management implemented, and the appropriateness of position emission tomography-induced changes was noted by subsequent clinical follow-up.

Compared with computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)), positron emission tomography (PET (positron emission tomography)) may have additional value in the assessment of primary and recurrent cervical cancer. However, the degree of tumour uptake of (18)F-2-fluoro-2-deoxy-D: -glucose (FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)) uptake is sometimes influenced by diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)). Therefore, we conducted this prospective study to compare the diagnostic ability of FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)-PET (positron emission tomography) in patients with cervical cancer complicated by DM (diabetes mellitus) and those without DM (diabetes mellitus).

The surgical management of 36 of 46 patients (78 percent) was unchanged as a result of position emission tomography, even though position emission tomography upstaged disease in 3 of 36 cases (8 percent) and downstaged disease in 5 of 36 cases (14 percent). In 8 of 46 cases (17 percent), management was altered because of the position emission tomography scan findings, including 6 cases (13 percent) in which surgery was cancelled and 2 other cases (4 percent) in which the radiotherapy field was changed. Where available, follow-up confirmed the appropriateness of position emission tomography-induced management change in each case. Two patients had a change in therapy independent of the position emission tomography scan due to clinical circumstances. Overall tumor stage was changed following position emission tomography in 18 of 46 patients (39 percent).

From February 2001 to January 2003, 219 patients (75 with primary and 144 with recurrent cervical cancer) were eligible for analysis. Sixteen had hyperglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus), 12 had euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and 191 were in the non-DM (diabetes mellitus) group. The diagnostic power of PET (positron emission tomography) in the hyperglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus), euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and non-DM (diabetes mellitus) groups did not differ significantly with regard to the identification of either metastatic lesions (AUC (area under the curve), 0.967/0.947/0.925, P>0.05) or primary tumours/local recurrence (AUC (area under the curve), 0.950/0.938/0.979, P>0.05). Considering all DM (diabetes mellitus) patients, PET (positron emission tomography) showed a significantly higher detection power than MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)/CT (computed tomography) scans in respect of metastatic lesions (AUC (area under the curve)=0.956 vs 0.824, P=0.012).
results.reference: Position emission tomography scanning appears to accurately change the stage or appropriately alter the therapy of almost a third of patients with advanced primary rectal cancer. In view of this, we suggest that position emission tomography scanning be considered part of standard workup for such patients, particularly if neoadjuvant chemoradiation is being considered as part of primary management.

results.question: Can you deliver accurate tidal volume by manual resuscitator?
results.answer:
The studies indicate that tidal volumes delivered by manual resuscitators vary depending on the method used, with two-handed techniques delivering significantly greater volumes than one-handed methods. Although physical characteristics and education/practice levels have weak correlations with volume accuracy, the pediatric BVM consistently provides lower and more appropriate tidal volumes, with only 1.5% of breaths below recommended volumes in one study. This suggests that accurate tidal volume delivery is achievable with manual resuscitators, especially when using appropriate techniques and equipment.

yes
contexts: One of the problems with manual resuscitators is the difficulty in achieving accurate volume delivery. The volume delivered to the patient varies by the physical characteristics of the person and method. This study was designed to compare tidal volumes delivered by the squeezing method, physical characteristics and education and practice levels.

The mean (standard deviation) volumes for the one-handed method were 592.84 ml (SD 117.39), two-handed 644.24 ml (SD 144.7) and two-handed half-compression 458.31 ml (SD 120.91) (p<0.01). Tidal volume delivered by two hands was significantly greater than that delivered by one hand (r = 0.398, p<0.01). The physical aspects including hand size, volume and grip power had no correlation with the volume delivered. There were slight increases in tidal volume with education and practice, but correlation was weak (r = 0.213, r = 0.281, r = 0.131, p<0.01).

114 individuals trained in basic life support and bag-valve-mask ventilation participated in this study. Individual characteristics were obtained by the observer and the education and practice level were described by the subjects. Ventilation was delivered with a manual resuscitator connected to a microspirometer and volumes were measured. Subjects completed three procedures: one-handed, two-handed and two-handed half-compression.

We enrolled 50 providers from a large, busy, urban fire-based EMS (emergency medical services) agency with 14.96 (SD = 9.92) mean years of experience. Only 1.5% of all breaths delivered with the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) during the ventilation scenarios were below the recommended tidal volume. A greater percentage of breaths delivered in the recommended range occurred when the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) was used (17.5% vs 5.1%, p<0.001). Median volumes for each scenario were 570.5mL, 664.0mL, 663.0mL for the pediatric BMV and 796.0mL, 994.5mL, 981.5mL for the adult BVM (bag-valve-mask). In all three categories of airway devices, the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) provided lower median tidal volumes (p<0.001).

Using a patient simulator of a head and thorax that was able to record respiratory rate, tidal volume, peak pressure, and minute volume via a laptop computer, participants were asked to ventilate the simulator during six 1-minute ventilation tests. The first scenario was BVM (bag-valve-mask) ventilation with an oropharyngeal airway in place ventilating with both an adult- and pediatric-sized BVM (bag-valve-mask), the second scenario had a supraglottic airway and both bags, and the third scenario had an endotracheal tube and both bags. Participants were enrolled in convenience manner while they were on-duty and the research staff was able to travel to their stations. Prior to enrolling, participants were not given any additional training on ventilation skills.
results.reference: The tidal volume delivered by a manual resuscitator shows large variations. There were significant differences in the volume delivered by compression methods, but physical characteristics are not a predictor of tidal volume delivery. The manual resuscitator is not a suitable device for accurate ventilation.

results.question: Can increases in the cigarette tax rate be linked to cigarette retail prices?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that despite the 2009 excise tax increase on cigarettes in China, the retail prices did not increase because the Chinese STMA used its authority to keep prices stable. This suggests that increases in the cigarette tax rate do not necessarily lead to higher retail prices, at least in the context described.

no
contexts: The 2009 excise tax increase on cigarettes in China has not translated into higher retail prices because the Chinese STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration) used its policy authority to ensure that retail cigarette prices did not change. The government tax increase is being collected at both the producer and wholesale levels. As a result, the 2009 excise tax increase in China has resulted in higher tax revenue for the government and lower profits for the tobacco industry, with no increase in the retail price of cigarettes for consumers.
To explain China's cigarette pricing mechanism and the role of the Chinese State Tobacco Monopoly Administration (STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration)) on cigarette pricing and taxation.

Published government tobacco tax documentation and statistics published by the Chinese STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration) are used to analyse the interrelations among industry profits, taxes and retail price of cigarettes in China.

Of study participants, 36% were male. Prevalence of casual high BP (blood pressure) was 19%. In the population, 10% were current cigarette smokers and habitual alcohol use was high at 56%. As measured by body mass index, 2% were obese and 14% had abdominal obesity. RHR (resting heart rate) was elevated (>90 bpm) in 19%. Overall, 79% of study participants were found to have at least one CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk factor. RHR (resting heart rate) was significantly associated with age, waist circumference, and BP (blood pressure). Individuals with an elevated RHR (resting heart rate) had a higher risk (OR 1.94, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.15-3.26%, p = 0.013) of casual high BP (blood pressure) compared with participants with normal RHR (resting heart rate) independently of several established CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk factors. The regression dilution ratio of RHR (resting heart rate) was 0.75 (95% CI (confidence interval) 0.62-0.89).

Higher benefits are linked to lower disability rates. Among all single elderly individuals, 30 percent have mobility limitations, and an increase of $100 per month in the maximum SSI (supplemental security income) benefit caused the rate of mobility limitations to fall by 0.46 percentage points. The findings were robust to sensitivity analyses. First, analyses limited to those most likely to receive SSI (supplemental security income) produced larger effects, but analyses limited to those least likely to receive SSI (supplemental security income) produced no measurable effect. Second, varying the disability measure did not meaningfully alter the findings. Third, excluding the institutionalized, immigrants, individuals living in states with exceptionally large benefit changes, and individuals living in states with no SSI (supplemental security income) supplements did not change the substantive conclusions. Fourth, Medicaid did not confound the effects. Finally, these results were robust for married individuals.
results.reference: Numerous studies have found that taxation is one of the most effective policy instruments for tobacco control. However, these findings come from countries that have market economies where market forces determine prices and influence how cigarette taxes are passed to the consumers in retail prices. China's tobacco industry is not a market economy; therefore, non-market forces and the current Chinese tobacco monopoly system determine cigarette prices. The result is that tax increases do not necessarily get passed on to the retail price.

results.question: Vertical lines in distal esophageal mucosa (VLEM): a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children?
results.answer:
The presence of vertical lines in the esophageal mucosa (VLEM) was found to be significantly associated with histologic esophagitis in children, particularly eosinophilic esophagitis, with high specificity and moderate sensitivity. Most patients with VLEM had moderate to severe eosinophilic esophagitis, indicating that VLEM is a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in this population.

yes
contexts: We observed an endoscopic abnormally in a group of children with histological esophagitis. We termed this finding "vertical lines in esophageal mucosa" (VLEM). We examined the relationship between the presence of VLEM and significant histologic changes in esophageal mucosal biopsies.

The esophageal mucosa had a normal appearance on 160 endoscopic studies (Group 1) and VLEM were the only mucosal abnormalities in 41 endoscopies (Group 2). Histology was normal in 92 of 160 biopsies (57.5%) from Group 1, and 1 of 41 biopsies (2.4%) from Group 2. Most patients in Group 2 had eosinophilic esophagitis (34 of 41, 83%, specificity 0.85, sensitivity 0.5, p>0.001) which was of moderate to severe intensity (31 of 34, 91.2%, specificity 0.88, sensitivity 0.73, p<0.001).

Between January 1, 1992, and August 31, 1994, the senior author (JFF) performed 255 esophageal biopsies. The procedure reports, available endoscopic photographs, and histology reports were reviewed to establish the endoscopic and histologic appearance of the esophageal mucosa. Intraepithelial cells were counted in a blind review of 42 randomly selected biopsies.

Primary eosinophilic esophagitis, a chronic inflammatory disorder of the esophagus, evokes recurrent dysphagia. Endoscopy is often unremarkable, and no consensus exists regarding management of resultant dysphagia. The response of a series of patients with primary eosinophilic esophagitis to dilation is reported together with a description of a possibly pathognomonic sign: fragile esophageal mucosa, for which the term "crêpe-paper" mucosa is introduced.

Mean mucosal thickness in patients with IHPS (infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis) approximated mean muscle thickness, with a ratio of 0.89. In infants with IHPS (infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis), the pyloric mucosa constitutes approximately one third of the cross-sectional diameter of the pyloric mass and fills and obstructs the pyloric canal.
results.reference: Histology usually demonstrated moderate to severe inflammation when VLEM were present. VLEM may be a highly specific endoscopic feature of esophagitis in children.

results.question: Does hypoglycaemia increase the risk of cardiovascular events?
results.answer:
The ORIGIN trial data indicate that severe hypoglycaemia is associated with a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular events, including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, and arrhythmic death. Non-severe hypoglycaemia was not associated with these outcomes, but severe episodes clearly increased cardiovascular risk.

yes
contexts: Hypoglycaemia caused by glucose-lowering therapy has been linked to cardiovascular (CV (cardiovascular)) events. The ORIGIN trial provides an opportunity to further assess this relationship.

Several studies have shown associations between hyperglycemia and risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD (cardiovascular disease)) and mortality, yet glucose-lowering treatment does little to mitigate this risk. We examined whether associations between hyperglycemia and CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk were explained by underlying insulin resistance.

A total of 12 537 participants with dysglycaemia and high CV (cardiovascular)-risk were randomized to basal insulin glargine titrated to a fasting glucose of ≤ 5.3 mmol/L (95 mg/dL) or standard glycaemic care. Non-severe hypoglycaemia was defined as symptoms confirmed by glucose ≤ 54 mg/dL and severe hypoglycaemia as a requirement for assistance or glucose ≤ 36 mg/dL. Outcomes were: (i) the composite of CV (cardiovascular) death, non-fatal myocardial infarction or stroke; (ii) mortality; (iii) CV (cardiovascular) mortality; and (iv) arrhythmic death. Hazards were estimated before and after adjustment for a hypoglycaemia propensity score. During a median of 6.2 years (IQR: 5.8-6.7), non-severe hypoglycaemic episodes occurred in 41.7 and 14.4% glargine and standard group participants, respectively, while severe episodes occurred in 5.7 and 1.8%, respectively. Non-severe hypoglycaemia was not associated with any outcome following adjustment. Conversely, severe hypoglycaemia was associated with a greater risk for the primary outcome (HR: 1.58; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.24-2.02, P<0.001), mortality (HR: 1.74; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.39-2.19, P<0.001), CV (cardiovascular) death (HR: 1.71; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.27-2.30, P<0.001) and arrhythmic death (HR: 1.77; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.17-2.67, P = 0.007). Similar findings were noted for severe nocturnal hypoglycaemia for the primary outcome and mortality. The severe hypoglycaemia hazard for all four outcomes was higher with standard care than with insulin glargine.

In 60 middle-aged individuals without diabetes we studied the associations of fasting plasma glucose, 2-hour post oral glucose tolerance test plasma glucose, insulin sensitivity as well as body fat percentage with CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk. Insulin sensitivity was measured as the glucose infusion rate during a euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamp, body fat percentage was measured by dual X-ray absorptiometry, and CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk was estimated using the Framingham risk score. Associations of fasting plasma glucose, 2-hour plasma glucose, insulin sensitivity and body fat percentage with the Framingham risk score were assessed in linear regression models.
Metabolic syndrome (MetS (metabolic syndrome)) is associated with increased risk for cardiovascular events. We evaluated heart dimensions in hypertensive patients with MetS (metabolic syndrome).
results.reference: Severe hypoglycaemia is associated with an increased risk for CV outcomes in people at high CV risk and dysglycaemia. Although allocation to insulin glargine vs. standard care was associated with an increased risk of severe and non-severe hypoglycaemia, the relative risk of CV outcomes with hypoglycaemia was lower with insulin glargine-based glucose-lowering therapy than with the standard glycaemic control. Trial Registration (ORIGIN ClinicalTrials.gov number NCT00069784).

results.question: Does the radiographic transition zone correlate with the level of aganglionosis on the specimen in Hirschsprung's disease?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that the radiographic transition zone on contrast enema correlates with the level of aganglionosis but with limited accuracy. The agreement between radiological findings and pathological specimens was moderate overall (58.1%, κ = 0.39), with better concordance in long-segment and total colonic forms but lower in rectal and rectosigmoid forms. Thus, while there is some correlation, it is not highly reliable.

yes
contexts: From 1998 to 2009, 79 patients were operated on for Hirschsprung's disease. All available preoperative contrast enemas (n = 61) had been single blind reviewed by the same radiologist who defined the radiographic transition zone when present in vertebral level. Four groups were determined (rectal, rectosigmoid, long segment, and absence of transition zone) and by Kappa coefficient of agreement correlated to the length of aganglionosis in the pathological report.

The correlation between radiographic transition zone on contrast enema in Hirschsprung's disease and the total length of aganglionosis is known to be inaccurate. The aim of our study was to analyse this correlation more precisely to improve preoperative planning of the corrective surgery.

To demonstrate that the radiographic scout image does not augment VCUG (voiding cystourethrography) interpretation or contribute management-changing information but nonetheless carries a non-negligible effective dose.

Radiological findings were concordant with the specimen in pathology in 8 cases of 19 in rectal form (42 %), in 20 cases of 35 in rectosigmoid form (57 %), in all 6 cases of long-segment form (100 %), in the 2 cases of total colonic form (100 %) with a global agreement of 58.1 %, κ = 0.39 CI (confidence interval) [0.24; 0.57].

The transanal endorectal pull-through (TERPT (transanal endorectal pull-through)) is becoming the most popular procedure in the treatment of Hirschsprung disease (HD (hirschsprung disease)), but overstretching of the anal sphincters remains a critical issue that may impact the continence. This study examined the long-term outcome of TERPT (transanal endorectal pull-through) versus conventional transabdominal (ABD) pull-through for HD (hirschsprung disease).
results.reference: Correlation between level of radiographic transition zone on contrast enema and length of aganglionosis remains low. Systematic preoperative biopsy by coelioscopy or ombilical incision is mandatory.

results.question: Is dexamethasone an effective alternative to oral prednisone in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that multiple pediatric clinical trials found dexamethasone to be as effective as prednisone in treating mild to moderate asthma exacerbations in children. Meta-analysis showed no significant difference in symptomatic return to baseline or unplanned physician revisits between the two drugs, and dexamethasone may have additional benefits such as improved compliance and less vomiting.

yes
contexts: A short course of systemic corticosteroids is an important therapy in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations. Although a 5-day course of oral prednisone or prednisolone has become the most commonly used regimen, dexamethasone has also been used for a shorter duration (1-2 days) with potential for improvement in compliance and palatability. We reviewed the literature to determine if there is sufficient evidence that dexamethasone can be used as an effective alternative in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations in the inpatient setting.

Six completed pediatric clinical trials met the inclusion criteria. All of the pediatric trials found that prednisone is not superior to dexamethasone in treating mild to moderate asthma exacerbations. Meta-analysis demonstrated homogeneity between the dexamethasone and prednisone groups when examining symptomatic return to baseline and unplanned physician revisits after the initial emergency department encounter. Some studies found potential additional benefits of dexamethasone, including improved compliance and less vomiting.

A Medline search was conducted on the use of dexamethasone in the treatment of asthma exacerbations in children. The studies selected were clinical trials comparing the efficacy of dexamethasone with prednisone. Meta-analysis was performed examining physician revisitation rates and symptomatic return to baseline.

To characterize the use and delivery of cough and cold medicines in children younger than 6 presenting to an inner-city pediatric emergency department (PED (pediatric emergency department)) following 2007 FDA (Food and Drug Administration) warnings.

To investigate if fetal gender (1) affects the risk of having an emergency department (ED (emergency department)) visit for asthma; and (2) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes among women who had at least one visit to the ED (emergency department) for asthma during pregnancy.
results.reference: The current literature suggests that dexamethasone can be used as an effective alternative to prednisone in the treatment of mild to moderate acute asthma exacerbations in children, with the added benefits of improved compliance, palatability, and cost. However, more research is needed to examine the role of dexamethasone in hospitalized children.

results.question: Mammographic screening in Sami speaking municipalities and a control group. Are early outcome measures influenced by ethnicity?
results.answer:
The attendance rate for mammographic screening was slightly higher in the Sami population (78%) compared to the non-Sami population (75%), and recall rates were significantly lower in the Sami group (2.4% vs. 3.3%). However, the rate of invasive screen-detected cancer was not significantly different, and the percentage of breast cancers detected in the screening program was lower in the Sami group but not statistically significant. These findings suggest that early outcome measures of mammographic screening are influenced by ethnicity.

yes
contexts: Female citizens of Sami (the indigenous people of Norway) municipalities in northern Norway have a low risk of breast cancer. The objective of this study was to describe the attendance rate and outcome of the Norwegian Breast Cancer Screening Program (NBCSP (norwegian breast cancer screening program)) in the Sami-speaking municipalities and a control group.

The 8 municipalities included in the administration area of the Sami language law (Sami) were matched with a control group of 11 municipalities (non-Sami). Population data were accessed from Statistics Norway. Data regarding invitations and outcome in the NBCSP (norwegian breast cancer screening program) during the period 2001-2010 was derived from the Cancer Registry of Norway (CRN (cancer registry of norway)). The NBCSP (norwegian breast cancer screening program) targets women aged 50-69 years. Rates and percentages were compared using chi-square test with a p-value<0.05 as statistical significant.

The attendance rate in the NBCSP (norwegian breast cancer screening program) was 78% in the Sami and 75% in the non-Sami population (p<0.01). The recall rates were 2.4 and 3.3% in the Sami and non-Sami population, respectively (p<0.01). The rate of invasive screen detected cancer was not significantly lower in the Sami group (p=0.14). The percentage of all breast cancers detected in the NBCSP (norwegian breast cancer screening program) among the Sami (67%) was lower compared with the non-Sami population (86%, p=0.06).

From January 2006 to August 2008, a group of 678 singleton pregnancies who had developed GDM (gestational diabetes mellitus) has been selected as a study group among a total of 3966 pregnant women who had undergone first trimester screening for aneuploidies at 11-14 weeks of gestation. A group of 420 single pregnant women with physiological pregnancy were enrolled as control group. Both fetal structural and karyotype's anomalies were excluded in the two groups. NT (nuchal translucency) was mesured by a Fetal Medicine Foundation certificated operator; GDM (gestational diabetes mellitus) was diagnosed at 24-28 weeks of gestation following Carpenter and Coustan criteria. In the analyses of continuos variables, study and control group were compared by Student's t-test and Anova test.

Coverage for breast cancer screening was 10.5% in South Africa, 19.3% in China, 33.8% in Russia and 43% in Mexico, and coverage for cervical cancer screening was 24% in South Africa, 27.2% in China, 63.7% in Mexico and 81.5% in Russia. Economic inequalities in screening participation were substantially lower or non-existent in countries with higher aggregate coverage, for both breast cancer screening (RII (relative index of inequality): 14.57 in South Africa, 4.90 in China, 2.01 in Mexico, 1.04 in Russia) and cervical cancer screening (RII (relative index of inequality): 3.60 in China, 2.47 in South Africa, 1.39 in Mexico, 1.12 in Russia).
results.reference: Despite a lower risk of breast cancer, the Sami attended the NBCSP more frequently than the control group. The recall and cancer detection rate was lower among the Sami compared with the non-Sami group.

results.question: Do Electrochemiluminescence Assays Improve Prediction of Time to Type 1 Diabetes in Autoantibody-Positive TrialNet Subjects?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that electrochemiluminescence (ECL) assays, specifically ECL-IAA and ECL-GADA, were significantly associated with progression to type 1 diabetes in autoantibody-positive TrialNet subjects. Adding ECL positivity to existing risk models improved prediction accuracy, with a higher risk of diabetes progression observed in ECL-positive individuals compared to ECL-negative ones. Therefore, the evidence supports that ECL assays improve prediction of time to type 1 diabetes in this population.

yes
contexts: To explore whether electrochemiluminescence (ECL (electrochemiluminescence)) assays can help improve prediction of time to type 1 diabetes in the TrialNet autoantibody-positive population.

TrialNet subjects who were positive for one or more autoantibodies (microinsulin autoantibody, GAD65 autoantibody [GADA], IA-2A, and ZnT8A) with available ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-insulin autoantibody (IAA (insulin autoantibody)) and ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-GADA data at their initial visit were analyzed; after a median follow-up of 24 months, 177 of these 1,287 subjects developed diabetes.

Univariate analyses showed that autoantibodies by radioimmunoassays (RIAs (radioimmunoassays)), ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-IAA (insulin autoantibody), ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-GADA, age, sex, number of positive autoantibodies, presence of HLA DR3/4-DQ8 genotype, HbA1c (hemoglobin A1c), and oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT (oral glucose tolerance test)) measurements were all significantly associated with progression to diabetes. Subjects who were ECL (electrochemiluminescence) positive had a risk of progression to diabetes within 6 years of 58% compared with 5% for the ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-negative subjects (P<0.0001). Multivariate Cox proportional hazards models were compared, with the base model including age, sex, OGTT (oral glucose tolerance test) measurements, and number of positive autoantibodies by RIAs (radioimmunoassays). The model with positivity for ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-GADA and/or ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-IAA (insulin autoantibody) was the best, and factors that remained significantly associated with time to diabetes were area under the curve (AUC (area under the curve)) C-peptide, fasting C-peptide, AUC (area under the curve) glucose, number of positive autoantibodies by RIAs (radioimmunoassays), and ECL (electrochemiluminescence) positivity. Adding ECL (electrochemiluminescence) to the Diabetes Prevention Trial risk score (DPTRS (diabetes prevention trial risk score)) improved the receiver operating characteristic curves with AUC (area under the curve) of 0.83 (P<0.0001).

An observational study was performed in 215 subjects with type 1 diabetes treated with multiple insulin injection therapy. Atherosclerosis was assessed by measurement of carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT (carotid intima-media thickness)).

Participants were 7 individuals with T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) and 10 controls.
