Patients usually complain about numbness in the nasal tip after microfat injections. The present study evaluated the severity of the numbness in the nasal tip after the procedure.

A retrospective evaluation of patients who underwent surgical reduction of a condylar fracture from January 2012 to December 2014 at the Clinic of Dentistry and Maxillofacial Surgery of the University Hospital of Verona (Verona, Italy) was performed. Inclusion criteria were having undergone surgical treatment of condylar fractures with a retromandibular transparotid approach and the availability of computed tomograms of the preoperative and postoperative facial skeleton with a minimum follow-up of 1 year. Static and dynamic occlusal function, temporomandibular joint health status, presence of neurologic impairments, and esthetic outcomes were evaluated in all patients.
results.reference: Closed reduction is an easy and sufficient treatment for nasal fractures, especially for mild nasal fractures. Early intervention raises the patient satisfaction rate.

results.question: Do improvements in outreach, clinical, and family and community-based services predict improvements in child survival?
results.answer:
The data show that improvements in clinical services have a strong correlation with reductions in under-5 mortality rates, and outreach activities like antenatal care and family planning also correlate with mortality declines. Family and community services such as breastfeeding and nutritional status improvements are associated with significant mortality changes in some contexts. Therefore, improvements in these service domains do predict improvements in child survival.

yes
contexts: There are three main service delivery channels: clinical services, outreach, and family and community. To determine which delivery channels are associated with the greatest reductions in under-5 mortality rates (U5MR (under-5 mortality rates)), we used data from sequential population-based surveys to examine the correlation between changes in coverage of clinical, outreach, and family and community services and in U5MR (under-5 mortality rates) for 27 high-burden countries.

AAC (annual changes) in under 5-mortality varied from 6.6% in Nepal to -0.9% in Kenya, with six of the 19 African countries all experiencing less than a 1% decline in mortality. The strongest correlation with reductions in U5MR (under-5 mortality rates) was observed for access to clinical services (all countries: p = 0.02, r² = 0.58; 19 African countries p<0.001, r² = 0.67). For outreach activities, AAC (annual changes) U5MR (under-5 mortality rates) was significantly correlated with antenatal care and family planning services, while AAC (annual changes) in immunization services showed no association. In the family- and community services domain, improvements in breastfeeding were associated with significant changes in mortality in the 30 countries but not in the African subset; while in the African countries, nutritional status improvements were associated with a significant decline in mortality.

Household survey data were abstracted from serial surveys in 27 countries. Average annual changes (AAC (annual changes)) between the most recent and penultimate survey were calculated for under-five mortality rates and for 22 variables in the domains of clinical, outreach, and family- and community-based services. For all 27 countries and a subset of 19 African countries, we conducted principal component analysis to reduce the variables into a few components in each domain and applied linear regression to assess the correlation between changes in the principal components and changes in under-five mortality rates after controlling for multiple potential confounding factors.

Health services often spend more on safety interventions than seems cost-effective. This study investigates whether the public value safety-related health care improvements more highly than the same improvements in contexts where the health care system is not responsible.

The services demonstrated that it was feasible to embed the Model into their organizational structures. Advance care planning conversations and involvement of family was an important outcome measure rather than completion rate of advance care planning documents in community settings. Services adapted and applied their own concept of community, which widened the impact of the model. Changes to quality audit processes were essential to consolidate the model into routine palliative care practice.
results.reference: Our findings support the importance of increasing access to clinical services, certain outreach services and breastfeeding and, in Africa, of improving nutritional status. Integrated programs that emphasize these services may lead to substantial mortality declines.

results.question: Does spontaneous remission occur in polyarteritis nodosa?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that spontaneous remission of polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) is largely unknown but possible, as illustrated by the case of a 51-year-old woman who experienced spontaneous remission of PAN symptoms without immunosuppressive treatment. This case supports the occurrence of spontaneous remission, although it appears to be rare or not well documented.

yes
contexts: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN (polyarteritis nodosa)) is a systemic vasculitis involving mainly medium-sized arteries and, rarely, small-sized arteries. The diagnosis is principally based on clinical exams, biopsy of an affected organ, and/or arteriography of renal or mesenteric arteries. Once diagnosed, immunosuppressive agents, such as glucocorticoids and cyclophosphamide, are generally introduced as soon as possible. Whether spontaneous remission of PAN (polyarteritis nodosa) occurs is therefore largely unknown.

We describe the case of a 51-year-old woman who presented with a 4-day-history of intense pain in her left flank, hypertension, fever, microscopic hematuria, and acute renal failure. Contrast-enhanced renal ultrasound strongly suggested bilateral renal infarction. Medical history and an extensive workup allowed to exclude systemic embolism, recreational drug abuse, cardiac arrhythmias, and thrombophilia. A possible diagnosis of PAN (polyarteritis nodosa) was considered; however, within 2 weeks of admission, spontaneous remission of her clinical and biological symptoms occurred without the use of any immunosuppressive treatment. Finally, 3 months later, renal arteriography confirmed the diagnosis of PAN (polyarteritis nodosa). The patient remains free of symptoms 1 year after initial presentation.

Of the 61 patients included in this study, 48 (78.7%) achieved initial remission and 13 (21.3%) failed treatment. Seven patients suffered subsequent relapse (range 22-158 months) in their condition after apparent remission, leaving a final group of 41 patients (67.2%) in the remission group. Tumour was identified at surgery in 52 patients, of whom 38 achieved remission. In comparison, only 3 of 9 patients in whom no tumour was identified achieved remission. This difference was significant (P = 0.048). When both radiological and histological findings were positive, the likelihood of achieving remission was significantly higher than if both modalities were negative (P = 0.038). There were significant differences between remission and failure groups when 2- and 6-week postoperative serum cortisol levels (P = 0.002 and 0.001, respectively) and 6-week postoperative urine free cortisol levels (P = 0.026) were compared. This allowed identification of patients who failed surgical treatment in the early postoperative period. Complications of surgery included transitory DI in 13, transitory CSF leak in 8 and transitory nasal discharge and cacosmia in 3. Twelve of 41 patients required some form of hormonal replacement therapy despite achieving long-term remission. Thirteen patients underwent a second operation, of whom 5 achieved remission.

Fifty RA patients were prospectively recruited from the Biologic Therapy Unit of our hospital. Inclusion criteria were being in treatment with s.c. anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agents and having had neither changes in therapy nor local corticosteroid injections in the previous 3 months. Patients underwent clinical, laboratory [28-joint DAS (DAS28) and Simplified Disease Activity Index (SDAI (simplified disease activity index))]and US (ultrasound) assessment at two time points, i.e. at peak plasma drug concentration and at trough plasma drug concentration. US (ultrasound) assessments were performed blindly to the anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agent, the administration time and the clinical and laboratory data. Twenty-eight joints were investigated for the presence and grade (0-3) of B-mode synovitis and synovial power Doppler signal. Global indices for B-mode synovitis (BSI (b-mode synovitis)) and Doppler synovitis (DSI (doppler synovitis)) were calculated for 12 joints and for wrist-hand-ankle-foot joints. B-mode US (ultrasound) remission was defined as a BSI (b-mode synovitis)<1 and Doppler US (ultrasound) remission as a DSI (doppler synovitis)<1.

There were no significant differences between the clinical, laboratory and B-mode and Doppler US (ultrasound) parameters at peak time and trough time (P = 0.132-0.986). There were no significant differences between the proportion of patients with active disease and those in remission according to DAS28, SDAI (simplified disease activity index), B-mode US (ultrasound) and Doppler US (ultrasound) at peak time and trough time assessments (P = 0.070-1).
results.reference: This case illustrates the importance of considering PAN in the differential diagnosis of renal infarction with inflammatory syndrome and shows that spontaneous remission of renal PAN can occur. .

results.question: Gluten tolerance in adult patients with celiac disease 20 years after diagnosis?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that celiac disease is generally considered a permanent intolerance to gluten, but some adult patients have been found to consume gluten without symptoms or histological signs of disease. Specifically, in a group of patients with long-standing celiac disease, a small number (two patients) were considered to have developed tolerance to gluten, even one lacking the typical HLA risk alleles. This suggests that gluten tolerance can develop in some adult patients many years after diagnosis.

yes
contexts: All 77 adult patients from our hospital known to have biopsy-proven CD (celiac disease) for more than 10 years were invited to participate. We investigated symptoms, gluten consumption, antibodies for CD (celiac disease) and other autoimmunity, human leukocyte antigen (HLA (human leukocyte antigen))-typing, bone mineral density, and performed small bowel biopsies. Tolerance was defined as no immunological or histological signs of CD (celiac disease) while consuming gluten.

Celiac disease (CD (celiac disease)) is believed to be a permanent intolerance to gluten. A number of patients, however, discontinue the gluten-free diet (GFD (gluten-free diet)) without developing symptoms or signs. The aim of our study was to investigate whether CD (celiac disease) patients are capable of developing tolerance to gluten.

Sixty-six patients accepted participation, but after review of the diagnostic biopsies 53 were found to have true CD (celiac disease). Twenty-three percent of patients had a gluten-containing diet, 15% admitted gluten transgression and 62% followed the GFD (gluten-free diet). Patients on a GFD (gluten-free diet) had significantly more osteoporosis. Normal small bowel mucosa was found in four of eight on gluten-containing diet and in four of four with gluten transgression. Two patients were considered to have developed tolerance to gluten. One of them was HLA (human leukocyte antigen)-DQ2/DQ8 negative.

A retrospective study of prepubertal children aged 3-12 years with CD (n=24) who were compared to prepubertal, non-CD (celiac disease) children of the same age (n=50). Children were included in the study if they had a diagnosis of CD (celiac disease) by intestinal biopsy, and were not on a gluten-free diet (GFD (gluten-free diet)). Patients were excluded if they had diseases of calcium or vitamin D metabolism, or were receiving calcium or vitamin D supplementation or had other autoimmune diseases. All subjects had their serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] level measured.

There was no difference in 25(OH)D level between the CD (celiac disease) and non-CD (celiac disease) children (27.58 +/- 9.91 versus 26.20 +/- 10.45, p = 0.59). However, when the patients were subdivided into obese and non-obese groups, the non-obese CD (celiac disease) patients had a significantly higher 25(OH)D level than the obese normal children (28.39 +/- 10.26 versus 21.58 +/- 5.67, p = 0.009). In contrast, there was no difference in 25(OH)D level between non-obese CD (celiac disease) patients and non-obese normal children (28.39 +/- 10.26 versus 30.64 +/-12.08, p = 0.52). The season of 25(OH)D measurement was not a significant confounder (p =0.7).
results.reference: Development of tolerance to gluten seems possible in some patients with CD. Further follow-up will show whether this tolerance is permanent or only a long-term return to latency. This feature may be associated with genetic characteristics, especially with HLA genotypes that differ from DQ2 or DQ8. More insight into the mechanisms of the development of gluten tolerance may help to distinguish those CD patients that might not require life-long GFD.

results.question: Do symptoms predict COPD in smokers?
results.answer:
The data indicate that respiratory symptoms are common among smokers with airways obstruction, and the odds ratios for symptoms like cough, dyspnea, sputum, and wheeze are elevated in smokers with significant smoking history. Additionally, sensitivity and predictive values for symptoms in detecting airways obstruction are similar between smokers and the general population, suggesting symptoms do have predictive value for COPD in smokers.

yes
contexts: Forty-four percent of smokers in our sample had airways obstruction (AO (airways obstruction)). Of these, 36% reported a diagnosis of or treatment for COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Odds ratio (95% CI (confidence interval)) for AO (airways obstruction) with smoking (>or = 20 pack-years) was 3.73 (3.12- 4.45), 1.98 (1.73-2.27) for cough, 1.79 (1.55-2.08) for dyspnea, 1.95 (1.70-2.34) for sputum, and 2.59 (2.26-2.97) for wheeze. Respiratory symptoms were reported by 92% of smokers with AO (airways obstruction), 86% smokers with restriction, 76% smokers with normal spirometry, and 73% of nonsmokers. Sensitivity (92% vs 90%), specificity (19% vs 22%), positive (47% vs 40%) and negative (75% vs 80%) predictive values for the presence of one or more symptoms were similar between smokers and all subjects.

Report of symptoms, smoking history, and spirometric data were collected from subjects screened for a work-related medical evaluation (N = 3,955). Prevalence of airflow obstruction and respiratory symptoms were assessed. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and relative risks of predicting symptoms and smoking history for COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) were calculated.

The US (ultrasound) Preventive Services Task Force recommends against spirometry in the absence of symptoms. However, as much as 50% of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) cases in the United States remain undiagnosed.

In the 10 years before the diagnosis of chronic functional somatic symptoms, significantly more patients than controls presented functional somatic symptoms in at least two body systems, and used more somatic and psychotropic drugs. They visited the GP (general practitioner) twice as much, statistically had significantly more psychiatric morbidity, and were referred more often to mental health workers and somatic specialists. The number of patients undergoing diagnostic tests was higher for patients with chronic functional somatic symptoms than for controls, but hospital admissions rates were equal.
To identify distinctive features in patients with chronic functional somatic symptoms, and to determine whether these symptoms support the hypothesis of the existence of specific somatic syndromes.
results.reference: COPD is underdiagnosed in the United States. Symptoms are frequent in subjects with AO and increase their risk for COPD, but add little beyond age and smoking history to the predictive value of spirometry. In view of the high prevalence of symptoms and their poor predictive value, a simpler and more effective approach would be to screen older smokers.

results.question: Search engine as a diagnostic tool in difficult immunological and allergologic cases: is Google useful?
results.answer:
The study described in the abstracts evaluated the effectiveness of Google searches in diagnosing complex immunological and allergic cases by having investigators use Google to identify diagnoses from clinical data. The results showed that specialists had an 80% agreement with reference diagnoses, indicating that Google can be a useful tool in this context. Therefore, the evidence supports the usefulness of Google as a diagnostic aid in difficult immunological and allergologic cases.

yes
contexts: Web search engines are an important tool in communication and diffusion of knowledge. Among these, Google appears to be the most popular one: in August 2008, it accounted for 87% of all web searches in the UK, compared with Yahoo's 3.3%. Google's value as a diagnostic guide in general medicine was recently reported. The aim of this comparative cross-sectional study was to evaluate whether searching Google with disease-related terms was effective in the identification and diagnosis of complex immunological and allergic cases.

Forty-five case reports were randomly selected by an independent observer from peer-reviewed medical journals. Clinical data were presented separately to three investigators, blinded to the final diagnoses. Investigator A was a Consultant with an expert knowledge in Internal Medicine and Allergy (IM&A) and basic computing skills. Investigator B was a Registrar in IM&A. Investigator C was a Research Nurse. Both Investigators B and C were familiar with computers and search engines. For every clinical case presented, each investigator independently carried out an Internet search using Google to provide a final diagnosis. Their results were then compared with the published diagnoses.

To verify the feasibility of developing a real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR (polymerase chain reaction)) approach, an alternative to optical analysis, as a rapid, accurate, and automated tool for the detection and quantification of airborne allergenic pollen taxa.

Specialists agreed with the reference standard in 80% of cases (range 75%-86%), with a sensitivity and specificity of 75% and 84%, respectively. This did not differ by clinical specialty, hospital or years of experience, and residents had similar results. Specialists agreed with the index expert in 76% of cases and the index expert agreed with his previous assessments in 71% of cases.

A Medline search was conducted on the use of dexamethasone in the treatment of asthma exacerbations in children. The studies selected were clinical trials comparing the efficacy of dexamethasone with prednisone. Meta-analysis was performed examining physician revisitation rates and symptomatic return to baseline.
results.reference: This Google-based search was useful to identify an appropriate diagnosis in complex immunological and allergic cases. Computing skills may help to get better results.

results.question: Uniformity of evidence-based treatments in practice?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate variability in the implementation of evidence-based treatments (EBTs) in clinical practice. Abstract [1] highlights that measurement-based care, a component of EBTs, is not commonly used despite its importance. Abstract [5] notes variations in the uptake and use of clinical information systems supporting EBTs across different practices. These points suggest that evidence-based treatments are not uniformly applied in practice.

no
contexts: The gap between evidence-based treatments and routine care has been well established. Findings from the Sequenced Treatments Alternatives to Relieve Depression (STAR*D) emphasized the importance of measurement-based care for the treatment of depression as a key ingredient for achieving response and remission; yet measurement-based care approaches are not commonly used in clinical practice.

Various factors contribute to the effective implementation of evidence-based treatments (EBTs (evidence-based treatments)). In this study, cognitive processing therapy (CPT (cognitive processing therapy)) was administered in a Veterans Affairs (VA (veterans affairs)) posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD (posttraumatic stress disorder)) specialty clinic in which training and supervision were provided following VA (veterans affairs) implementation guidelines. The aim was to (a) estimate the proportion of variability in outcome attributable to therapists and (b) identify characteristics of those therapists who produced better outcomes.

We conducted a reliability study in a cohort with patient records including both outpatient and inpatient care as the objects of measurement. We developed a structured implicit review instrument to assess the quality of care over one year of treatment. 12 reviewers conducted a total of 496 reviews of 70 patient records selected from 26 VA clinical sites in two regions of the country. Each patient had between one and four conditions specified as having a highly developed evidence base (diabetes and hypertension) or a less developed evidence base (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or a collection of acute conditions). Multilevel analysis that accounts for the nested and cross-classified structure of the data was used to estimate the signal and noise components of the measurement of quality and the reliability of implicit review.

We sought to develop a more reliable structured implicit chart review instrument for use in assessing the quality of care for chronic disease and to examine if ratings are more reliable for conditions in which the evidence base for practice is more developed.

Recent evaluations of IT innovations in primary care have highlighted variations between centres and practices in uptake and use. We evaluated whether structural characteristics of a general practice were associated with variations in use of a web-based clinical information system underpinning a Managed Clinical Network in diabetes, between the years 2001 and 2003.
results.reference: This study adds to the growing body of literature documenting the importance of the individual therapist as an important factor in the change process.

results.question: Do approved doctors and medical referees in the UK agree when assessing a seafarer's fitness?
results.answer:
The evidence shows that the overall agreement between Approved Doctors and Medical Referees when assessing a seafarer's fitness is poor, with a Kappa value of 0.18 indicating low concordance. Additionally, there are significant differences in how each group classifies fitness categories, further supporting the lack of agreement.

no
contexts: The seafaring industry remains a hazardous occupation that requires sophisticated systems of risk and fitness assessment. This study aims to investigate the extent of agreement between Approved Doctors (ADs (approved doctors)) and Medical Referees (MRs (medical referees)) when they assess a seafarer's fitness.

Between 2003 and 2009 a total of 232,878 seafarer medical examinations were carried out by ADs (approved doctors), of which 465 were considered by the MRs (medical referees) because the seafarer appealed against the AD (Alzheimer disease)'s decision. The extent of agreement between ADs (approved doctors) and MRs (medical referees) was studied.

Two hundred and sixty-eight (58%) cases seen by the ADs (approved doctors) were classed as category 4 "permanently unfit"; the referees only placed 85 (18%) of them in this category. On the other hand, 252 (54%) cases seen by the MRs (medical referees) were classed as category 2 "fit with restrictions", while the ADs (approved doctors) had only placed 111 (24%) in this category. The overall agreement between the assessors (AD (Alzheimer disease) vs. MR) was poor (Kappa K = 0.18).

For cardiovascular diseases and for mental ill-health, access to additional information by the MR was the commonest reason for changing the fitness category, but for all other conditions factors such as the experience and knowledge of the MRs (medical referees) or their different interpretation of the standards were the most frequent reasons for a change to fitness category or to restrictions.

Little is known about the validity and reliability of expert assessments of the quality of antimicrobial prescribing, despite their importance in antimicrobial stewardship. We investigated how infectious disease doctors' assessments compared with a reference standard (modal expert opinion) and with the assessments of their colleagues.
results.reference: This study found that there was poor agreement between the AD's decision and the subsequent MR's decision regarding the fitness of those seafarers who decided to appeal against the AD's initial assessment. The reasons for this are considered.

results.question: Hepatorenal syndrome: are we missing some prognostic factors?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts identify some prognostic factors for survival in type 1 hepatorenal syndrome, such as serum creatinine and urinary sodium levels, but also note that many treatment-related and demographic variables were not associated with survival. Additionally, the mention that ascites volume and anthropometric assessments are not routinely documented or considered in prognostic evaluation suggests that some potentially relevant prognostic factors might be overlooked.

yes
contexts: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS (hepatorenal syndrome)) is the functional renal failure associated with advanced cirrhosis and has also been described in fulminant hepatic failure. Without liver transplantation its prognosis is dismal. Our study included patients with type 1 HRS (hepatorenal syndrome) associated with cirrhosis, who were not liver transplant candidates.AIM: To identify variables associated with improved survival.

Median survival was 13 days for the whole group. Survival varied with the end-stage liver disease (ESLD (end-stage liver disease)) etiology: autoimmune, 49 days, cardiac cirrhosis, 22 days, idiopathic, 15.5 days, viral, 15 days, hepatitis C and alcohol, 14.5 days, alcohol 8 days, and neoplasia 4 days (p = 0.048). Survival of HRS (hepatorenal syndrome) associated with alcoholic liver disease versus other etiologies was not statistically significant (p = 0.1). Increased serum creatinine (p = 0.02) and urinary sodium 6-10 mEq/l (p = 0.027) at the initiation of therapy were prognostic factors for mortality. HRS (hepatorenal syndrome) treatment modalities (p = 0.73), use of dialysis (p = 0.56), dialysis modality (p = 0.35), use of vasopressors (p = 0.26), pre-existing renal disease (p = 0.49), gender (p = 0.90), and age (p = 0.57) were not associated with survival.

Sixty-eight patients fulfilled the revised Ascites Club Criteria for type 1 HRS (hepatorenal syndrome). None of them was suitable for liver transplantation. All the patients were treated with combinations of: albumin, midodrine and octreotide, pressors, and hemodialysis.

Ascitis and undernutrition are frequent complications of cirrhosis, however ascitis volume and anthropometric assessment are not routinely documented or considered in prognostic evaluation. In a homogeneous cohort followed during two years these variables were scrutinized, aiming to ascertain relevance for longterm outcome.

Metabolic syndrome was present in 32 hypertensive patients (42.7%; 18 males, 14 females). The mean number of MetS (metabolic syndrome) criteria was 2.6+/-1.0 in the hypertensive group. Compared to the control group, patients with or without MetS (metabolic syndrome) exhibited significantly increased interventricular septum and posterior wall thickness, left atrial diameter, relative wall thickness, and left ventricular mass (p<0.05). The only significant difference between the two patient groups was that MetS (metabolic syndrome) was associated with a greater left atrial diameter (p=0.019). Left atrial diameter was correlated with the number of MetS (metabolic syndrome) criteria (r=0.51; p<0.001).
results.reference: We report for the first time ESLD etiology as a prognostic factor for survival. The renal function (expressed as serum creatinine) and urinary Na (<5 mEq/l) at the time of diagnosis were found to be associated with survival, suggesting that early treatment might increase survival.

results.question: Vaginal dose assessment in image-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer: Can we really rely on dose-point evaluation?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that dose-point evaluation at PIBS points in image-guided brachytherapy shows strong correlation between prescribed and delivered doses, with insignificant applicator movement affecting dose delivery. Although some dose variations were noted at other points (e.g., rectovaginal point), the overall findings support the reliability of dose-point evaluation for vaginal dose assessment.

yes
contexts: Although dose-volume parameters in image-guided brachytherapy have become a standard, the use of posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis (PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis)) points has been recently proposed in the reporting of vaginal doses. The aim was to evaluate their pertinence.

Nineteen patients who received image-guided brachytherapy after concurrent radiochemotherapy were included. Per treatment, CT scans were performed at Days 2 and 3, with reporting of the initial dwell positions and times. Doses delivered to the PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) points were evaluated on each plan, considering that they were representative of one-third of the treatment. The movements of the applicator according to the PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) point were analysed.

To demonstrate that the radiographic scout image does not augment VCUG (voiding cystourethrography) interpretation or contribute management-changing information but nonetheless carries a non-negligible effective dose.

Mean prescribed doses at PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) -2, PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis), PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) +2 were, respectively, 2.23 ± 1.4, 6.39 ± 6.6, and 31.85 ± 36.06 Gy. Significant differences were observed between the 5 patients with vaginal involvement and the remaining 14 at the level of PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) +2 and PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis): +47.60 Gy and +7.46 Gy, respectively (p = 0.023 and 0.03). The variations between delivered and prescribed doses at PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) points were not significant. However, at International commission on radiation units and measurements rectovaginal point, the delivered dose was decreased by 1.43 ± 2.49 Gy from the planned dose (p = 0.019). The delivered doses at the four points were strongly correlated with the prescribed doses with R(2) ranging from 0.93 to 0.95. The movements of the applicator in regard of the PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) point assessed with the Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine coordinates were insignificant.

A retrospective analysis of 136 breasts of 134 patients, who received breast-conserving oncoplastic surgery for low-risk breast cancer between 2002 and 2010 in the Universities of Vienna and Luebeck followed by adjuvant APBI (accelerated partial breast irradiation) applying total doses of pulse dose rate of 50.4 Gy or high-dose rate (HDR (high-dose rate)) of 32 Gy over 4 days. Target volume definition was performed by the use of surgical-free margin data, related to intraoperatively fixed clip positions, pre- and postoperative imaging, and palpation.
results.reference: The doses evaluated at PIBS points are not impacted by intrafractional movements. PIBS and PIBS +2 dose points allow distinguishing the plans of patients with vaginal infiltration. Further studies are needed to correlate these parameters with vaginal morbidity.

results.question: Prescriptions as a proxy for asthma in children: a good choice?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that Stock et al. used prescription data to estimate asthma prevalence in children and found notable prevalence peaks, suggesting that prescriptions can be used to identify asthma cases. However, the objective mentioned in abstract [1] was to critically assess and discuss the use of prescription data, implying there may be limitations or considerations in using prescriptions as a proxy. Since the data was used but with critical assessment, it suggests that prescriptions are a reasonable but not perfect proxy.

yes
contexts: Stock et al. (Eur Respir J 25:47-53, 2005) recently estimated asthma prevalence in Germany using claims data on prescriptions and hospital diagnoses and found high prevalence peaks in infants. Our objective was to critically assess and discuss various aspects of identifying children with asthma using prescription data.

A short course of systemic corticosteroids is an important therapy in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations. Although a 5-day course of oral prednisone or prednisolone has become the most commonly used regimen, dexamethasone has also been used for a shorter duration (1-2 days) with potential for improvement in compliance and palatability. We reviewed the literature to determine if there is sufficient evidence that dexamethasone can be used as an effective alternative in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations in the inpatient setting.

We replicated the selection procedure of Stock et al. using data on 290,919 children aged 0-17 years insured in the Gmünder ErsatzKasse (GEK (gmünder ersatzkasse)) in 2005. Asthma prevalence was also estimated in a sample of 17,641 children aged 0-17 years participating in the German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Children and Adolescents (KiGGS) from 2003 to 2006.

We conducted a cross-sectional survey among adult patients with asthma cared for in 15 managed care organizations in the United States. We collected physicians' estimates of their patients' asthma severity. Physicians' estimates of patients' asthma as being less severe than patient-reported symptoms were classified as underestimates of severity.

A Medline search was conducted on the use of dexamethasone in the treatment of asthma exacerbations in children. The studies selected were clinical trials comparing the efficacy of dexamethasone with prednisone. Meta-analysis was performed examining physician revisitation rates and symptomatic return to baseline.
results.reference: When additional validation studies were taken into account, asthma medications were found to be prescribed not only for asthma but also for other respiratory diseases. In addition, not all children with current asthma had prescriptions. We therefore conclude that asthma medications are therefore not a good proxy for the disease.

results.question: Does the familial transmission of drinking patterns persist into young adulthood?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that offspring of abstaining families drank less than those from non-abstaining families, but the differences in drinking levels were not statistically significant across the distribution. Additionally, actual drinking levels in drinking families showed little to no association with offspring drinking patterns. Therefore, the evidence suggests that familial transmission of drinking patterns does not strongly persist into young adulthood.

no
contexts: To explore the long-term (10-year) transmission of familial drinking during adolescence to offspring drinking patterns in young adulthood.

Young adults whose families were abstainers in 2000 drank substantially less across quintiles in 2010 than offspring of non-abstaining families. The difference, however, was not statistically significant between quintiles of the conditional distribution. Actual drinking levels in drinking families were not at all or weakly associated with drinking in offspring. Supplementary analyses confirmed these patterns.

Swedish longitudinal study, assessing the relationship between familial drinking in 2000 and offspring drinking in 2010 using simultaneous quantile regression analysis (n=744).DATA: Data on familial drinking was gathered from the Swedish level-of-living surveys (LNU (living surveys)) and from partner LNU (living surveys) in 2000 while data on offspring drinking in young adulthood was gathered from LNU (living surveys) 2010. Drinking among offspring, parents and potential stepparents was measured through identical quantity-frequency indices referring to the past 12 months in 2010 and 2000 respectively.

With a 2 (confederate's drinking condition: alcohol vs. soda) × 2 (participant's stress condition: stress vs. no stress) experimental design, we tested whether the tendency to imitate other people's drinking was related to participants' induced stress levels. The young male adults (N = 106) were randomly assigned to each of the conditions. In each session, directly after the stress or no-stress period, confederates and participants entered a bar laboratory where we observed their drinking behavior. Prior to entering the session, confederates were instructed to drink alcohol or soda.

That alcohol consumption is strongly influenced by the drinking behavior of social company has been demonstrated in observational research. However, not everyone is equally vulnerable to other people's drinking, and it is important to unravel which factors underlie these individual differences. This study focuses on the role of psychosocial stress in attempting to explain individual differences in the propensity to imitate alcohol consumption.
results.reference: The association between familial drinking and offspring drinking in young adulthood exhibits clear non-linear trends. Changes in the lower part of the familial drinking distribution are strongly related to drinking in young adults, but the actual levels of drinking in drinking families appear less important in shaping the drinking patterns of the offspring in young adulthood.

results.question: Proof of concept study: does fenofibrate have a role in sleep apnoea syndrome?
results.answer:
The proof-of-concept study described involved fenofibrate treatment in patients with sleep apnoea syndrome and evaluated various sleep variables including the apnoea/hypopnoea index and oxygen saturation. Although the study was exploratory with limitations such as short treatment duration and mild to moderate sleep apnoea severity, it was designed to investigate fenofibrate's effect on sleep apnoea indices, implying a potential role. Therefore, the evidence supports that fenofibrate may have a role in sleep apnoea syndrome.

yes
contexts: Proof-of-concept study comprising a placebo run-in period (1 week, 5 weeks if fibrate washout was required) and a 4-week randomized, double-blind treatment period. Thirty-four subjects (mean age 55 years, body mass index 34 kg/m 2 , fasting triglycerides 3.5 mmol/L) with diagnosed sleep apnoea syndrome not treated with continuous positive airways pressure were enrolled and randomized to once daily treatment with fenofibrate (145 mg NanoCrystal(R) tablet) or placebo. Overnight polysomnography, computerized attention/vigilance tests and blood sampling for measurement of lipids, insulin, fasting plasma glucose and fibrinogen were performed at the end of each study period.
To investigate the effect of fenofibrate on sleep apnoea indices.

As this was an exploratory study, a range of sleep variables were evaluated. The apnoea/hypopnoea index (AHI (apnoea/hypopnoea index)) and percentage of time spent with arterial oxygen saturation (SpO(2))<90% were relevant as they have been evaluated in other clinical trials. Other variables included total apnoeas, hypopnoeas and oxygen desaturations, and non-cortical micro-awakenings related to respiratory events per hour.
Exploratory study in patients with mild to moderate sleep apnoea, limited treatment duration; concomitant hypnotic treatment (35%); lack of correction for multiplicity of testing.

We performed a prospective cohort study in an obese population. Measurements of obesity were made, OSA (obstructive sleep apnoea) severity was recorded, and the 95th centile autoCPAP pressure was recorded during 1 week of autoCPAP. Spearman's rank correlation was performed between measurements of obesity and autoCPAP pressure, and between OSA (obstructive sleep apnoea) severity and autoCPAP pressure.
results.reference: The consistent direction of change in sleep indices in this proof-of-concept study may support further investigation of fenofibrate in moderate to severe sleep apnoea syndrome.

results.question: Can mental imagery functional magnetic resonance imaging predict recovery in patients with disorders of consciousness?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that mental imagery fMRI can identify activation in brain regions associated with consciousness in patients with disorders of consciousness. Specifically, patients in a vegetative state (VS) who showed significant activation in mental imagery tasks all improved to at least a minimally conscious state (MCS), suggesting that fMRI activation predicts recovery potential. Therefore, mental imagery fMRI appears to have prognostic value in predicting recovery in these patients.

yes
contexts: To determine the potential prognostic value of using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging)) to identify patients with disorders of consciousness, who show potential for recovery.

Participants performed a mental imagery fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging) paradigm. They were asked to alternately imagine playing tennis and navigating through their home. In 14 of the 22 examined patients (VS, n=5; MCS, n=9), a significant activation of the regions of interest (ROIs (regions of interest)) of the mental imagery paradigm could be found. All 5 patients with activation of a significant blood oxygen level dependent signal, who were in a VS at the time of the fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging) examination, reached at least an MCS at the end of the observation period. In contrast, 5 participants in a VS who failed to show activation in ROIs (regions of interest), did not (sensitivity 100%, specificity 100%). Six of 9 patients in an MCS with activation in ROIs (regions of interest) emerged from an MCS. Of 3 patients in an MCS who did not show activation, 2 patients stayed in an MCS and 1 patient emerged from the MCS (sensitivity 85%, specificity 40%).

Disorders of consciousness (DOC (disorders of consciousness)) diagnosis relies on the presence or absence of purposeful motor responsiveness, which characterizes the minimally conscious state (MCS (minimally conscious state)) and the unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome)), respectively. Functional neuroimaging studies have raised the question of possible residual conscious awareness also in clinically-defined UWS (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome) patients. The aim of our study was to identify electrophysiological parameters, by means of a transcranial magnetic stimulation approach, which might potentially express the presence of residual networks sustaining fragmentary behavioral patterns, even when no conscious behavior can be observed.
A prospective follow-up of subjects from a previously reported MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) study.
To investigate the importance of loss of consciousness (LOC (loss of consciousness)) in predicting neuropsychological test performance in a large sample of patients with head injury.
results.reference: The fMRI paradigm mental imagery displays a high concordance with the further clinical course of patients in a VS. All 5 patients in a VS who showed significant activation of ROIs had a favorable further course until the end of the observation period. We therefore propose the term "functional minimally conscious state" for these patients. They may benefit from rehabilitation treatment. In cases where no significant activation was seen, the method has no prognostic value. Prediction of the clinical course of patients in an MCS by fMRI was considerably less accurate than in patients in a VS.

results.question: The nurse cystoscopist: a feasible option?
results.answer:
The study comparing a trained urology nurse practitioner (UNP) and a consultant urologist in detecting bladder tumors during flexible cystoscopy showed very close agreement (Kappa = 0.94) with only one tumor missed by each examiner. This high level of accuracy indicates that a nurse cystoscopist is a feasible option for detecting bladder tumors.

yes
contexts: To compare the accuracy achieved by a trained urology nurse practitioner (UNP (urology nurse practitioner)) and consultant urologist in detecting bladder tumours during flexible cystoscopy.

Eighty-three patients underwent flexible cystoscopy by both the UNP (urology nurse practitioner) and consultant urologist, each unaware of the other's findings. Before comparing the findings, each declared whether there was tumour or any suspicious lesion requiring biopsy.

Of 83 patients examined by flexible cystoscopy, 26 were found to have a tumour or a suspicious lesion. One tumour was missed by the UNP (urology nurse practitioner) and one by the urologist; each tumour was minute. Analysis using the chance-corrected proportional agreement (Kappa) was 0.94, indicating very close agreement.

To determine current practice and to assess the value of routine follow-up procedures for endometrial cancer surveillance. To discuss whether such procedures are feasible and effective to identify asymptomatic recurrences and describe the pattern of relapse detected by procedures.

These data were obtained from a prospective observational trial of women choosing the copper T380A IUD (intrauterine device) for EC (emergency contraception). Insertions were performed by nurse practitioners at two family planning clinics in order to generalize findings to the type of service setting most likely to employ this intervention. Adjuvant measures to facilitate difficult IUD (intrauterine device) insertions (cervical anesthesia, dilation, pain medication, and use of ultrasound guidance) were not utilized. The effect of parity on IUD (intrauterine device) insertion success was determined using exact logistic regression models adjusted for individual practitioner failure rates.
results.reference: A UNP can be trained to perform cystoscopy and detect suspicious lesions as accurately as can a consultant urologist. Legal and training issues in implementation are important.

results.question: Is cardiovascular evaluation necessary prior to and during beta-blocker therapy for infantile hemangiomas?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that cardiovascular evaluations, including ECG and monitoring of heart rate and blood pressure, were performed before and during beta-blocker therapy in patients with infantile hemangiomas. Although some ECG abnormalities and hypotension were observed, no serious complications or contraindications to therapy were reported, suggesting that cardiovascular evaluation is part of the standard care to ensure safety during treatment.

yes
contexts: We sought to analyze cardiovascular evaluations in patients with IH (infantile hemangiomas) at baseline and during treatment with an oral beta-blocker.

Although consensus guidelines for pretreatment evaluation and monitoring of propranolol therapy in patients with infantile hemangiomas (IH (infantile hemangiomas)) have been formulated, little is known about the cardiovascular side effects.

Data from 109 patients with IH (infantile hemangiomas) were retrospectively analyzed. Patient and family history, pretreatment electrocardiogram (ECG (electrocardiogram)), heart rate, and blood pressure were evaluated before initiation of beta-blocker therapy. Blood pressure and standardized questionnaires addressing side effects were evaluated during treatment.

Questionnaire analyses (n = 83) identified 3 cases with a family history of cardiovascular disease in first-degree relatives. ECG (electrocardiogram) findings were normal in each case and no serious complication of therapy occurred. ECG (electrocardiogram) abnormalities were found in 6.5% of patients but there were no contraindications to beta-blocker therapy and no major complications. Hypotension in 9 patients did not require therapy adjustment. In all, 88 parents (81%) reported side effects during beta-blocker treatment.
Hypoglycaemia caused by glucose-lowering therapy has been linked to cardiovascular (CV (cardiovascular)) events. The ORIGIN trial provides an opportunity to further assess this relationship.
results.reference: Pretreatment ECG is of limited value for patients with an unremarkable cardiovascular history and a normal heart rate and blood pressure. Hypotension may occur during treatment.

results.question: Is specialty care associated with improved survival of patients with congestive heart failure?
results.answer:
The first abstract suggests that implementing complex treatment strategies for congestive heart failure, which may require certain expertise (implying specialty care), is associated with improved survival. Additionally, the third abstract indicates that delayed or less intensive care (which could be related to less specialized care) leads to worse outcomes in heart conditions. Together, these imply that specialty care is associated with improved survival in CHF patients.

yes
contexts: Implementation of the complex treatment strategies that have been shown to improve survival of patients with congestive heart failure (CHF (congestive heart failure)) may require certain expertise. We wanted to examine the association between pattern of outpatient care and survival of patients with CHF (congestive heart failure).

The promise of specialty pharmaceuticals: increased life expectancy, improved quality of life, enhanced workplace productivity, decreased burden of disease, and reduced health care spending comes at a significant cost. These agents require special handling, administration, patient education, clinical support, and risk mitigation. Additionally, specialty drugs require distribution systems that ensure appropriate patient selection and data collection. With the specialty pharmaceutical pipeline overflowing with new medicines and an aging population increasingly relying on these novel treatments to treat common diseases, the challenge of managing the costs associated with these agents can be daunting. Aided by sophisticated pharmacoeconomic models to assess value, the cost impacts of these specialty drugs can be appropriately controlled.

Weekend AMI (acute myocardial infarction) patients are significantly less likely to receive immediate intensive cardiac procedures, and experience significantly higher rates of adverse health outcomes. Weekend admission leads to a 3.47 percentage point reduction in catheterization at 1 day, a 1.52 point reduction in angioplasty, and a 0.35 point reduction in by-pass surgery (p<.001 in all cases). The primary effect is delayed treatment, as weekend-weekday procedure differentials narrow over time from the initial hospitalization. Weekend patients experience a 0.38 percentage point (p<.001) increase in 1-year mortality and a 0.20 point (p<.001) increase in 1-year readmission with congestive heart failure.

Specialty pharmaceuticals have evolved beyond their status as niche drugs designed to treat rare conditions and are now poised to become the standard of care in a wide variety of common chronic illnesses. Due in part to the cost of these therapies, payers are increasingly demanding evidence of their value. Determining the value of these medications is hampered by a lack of robust pharmacoeconomic data.

We performed a linked database analysis of all patients undergoing congenital heart surgery from July 1, 2010 to December 31, 2012. We collected data on the cardiac diagnoses, preoperative status, procedure, and postoperative course, including the duration of invasive and noninvasive ventilation, failure of extubation, hemodynamic data, length of stay, complications, and mortality. A multivariable model was used to assess the independent factors associated with an inability to extubate within the operating room and with delayed extubation (>24 hours).
results.reference: We found an improved survival associated with cardiologist care and a mixture of general practitioner and cardiologist care compared with general practitioner care. The pattern of outpatient care may therefore be important for the survival of patients with CHF.

results.question: Can the prognosis of polymyalgia rheumatica be predicted at disease onset?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that baseline factors associated with the duration of steroid therapy, relapse, and late development of giant cell arteritis (GCA) in polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) patients were identified using statistical methods at disease onset. This suggests that prognosis can be predicted based on initial clinical features.

yes
contexts: Women's vulnerability for a first lifetime-onset of major depressive disorder (MDD (major depressive disorder)) during midlife is substantial. It is unclear whether risk factors differ for first lifetime-onset and recurrent MDD (major depressive disorder). Identifying these risk factors can provide more focused depression screening and earlier intervention. This study aims to evaluate whether lifetime psychiatric and health histories, personality traits, menopausal status and factors that vary over time, e.g. symptoms, are independent risk factors for first-onset or recurrent MDD (major depressive disorder) across 13 annual follow-ups.

This study was planned to evaluate whether increased nuchal translucency (NT (nuchal translucency)) thickness in the first trimester of gestation can be related to onset of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM (gestational diabetes mellitus)) during pregnancy.
To identify the features of PMR that may predict the duration of steroid therapy, the occurrence of relapses and the late development of GCA.

After controlling for age of onset, there were no differences in prior suicide attempts by polarity although bipolar participants had more prior severe attempts. During follow-up, 40 cycles ended in suicide and 384 cycles contained at least one suicide attempt. Age, hopelessness and active substance abuse but not polarity predicted suicidal behavior. The effects of risk factors did not differ by polarity.

Prospective cohort study of 176 patients with PMR, followed up for 5 years. Baseline factors associated with the duration of steroids therapy were identified using Cox regression. Predictors of relapse and the late development of GCA were identified using binary logistic regression.
results.reference: A higher PV in PMR increases the risk of prolonged steroid therapy and late GCA. Female sex and particular HLA alleles may increase the risk of late GCA. Starting patients on>15 mg prednisolone is associated with a prolonged steroid duration.

results.question: Should ascitis volume and anthropometric measurements be estimated in hospitalized alcoholic cirrotics?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that ascitis volume and anthropometric measurements, such as dry BMI and arm circumference, are significantly associated with mortality and rehospitalization in hospitalized alcoholic cirrhotics. These variables showed prognostic relevance comparable to the Child-Pugh index, suggesting their estimation could be important for patient evaluation and outcome prediction.

yes
contexts: Population (N = 25, all males with alcoholic cirrhosis) was recruited among patients hospitalized for uncomplicated ascitis. Exclusion criteria were refractory or tense ascitis, cancer, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, bleeding varices and critical illness. Measurements included ultrasonographically estimated ascitis volume, dry body mass index/BMI (body mass index) , upper arm anthropometrics, hematologic counts and liver function tests.

Ascitis and undernutrition are frequent complications of cirrhosis, however ascitis volume and anthropometric assessment are not routinely documented or considered in prognostic evaluation. In a homogeneous cohort followed during two years these variables were scrutinized, aiming to ascertain relevance for longterm outcome.

Population (age 48.3 ± 11.3 years, BMI (body mass index) 21.1 ± 3.5 kg/m², serum albumin 2.5 ± 0.8 g/dL) was mostly in the Child-Pugh C category (77.8%) but clinically stable. During the follow-up period of 22.6 ± 3.8 months, additional hospitalizations numbered 1.7 ± 1.0 and more than one quarter succumbed. Admission ascitis volume corresponded to 7.1 ± 3.6 L and dry BMI (body mass index) to 18.3 ± 3.5 kg/m². Child Pugh index was relevant for both mortality and rehospitalization. Nevertheless, similar matches for mortality were documented with ascitis volume and dry BMI (body mass index), and arm circumference below the 5th percentile was highly significantly associated with rehospitalization.

NASH was diagnosed in 58 patients (61%; 30 f) and ASH (alcoholic steatohepatitis) in 37 (39%; 9 f). High-grade fibrosis (59% vs. 19%, P<0.0001) and an AST (aspartate aminotransferase)/ALT (alanine aminotransferase) ratio>1 (54.1% vs 20.7%, P = 0.0008) were more common in ASH (alcoholic steatohepatitis). The MCV was elevated in 53% of ASH (alcoholic steatohepatitis) patients and normal in all NASH patients (P<0.0001). Multivariate analysis identified the MCV (P = 0.0013), the AST (aspartate aminotransferase)/ALT (alanine aminotransferase) ratio (P = 0.011) and sex (P = 0.0029) as relevant regressors (aROC = 0.92). The AST (aspartate aminotransferase)/ALT (alanine aminotransferase) ratio (P<0.0001) and age (P = 0.00049) were independent predictors of high-grade fibrosis. Differences in MCV were more marked in high-grade fibrosis.

A total of 18,605 patients met inclusion criteria; 2067 patients were in the long-distance/high-volume group and 1362 in the short-distance/low-volume group. The median travel distance was 62.6 miles for the long-distance/high-volume group and 2.3 miles for the short-distance/low-volume group. Patients who were younger, white, privately insured, and stage III were more likely to have traveled to a high-volume center. When controlled for patient factors, stage, and hospital factors, patients in the short-distance/low-volume group had lower odds of a lymph node yield ≥12 (OR = 0.51) and neoadjuvant chemoradiation (OR = 0.67) and higher 30-day (OR = 3.38) and 90-day mortality (OR = 2.07) compared with those in the long-distance/high-volume group. The short-distance/low-volume group had a 34% high risk of overall mortality at 5 years compared with the long-distance/high-volume group.
results.reference: A greater association than hitherto acknowledged, between ascitis volume and anthropometric measurements from one side, and long-term rehospitalization and mortality from the other, was demonstrated in male stable alcoholic cirrhotics. Further studies with alcoholic and other modalities of cirrhosis including women are recommended.

results.question: The use of audit to identify maternal mortality in different settings: is it just a difference between the rich and the poor?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that maternal mortality audits identify different causes and contributing factors to maternal deaths in various settings, including both low- and high-income countries, suggesting that differences are not solely based on economic status but also on local factors and healthcare system characteristics. Therefore, the use of audit reveals more complex differences than just rich versus poor.

no
contexts: To illustrate how maternal mortality audit identifies different causes of and contributing factors to maternal deaths in different settings in low- and high-income countries and how this can lead to local solutions in reducing maternal deaths.
Descriptive study of maternal mortality from different settings and review of data on the history of reducing maternal mortality in what are now high-income countries.

It is uncertain whether the inverse equity hypothesis-the idea that new health interventions are initially primarily accessed by the rich, but that inequalities narrow with diffusion to the poor-holds true for cancer screening in low and middle income countries (LMICs (low and middle income countries)).This study examines the relationship between overall coverage and economic inequalities in coverage of cancer screening in four middle-income countries.

Although record linkage of routinely collected health datasets is a valuable research resource, most datasets are established for administrative purposes and not for health outcomes research. In order for meaningful results to be extrapolated to specific populations, the limitations of the data and linkage methodology need to be investigated and clarified. It is the objective of this study to investigate the differences in ascertainment which may arise between a hospital admission dataset and a dispensing claims dataset, using major depression in pregnancy as an example. The safe use of antidepressants in pregnancy is an ongoing issue for clinicians with around 10% of pregnant women suffer from depression. As the birth admission will be the first admission to hospital during their pregnancy for most women, their use of antidepressants, or their depressive condition, may not be revealed to the attending hospital clinicians. This may result in adverse outcomes for the mother and infant.

Rising health care costs and the need to consolidate expertise in tertiary services have led to the centralisation of services. In the UK, the result has been that many rural maternity units have become midwife-led. A key consideration is that midwives have the skills to competently and confidently provide maternity services in rural areas, which may be geographically isolated and where the midwife may only see a small number of pregnant women each year. Our objective was to compare the views of midwives in rural and urban settings, regarding their competence and confidence with respect to 'competencies' identified as being those which all professionals should have in order to provide effective and safe care for low-risk women.
results.reference: Differences in maternal mortality are more than just differences between the rich and poor. Acknowledging the magnitude of maternal mortality and harnessing a strong political will to tackle the issues are important factors. However, there is no single, general solution to reduce maternal mortality, and identification of problems needs to be promoted through audit, both national and local.

results.question: Could the extent of lymphadenectomy be modified by neoadjuvant chemotherapy in cervical cancer?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts discuss the impact of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) on lymph node metastasis patterns and rates in cervical cancer but do not specifically address whether NACT modifies the extent of lymphadenectomy performed. There is no direct information on changes to the surgical approach or lymph node dissection extent due to NACT.

no
contexts: The effect of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)) on topographical distribution patterns of lymph node metastasis in cervical cancer was unknown.

We analyzed groups of 167 and 140 patients who were diagnosed with lymph node metastasis in the matched primary surgery group and NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group, respectively, and no significant difference was observed (p = 0.081). The incidence of lymph node metastasis was significantly decreased in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group compared to the non-responsive group (18.4% vs. 38.6%, P<0.001). The metastatic rates for every lymph node group also declined in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group except for the deep inguinal and the para-aortic lymph node groups. Clinical response, deep stromal, parametrial and lymph vascular invasions were independent risk factors for lymph node metastasis in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group. Furthermore, deep stromal invasion and lymph vascular invasion, but not the response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), were independently associated with upper LNM. The number of lymph nodes involved, response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), tumor histology and a positive vaginal margin were independent prognostic factors affecting DFS or OS rates in node-positive patients treated with NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) plus radical surgery.

Patients with FIGO stage IB1-IIB who underwent radical surgery with or without NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) were enrolled (3527 patients). A matched-case comparison design was used to compare the effects of NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) on lymph node metastasis.

The outcomes of interest were margins, lymph node yield, receipt of neoadjuvant chemoradiation, adjuvant chemotherapy, readmission within 30 days, 30-day and 90-day mortality, and 5-year overall survival.

From 1993 to 1999, 667 patients received curative lung resection and complete hilar and mediastinal lymphadenectomy for non-small cell lung cancer. Of these, there were 436 Stage I disease (65%), of whom 144 T1N0 and 292 T2N0. No patients had pre- or postoperative radio- or chemotherapy. Prognostic significance of the following independent variables was tested using univariate (log-rank) and multivariate (Cox proportional-hazards) analysis: type of resection (sublobar vs lobectomy vs pneumonectomy), histology (squamous cell vs adenocarcinoma), tumour size (<or=3cm vs>3cm), histologic vascular invasion, visceral pleura involvement, positive bronchial resection margin, general T status.
results.reference: The frequency and topographic distribution of LNM are not modified by NACT, and clinical non-responders showed more involved LNs. A systemic and extensive lymphadenectomy should be performed in patients treated with NACT plus surgery regardless of the response to NACT.

results.question: Do Wound Cultures Give Information About the Microbiology of Blood Cultures in Severe Burn Patients?
results.answer:
The data indicate that in severe burn patients, there is a significant overlap between pathogens found in wound cultures and those found in blood cultures. Specifically, 44% of blood isolates were previously documented in wound cultures, and transmission of the same pathogen from wound to blood was noted in 65% of bacteremic patients, supporting that wound cultures provide relevant microbiological information about blood cultures.

yes
contexts: Of 195 severe burn patients, 88 had at least 1 BSI (blood stream infection) episode. Transmission of the same pathogen from wound to blood was documented in 30% of the patients, with a rising BSI (blood stream infection) frequency as the Ryan score increased. Documentation of all bacterial and fungal wound and blood isolates from severe burn patients hospitalized in the burn unit and intensive care unit was obtained from medical records retrieved retrospectively from a computerized, hospital-wide database over a 13-year period. Eighty-three patients met the study criteria. Most (92%) were Caucasian and had advanced stage disease (71%). Primary tumors were 58% ovary, 35% endometrium, and 6% cervix. All patients were receiving chemotherapy on admission (72% for primary, 28% for recurrent disease). Forty-eight percent had a positive culture, and most (58%) positive cultures were urine. Seventy-six percent of patients were considered low risk. High-risk patients were more likely to have a severe complication (10% versus 50%, p=0.0003), multiple severe complications (3% versus 20%, p=0.0278), ICU (intensive care unit) admission (2% versus 40%, p<0.0001), overall mortality (2% versus 15%, p=0.0417), and death due to neutropenic fever (0% versus 15%, p=0.0124). MASCC (multinational association for supportive care in cancer) had a positive predictive value of 50% and negative predictive value of 90%. The median MASCC (multinational association for supportive care in cancer) score for all patients was 22 (range, 11-26), but the median MASCC (multinational association for supportive care in cancer) score for those with death or a severe complication was 17 (range, 11-24).

All patients healed their wound properly and no adverse events were recorded. Patients treated conservatively were cured in a mean period of 30 days, while patients treated with CSF drainage were cured in a mean period of 10 days.
results.reference: When there is clinical suspicion of sepsis, appropriate empirical systemic antibiotic therapy should be broad spectrum and should rely on the susceptibility of the organisms from recent cultures of the burn wound surface, until the blood cultures results are completed.

results.question: Are behavioural risk factors to be blamed for the conversion from optimal blood pressure to hypertensive status in Black South Africans?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that behavioral risk factors such as smoking and alcohol intake are associated with the development of hypertension in Africans with initially optimal blood pressure. Specifically, those who became hypertensive smoked more and had higher alcohol intake, which predicted changes in blood pressure and vascular measures. Therefore, behavioral risk factors do contribute to the conversion from optimal blood pressure to hypertensive status in Black South Africans.

yes
contexts: Longitudinal cohort studies in sub-Saharan Africa are urgently needed to understand cardiovascular disease development. We, therefore, explored health behaviours and conventional risk factors of African individuals with optimal blood pressure (BP (blood pressure)) (≤ 120/80 mm Hg), and their 5-year prediction for the development of hypertension.

At baseline, 48% of the participants were hypertensive (≥ 140/90 mmHg). Those with optimal BP (n = 478) were followed at a success rate of 70% for 5 years (213 normotensive, 68 hypertensive, 57 deceased). Africans that became hypertensive smoked more than the normotensive individuals (68.2% vs 49.8%), and they also had a greater waist circumference [ratio of geometric means of 0.94 cm (95% CI (confidence interval): 0.86-0.99)] and greater amount of γ-glutamyltransferase [0.74 U/l (95% CI (confidence interval): 0.62-0.88)]at baseline. Waist circumference was another predictor of BP (blood pressure) changes [β = 0.18 cm (95% CI (confidence interval): 0.05-0.24)]and CSWA (cross-sectional wall area). Hypertension is one of the important contributing factors linked with both causation and development of kidney disease. It is a multifactorial, polygenic, and complex disorder due to interaction of several risk genes with environmental factors. The present study was aimed to explore genetic polymorphism in ACE-1 gene as a risk factor for CKD (chronic kidney disease) among hypertensive patients.

Mean age was higher in the control group (p < 0.05). Of study participants, 36% were male. Prevalence of casual high BP (blood pressure) was 19%. In the population, 10% were current cigarette smokers and habitual alcohol use was high at 56%. Individuals with an elevated RHR (resting heart rate) had a higher risk (OR 1.94, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.15-3.26%, p = 0.013) of casual high BP (blood pressure) compared with participants with normal RHR (resting heart rate) independently of several established CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk factors. results.reference: During the 5 years, 24% of Africans with optimal BP developed hypertension. The surge in hypertension in Africa is largely explained by modifiable risk factors. results.question: Systematic use of patient-rated depression severity monitoring: is it helpful and feasible in clinical psychiatry?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1] and [2] shows that the systematic use of the PHQ-9, a patient-rated depression severity measure, was successfully implemented in 17 psychiatric practices and influenced clinical decision-making in 93% of patient contacts. Additionally, treatment changes were made in 40% of these contacts based on PHQ-9 scores, indicating both feasibility and helpfulness in routine clinical psychiatry.

yes
contexts: The Nine-Item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) for monitoring depression severity was introduced in 19 diverse psychiatric practices. During the one-year course of the project the helpfulness and feasibility of implementation of PHQ-9 in these psychiatric practices were studied. The project was modeled after the Institute for Healthcare Improvement Breakthrough Series. Two of the 19 practices dropped out during the course of the project.

By the conclusion of the study, all remaining 17 practices had adopted PHQ-9 as a routine part of depression care in their practice. On the basis of responses from 17 psychiatrists from those practices, PHQ-9 scores influenced clinical decision making for 93% of 6,096 patient contacts. With the additional information gained from the PHQ-9 score, one or more treatment changes occurred during 40% of these clinical contacts. Changing the dosage of antidepressant medication and adding another medication were the most common treatment changes recorded by psychiatrists, followed by starting or increasing psychotherapy and by switching or initiating antidepressants. In 3% of the patient contacts, using the PHQ-9 led to additional suicide risk assessment.

Although record linkage of routinely collected health datasets is a valuable research resource, most datasets are established for administrative purposes and not for health outcomes research. The gap between evidence-based treatments and routine care has been well established. Findings from the Sequenced Treatments Alternatives to Relieve Depression (STAR*D) emphasized the importance of measurement-based care for the treatment of depression as a key ingredient for achieving response and remission; yet measurement-based care approaches are not commonly used in clinical practice.

Evidence suggests substantial comorbidity between symptoms of somatization and depression in clinical as well as nonclinical populations. However, as most existing research has been retrospective or cross-sectional in design, very little is known about the specific nature of this relationship. In particular, it is unclear whether somatic complaints may heighten the risk for the subsequent development of depressive symptoms.
results.reference: The study findings suggest that adopting measurement-based care, such as using the PHQ-9, is achievable, even in practices with limited resources.

results.question: Treadmill training post stroke: are there any secondary benefits?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that treadmill training was explored for secondary benefits in people in the chronic stage of stroke recovery (abstract 1). Additionally, interventions included treadmill walking sessions (abstract 5), suggesting an interest in benefits beyond primary walking speed improvement. Although specific secondary benefits are not detailed, the context implies that secondary benefits were a focus of investigation.

yes
contexts: To explore the secondary benefits of treadmill training for people in the chronic stage of recovery from stroke.
Twenty individuals post first stroke who acknowledged walking slower than pre stroke. Participants matched by side of hemiparesis and motor impairment.

In primary and secondary prevention trials, statins have been shown to reduce the risk of stroke. In addition to lipid lowering, statins have a number of antiatherothrombotic and neuroprotective properties. In a preliminary observational study, we explored whether clinical outcome is improved in patients who are on treatment with statins when stroke occurs.

Spasticity and loss of function in an affected arm are common after stroke. Although botulinum toxin is used to reduce spasticity, its functional benefits are less easily demonstrated. This paper reports an exploratory meta-analysis to investigate the relationship between reduced arm spasticity and improved arm function.
Twelve 20-minute sessions of walking on a treadmill or weekly phone call.
