contexts: There is no standard protocol for the evaluation of antiseptics used for skin and mucous membranes in the presence of interfering substances. Our objective was to suggest trial conditions adapted from the NF EN 13727 standard, for the evaluation of antiseptics used in gynecology and dermatology.

Three antiseptic solutions were tested in vitro: a chlorhexidine-benzalkonium (CB (chlorhexidine-benzalkonium)) combination, a hexamidine-chlorhexidine-chlorocresol (HCC (hexamidine-chlorhexidine-chlorocresol)) combination, and povidone iodine (P). The adaptation of trial conditions to the standard involved choosing dilutions, solvent, and interfering substances. The activity of solutions was assessed on the recommended strains at concentrations of 97% (pure solution), 50%, and 10% (diluted solution), and 1%. A logarithmic reduction ≥ 5 was expected after 60seconds of contact, to meet requirements of bactericidal activity.

HCC (hexamidine-chlorhexidine-chlorocresol) did not present any bactericidal activity except on P. aeruginosa at a concentration of 97%. P was not bactericidal on E. hirae at any concentration and on S. aureus at 97%. CB (chlorhexidine-benzalkonium) had the most homogeneous bactericidal activity with a reduction>5 log on the 4 bacterial strains at concentrations of 97%, 50% and 10%.

Little is known about the validity and reliability of expert assessments of the quality of antimicrobial prescribing, despite their importance in antimicrobial stewardship. We investigated how infectious disease doctors' assessments compared with a reference standard (modal expert opinion) and with the assessments of their colleagues.

The accepted treatment protocol for necrotizing fasciitis (NF (necrotizing fasciitis)) consists of extensive surgery and wide spectrum antibiotics. Hyperbaric oxygenation (HBO (hyperbaric oxygenation)) has been recommended as adjuvant therapy for NF (necrotizing fasciitis), improving patient mortality and outcome. However, the beneficial effect of HBO (hyperbaric oxygenation) for NF (necrotizing fasciitis) remains controversial.
results.reference: Adapting the NF EN 13727 standard allowed assessing the 3 tested solutions: only CB was bactericidal in dirty conditions. This study proved the possibility of validating antiseptic choice in vitro, in current practice conditions, for adjunctive treatment of skin and mucous membranes disorders, primarily of bacterial origin or with a potential of superinfection.

results.question: Empiric treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infection with fluoroquinolones in older women in Israel: another lost treatment option?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that resistance rates of Escherichia coli to fluoroquinolones were analyzed in older women with uncomplicated UTI in Israel, with a focus on identifying age groups where resistance surpasses 10%. Since current guidelines recommend avoiding empiric fluoroquinolone therapy when resistance exceeds 10-20%, and the study aimed to identify if this threshold was surpassed in older women, it implies that fluoroquinolones may no longer be appropriate in this population due to increased resistance.

yes
contexts: Current guidelines for the treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI (urinary tract infection)) in women recommend empiric therapy with antibiotics for which local resistance rates do not exceed 10-20%. We hypothesized that resistance rates of Escherichia coli to fluoroquinolones may have surpassed this level in older women in the Israeli community setting.
To identify age groups of women in which fluoroquinolones may no longer be appropriate for empiric treatment of UTI (urinary tract infection).

Resistance rates for ofloxacin were calculated for all cases of uncomplicated UTI (urinary tract infection) diagnosed during the first 5 months of 2005 in a managed care organization (MCO (managed care organization)) in Israel, in community-dwelling women aged 41-75 years. The women were without risk factors for fluoroquinolone resistance. Uncomplicated UTI (urinary tract infection) was diagnosed with a urine culture positive for E. coli. The data set was stratified for age, using 5 year intervals, and stratum-specific resistance rates (% and 95% CI (confidence interval)) were calculated. These data were analyzed to identify age groups in which resistance rates have surpassed 10%.

No clinically significant or management-changing findings were present on scout images, and no radiopaque urinary tract calculi or concerning incidental finding was identified. Scout image estimated effective radiation dose averaged 0.09 mSv in children younger than 1 y, 0.09 mSv in children age 1-5, 0.13 mSv in children age 6-10 and 0.18 mSv in children age 11-18. Total fluoroscopy time per examination averaged 36.7 s (range 34.8-39.6 s for all age group averages). Evaluation of known or suspected vesicoureteral reflux (VUR (vesicoureteral reflux)) and urinary tract infection (UTI (urinary tract infection)) were the most common clinical indications, stated in 40.9% and 37.0% of exams, respectively.

Infection control rate was 31% in retention and 59% in the removal group after initial surgical treatment, and 81% and 91% at latest followup, respectively. Treatment duration was shorter in the retention group and there was no difference in number of additional surgeries and length of hospital stay. Type of treatment (retention versus removal) was the only factor associated with infection control; subgroup analysis in the retention group showed Staphylococcus aureus infection and polyethylene nonexchange as contributing factors for failure of infection control.
results.reference: Physicians who opt to treat UTI in postmenopausal women empirically should consider prescribing drugs other than fluoroquinolones. Concomitant longitudinal surveillance of both antibiotic utilization patterns and uropathogen resistance rates should become routine practice in this managed-care organization.

results.question: Do risk calculators accurately predict surgical site occurrences?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that existing risk calculators for surgical site occurrence (SSO) after open ventral hernia repair have low predictive accuracy, as shown by low AUC values (ranging from 0.50 to 0.69). Although some models can stratify patients into risk tiers significantly, overall, they tend to overestimate or underestimate the actual risk, suggesting limited accuracy in prediction.

no
contexts: Current risk assessment models for surgical site occurrence (SSO (surgical site occurrence)) and surgical site infection (SSI (surgical site infection)) after open ventral hernia repair (VHR (ventral hernia repair)) have limited external validation. Our aim was to determine (1) whether existing models stratify patients into groups by risk and (2) which model best predicts the rate of SSO (surgical site occurrence) and SSI (surgical site infection).

The Ventral Hernia Outcomes Collaborative database (n = 795) had an overall SSO (surgical site occurrence) and SSI (surgical site infection) rate of 23% and 17%, respectively. The AUCs were low for SSO (0.56, 0.54, 0.52, and 0.60) and SSI (0.55, 0.53, 0.50, and 0.58). The VHRS (P = 0.01) and HW-RAT (P < 0.01) significantly stratified patients into tiers for SSO (surgical site occurrence), whereas the VHWG (P < 0.05) and HW-RAT (P < 0.05) stratified for SSI (surgical site infection). In the Prospective database (n = 88), 14% and 8% developed an SSO (surgical site occurrence) and SSI (surgical site infection), respectively. The AUCs were low for SSO (0.63, 0.54, 0.50, 0.57, and 0.69) and modest for SSI (0.81, 0.64, 0.55, 0.62, and 0.73). The ACS-NSQIP (P < 0.01) stratified for SSO (surgical site occurrence), whereas the VHRS (P < 0.01) and ACS-NSQIP (P < 0.05) stratified for SSI (surgical site infection). In both databases, VHRS (ventral hernia risk score), VHWG (ventral hernia working group), and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention overestimated risk of SSO (surgical site occurrence) and SSI (surgical site infection), whereas HW-RAT and ACS-NSQIP underestimated risk for all groups.

Patients who underwent open VHR (ventral hernia repair) and were followed for at least 1 mo were included. Using two data sets-a retrospective multicenter database (Ventral Hernia Outcomes Collaborative) and a single-center prospective database (Prospective)-each patient was assigned a predicted risk with each of the following models: Ventral Hernia Risk Score (VHRS (ventral hernia risk score)), Ventral Hernia Working Group (VHWG (ventral hernia working group)), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wound Class, and Hernia Wound Risk Assessment Tool (HW-RAT). Patients in the Prospective database were also assigned a predicted risk from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP). Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (area under the curve [AUC (area under the curve)]) were compared to assess the predictive accuracy of the models for SSO (surgical site occurrence) and SSI (surgical site infection). Pearson's chi-square was used to determine which models were able to risk-stratify patients into groups with significantly differing rates of actual SSO (surgical site occurrence) and SSI (surgical site infection).

We found that each nomogram could predict aggressive BCR (biochemical recurrence) and PCSM (prostate cancer-specific mortality) in a statistically significant manner and that they all predicted PCSM (prostate cancer-specific mortality) more accurately than they predicted BCR (ie, with higher c-index values).

To examine the ability of various postoperative nomograms to predict prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM (prostate cancer-specific mortality)) and to validate that they could predict aggressive biochemical recurrence (BCR (biochemical recurrence)). Prostate-specific antigen (PSA (prostate-specific antigen)), grade, and stage are the classic triad used to predict BCR (biochemical recurrence) after radical prostatectomy (RP (radical prostatectomy)). Multiple nomograms use these to predict risk of BCR (biochemical recurrence). A previous study showed that several nomograms could predict aggressive BCR (prostate-specific antigen doubling time [PSADT] <9 months) more accurately than BCR (biochemical recurrence). However, it remains unknown if they can predict more definitive endpoints, such as PCSM (prostate cancer-specific mortality).
results.reference: All five existing predictive models have limited ability to risk-stratify patients and accurately assess risk of SSO. However, both the VHRS and ACS-NSQIP demonstrate modest success in identifying patients at risk for SSI. Continued model refinement is needed to improve the two highest performing models (VHRS and ACS-NSQIP) along with investigation to determine whether modifications to perioperative management based on risk stratification can improve outcomes.

results.question: Can EMS Providers Provide Appropriate Tidal Volumes in a Simulated Adult-sized Patient with a Pediatric-sized Bag-Valve-Mask?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that EMS providers using a pediatric BVM delivered lower median tidal volumes compared to the adult BVM, with volumes closer to lung-protective ventilation targets. Although the pediatric BVM provided lower volumes, it still delivered breaths within recommended tidal volume ranges in a simulated setting, suggesting EMS providers can provide appropriate tidal volumes with a pediatric-sized BVM on an adult simulator.

yes
contexts: We enrolled 50 providers from a large, busy, urban fire-based EMS (emergency medical services) agency with 14.96 (SD = 9.92) mean years of experience. Only 1.5% of all breaths delivered with the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) during the ventilation scenarios were below the recommended tidal volume. A greater percentage of breaths delivered in the recommended range occurred when the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) was used (17.5% vs 5.1%, p<0.001). Median volumes for each scenario were 570.5mL, 664.0mL, 663.0mL for the pediatric BMV and 796.0mL, 994.5mL, 981.5mL for the adult BVM (bag-valve-mask). In all three categories of airway devices, the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) provided lower median tidal volumes (p<0.001).

In the prehospital setting, Emergency Medical Services (EMS (emergency medical services)) professionals rely on providing positive pressure ventilation with a bag-valve-mask (BVM (bag-valve-mask)). Multiple emergency medicine and critical care studies have shown that lung-protective ventilation protocols reduce morbidity and mortality. Our primary objective was to determine if a group of EMS (emergency medical services) professionals could provide ventilations with a smaller BVM (bag-valve-mask) that would be sufficient to ventilate patients. Secondary objectives included 1) if the pediatric bag provided volumes similar to lung-protective ventilation in the hospital setting and 2) compare volumes provided to the patient depending on the type of airway (mask, King tube, and intubation).

Using a patient simulator of a head and thorax that was able to record respiratory rate, tidal volume, peak pressure, and minute volume via a laptop computer, participants were asked to ventilate the simulator during six 1-minute ventilation tests. The first scenario was BVM (bag-valve-mask) ventilation with an oropharyngeal airway in place ventilating with both an adult- and pediatric-sized BVM (bag-valve-mask), the second scenario had a supraglottic airway and both bags, and the third scenario had an endotracheal tube and both bags. Participants were enrolled in convenience manner while they were on-duty and the research staff was able to travel to their stations. Prior to enrolling, participants were not given any additional training on ventilation skills.

114 individuals trained in basic life support and bag-valve-mask ventilation participated in this study. Individual characteristics were obtained by the observer and the education and practice level were described by the subjects. Ventilation was delivered with a manual resuscitator connected to a microspirometer and volumes were measured. Subjects completed three procedures: one-handed, two-handed and two-handed half-compression.

An instruction manual of four illustrations with speech bubbles displaying the correct use of the LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®) was designed. Laypersons were handed a bag containing a LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®), a bag mask valve device (BMV (bag mask valve device)), a syringe prefilled with air and the instruction sheet, and were asked to perform and ventilate the manikin as displayed. Time to ventilation was recorded and degree of success evaluated.
results.reference: The study suggests that ventilating an adult patient is possible with a smaller, pediatric-sized BVM. The tidal volumes recorded with the pediatric BVM were more consistent with lung-protective ventilation volumes.

results.question: Can students' scores on preclerkship clinical performance examinations predict that they will fail a senior clinical performance examination?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that students' low performances on year 2 clinical performance examinations (CPEs) strongly predict failure on the senior CPE. Additionally, statistical analyses such as contingency tables and correlations support the predictive value of preclerkship CPE scores for senior CPE outcomes. Therefore, the evidence supports that preclerkship CPE scores can predict failure on the senior CPE.

yes
contexts: Students' low performances relative to their class on the year 2 CPEs were a strong predictor that they would fail the senior CPE (clinical performance examination). Their USMLE (united states medical licensing examination) Step 1 scores also correlated with their performance on the senior CPE (clinical performance examination), although the predictive values for these scores were considerably weaker.

This study was designed to determine whether preclerkship performance examinations could accurately identify medical students at risk for failing a senior clinical performance examination (CPE (clinical performance examination)).

This study used a retrospective case-control, multiyear design, with contingency table analyses, to examine the performance of 412 students in the classes of 2005 to 2010 at a midwestern medical school. During their second year, these students took four CPEs that each used three standardized patient (SP (standardized patient)) cases, for a total of 12 cases. The authors correlated each student's average year 2 case score with the student's average case score on a senior (year 4) CPE (clinical performance examination). Contingency table analysis was carried out using performance on the year 2 CPEs and passing/failing the senior CPE (clinical performance examination). Similar analyses using each student's United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE (united states medical licensing examination)) Step 1 scores were also performed. Sensitivity, specificity, odds ratio, and relative risk were calculated for two year 2 performance standards.

We tested the hypothesis that equal mastery of surgical clerkship objectives can be obtained in a clerkship with and without general surgery. Students chose any two surgical rotations and were assessed by written examination, objective structured clinical examination (OSCE (objective structured clinical examination)), ward evaluations, self-assessment objectives questionnaire, and satisfaction survey.

The score for overall performance at selection achieved statistically significant correlation  with examination performance (r = 0.491 for the AKT (applied knowledge test) and r = 0.526 for the CSA (clinical skills assessment), P<0.01).
results.reference: Under the conditions of this study, preclerkship (year 2) CPEs strongly predicted medical students at risk for failing a senior CPE. This finding opens the opportunity for remediation of deficits prior to or during clerkships.

results.question: Recovery Outcome Measures: Is There a Place for Culture, Attitudes, and Faith?
results.answer:
The first abstract suggests that the Recovery Attitudes Questionnaire (RAQ) raised questions about the links between attitudes, faith, and culture in supporting recovery for people with mental illness in secular multicultural societies, indicating these factors may play a role in recovery outcome measures. Although the other abstracts focus on different topics, the first provides direct evidence that culture, attitudes, and faith are relevant considerations in recovery outcomes.

yes
contexts: Utilization of the Recovery Knowledge Inventory (RKI (recovery knowledge inventory)) and Recovery Attitudes Questionnaire (RAQ (recovery attitudes questionnaire)) in southeastern Australia raised questions about the RAQ (recovery attitudes questionnaire), including links between attitudes, faith, and culture in supporting the recovery journey. These questions are particularly important when considered in the context of people with mental illness who live in secular multicultural societies.
Retrospective analysis of outcome measures.

In a retrospective review of 150 culture-positive and 150 culture-negative consecutively sampled tuberculosis (TB (tuberculosis)) suspects, treatment decisions were analysed at presentation, after the availability of culture detection results and after the availability of drug susceptibility testing (DST (drug susceptibility testing)) culture results.

Although there is evidence for the influential role of transformational leadership on health outcomes, researchers have used either attitude outcomes (e.g. job satisfaction) or softer health measures, such as general well-being. Specific measures of well-being such as sleep quality have not been used, despite its association with working conditions.

A total of 124 (82.7%) culture-positive patients and 35 (23.3%) culture-negative patients started anti-tuberculosis treatment prior to receiving their culture results; 101 patients (33.7%) returned for their results; two (1.3%) initiated treatment based on positive culture and no culture-negative patients discontinued treatment. DST (drug susceptibility testing) was performed on 119 (79.3%) positive cultures: 30 (25.2%) showed any resistance, eight (6.7%) showed multidrug resistance and one (0.84%) showed extensively drug-resistant TB (tuberculosis). Twenty-eight patients (23.5%) returned for their DST (drug susceptibility testing) results. Based on DST (drug susceptibility testing), treatment was modified in four patients (3.4%).
results.reference: This paper discusses the cultural appropriateness of the RAQ in Australian settings, and identifies the need to develop rigorous, inclusive recovery outcome measures.

results.question: Can surgeon familiarization with current evidence lead to a change in practice?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1] and [2] shows that mailing a summary of current evidence to surgeons about prophylactic nasogastric decompression led to a comparison of practice before and after the intervention. This implies that surgeon familiarization with current evidence can influence and change their clinical practice to align more closely with evidence-based recommendations.

yes
contexts: Despite evidence against its utility, many surgeons continue to employ prophylactic nasogastric decompression in elective colonic resection. This study aimed to establish whether an easy and practical intervention, mailing out a summary of current evidence to surgeons, can change surgeons practice to bring it more in line with current evidence.

The use of prophylactic nasogastric (NG (nasogastric)) decompression in elective colonic resections was documented for the 2 consecutive months of October and November, 2004 at the Royal Alexandra Hospital (RAH (royal alexandra hospital)). A one page summary of recent evidence concerning this practice was then mailed to all general surgeons at that institution. A similar second review was carried out for the months of January and February, 2005. The two periods were compared with regards to prophylactic NG (nasogastric) use.

To determine current practice and to assess the value of routine follow-up procedures for endometrial cancer surveillance. To discuss whether such procedures are feasible and effective to identify asymptomatic recurrences and describe the pattern of relapse detected by procedures.

The "July effect" refers to the phenomenon of adverse impacts on patient care arising from the changeover in medical staff that takes place during this month at academic medical centres in North America. There has been some evidence supporting the presence of the July effect, including data from surgical specialties. Uniformity of care, regardless of time of year, is required for patients undergoing major cancer surgery. We therefore sought to perform a population-level assessment for the presence of a July effect in this field.

As with some procedures, trauma fellowship training and greater surgeon experience may result in better outcomes following intramedullary nailing (IMN (intramedullary nailing)) of diaphyseal femur fractures. However, surgeons with such training and experience may not always be available to all patients. The purpose of this study is to determine whether trauma training affects the post-operative difference in femoral version (DFV (difference in femoral version)) following IMN (intramedullary nailing).
results.reference: This study has shown that mailing out a summary of current evidence to surgeons concerning a certain issue is not sufficient to lead to a change in practice.

results.question: Advanced epithelial ovarian carcinoma in Thai women: should we continue to offer second-look laparotomy?
results.answer:
The study shows that patients who underwent second-look laparotomy (SLL) had a significantly lower five-year survival rate (37%) compared to those who refused the procedure (88%), with a statistically significant difference (P<0.001). Additionally, disease-free survival was not significantly improved by SLL. Tumor grade, not SLL, was the only significant prognostic factor for survival. Therefore, the evidence suggests that continuing to offer second-look laparotomy may not be beneficial.

no
contexts: To determine survival among patients with epithelial ovarian carcinoma (EOC (epithelial ovarian carcinoma)) who underwent a second-look laparotomy (SLL (second-look laparotomy)) and those refusing the procedure. Also to analyze factor(s) influencing the survival of the patients.

Medical records were reviewed of patients with advanced EOC (epithelial ovarian carcinoma) who were clinically free of disease after primary surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy between January 1, 1992, and December 31, 1998. All of them were offered SLL (second-look laparotomy). Measurement outcomes include patient survival and disease-free survival.

There were 50 patients with clinically complete remission after chemotherapy. Sixteen patients underwent SLL (second-look laparotomy), and thirty-four patients refused the procedure (NSLL). Seven patients (43.8%) were reported to have positive SLL (second-look laparotomy). After the median follow-up time of 35 months, 12 patients had died, and 5 patients were lost to follow-up. The median survival time for patients with SLL (second-look laparotomy) was about 60 months. Five-year survival rates of patients in the SLL (second-look laparotomy), and NSLL groups were 37 per cent (95%CI (confidence interval) = 7%-69%), and 88 per cent (95%CI (confidence interval) = 65%-96%) respectively (P<0.001). The median time to relapse was about 25 months for patients with negative SLL (second-look laparotomy). Five-year disease-free survival rates of patients in the negative SLL (second-look laparotomy), and NSLL groups were 28 per cent (95%CI (confidence interval) = 4%-59%), and 54 per cent (95%CI (confidence interval) = 34%-70%) respectively (P=0.251). By Cox regression analysis, tumor grade was the only significant prognostic factor influencing patients' survival (HR = 6, 95%CI (confidence interval) of HR = 1.2-34.2).

Surgical excision of ovarian endometriomas in patients desiring pregnancy has recently been criticized because of the risk of damage to healthy ovarian tissue and consequent reduction of ovarian reserve. A correct diagnosis in cases not scheduled for surgery is therefore mandatory in order to avoid unexpected ovarian cancer misdiagnosis. Endometriosis is often associated with high levels of CA125. This marker is therefore not useful for discriminating ovarian endometrioma from ovarian malignancy. The aim of this study was to establish if the serum marker CA72-4 could be helpful in the differential diagnosis between ovarian endometriosis and epithelial ovarian cancer.
To evaluate surgical outcome and survival benefit after quaternary cytoreduction (QC (quaternary cytoreduction)) in epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC (epithelial ovarian cancer)) relapse.
results.reference: The second-look laparotomy doesn't have a favorable impact on overall and disease-free survival. Tumor grade is the only independent prognostic variable for survival of the patients.

results.question: Is high-sensitivity C-reactive protein associated with carotid atherosclerosis in healthy Koreans?
results.answer:
The studies show that while higher hsCRP quartiles initially correlated with increased carotid intima-media thickness (IMT), this association disappeared after adjusting for age and other cardiovascular risk factors. Therefore, hsCRP is not independently associated with carotid atherosclerosis in healthy Koreans.

no
contexts: There is a positive association between chronic inflammation and the risk of cardiovascular disease, but whether there is an association between C-reactive protein (CRP (c-reactive protein)) and carotid atherosclerosis is controversial. We investigated the relationship between high-sensitivity CRP (hsCRP (high-sensitivity crp)) levels and carotid intima-media thickness (IMT (intima-media thickness)) in healthy Koreans.

The serum C-reactive protein (CRP (c-reactive protein)) level correlates with the clinical prognosis in patients with kidney, penile and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (PC (prostate cancer)). We prospectively evaluated the preoperative CRP (c-reactive protein) level as a predictive marker for an advanced tumor stage or high-grade cancer in patients with clinically localized PC (prostate cancer).

We measured hsCRP (high-sensitivity crp) levels, the carotid IMT (intima-media thickness), and conventional cardiovascular risk factors including obesity parameters, blood pressure, lipid profiles, insulin resistance, and smoking habits in 820 volunteers (35-79 years old) in a cross-sectional study.

Poorly differentiated PC (prostate cancer) tends to be more common in patients with elevated CRP (c-reactive protein) levels (15.5 vs. 9.5%, p = 0.08). Analogously, patients with a Gleason score ≥8 PC (prostate cancer) had significantly higher median CRP (c-reactive protein) levels than those with a Gleason score ≤7 PC (1.9 vs. 1.2 mg/l, p = 0.03). However, neither uni- nor multivariate analysis showed an association between the preoperative CRP (c-reactive protein) level and the presence of a locally advanced tumor stage, lymph node metastases or a positive surgical margin. CRP (c-reactive protein) also failed to correlate with the initial PSA (prostate specific antigen) level and the clinical tumor-associated findings. Moreover, multivariate analysis relativized the association between an elevated CRP (c-reactive protein) level and poor tumor differentiation.

Higher hsCRP (high-sensitivity crp) quartile groups had higher mean IMTs, as compared with the lowest quartile (P<0.001 for the trend across quartiles). However, after adjustment for age, the relationship between hsCRP (high-sensitivity crp) level and IMT (intima-media thickness) was substantially weaker (P = 0.018). After additional adjustments for conventional cardiovascular risk factors, no significant association was observed (P = 0.548). The unadjusted risk for a high carotid IMT (intima-media thickness) value (>or = 1.0 mm) was also positively related to hsCRP (high-sensitivity crp) quartile, but this relationship was not significant after adjustment for age and other cardiovascular risk factors.
results.reference: Both hsCRP levels and the carotid IMT were strongly correlated with conventional cardiovascular risk factors, but there was no independent association between hsCRP levels and carotid IMT in healthy Korean adults.

results.question: Validation of the 2009 TNM version in a large multi-institutional cohort of patients treated for renal cell carcinoma: are further improvements needed?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts discuss the TNM staging system for kidney cancers, including recent modifications and subclassifications (abstracts [3] and [5]). However, none of the abstracts specifically address validation of the 2009 TNM version in a large multi-institutional cohort or whether further improvements are needed. Therefore, there is no direct evidence in the provided context to answer the question.

maybe
contexts: To determine whether there is a relationship between VEGF expression and renal vein and vena cava invasion in stage pT3 renal cell carcinoma and to evaluate the impact of VEGF expression on survival in pT3 renal cell carcinoma.

Patients enrolled in the study had been diagnosed with non-small cell carcinoma in stages IV or IIIB with pleural or N2-N3 involvement and with a performance status of 2 or below according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG (eastern cooperative oncology group)). Survival was analyzed with regard to the following variables: age, sex, comorbidity, weight loss, laboratory test results, histological type, ECOG (eastern cooperative oncology group) score, TNM staging, and treatment. The Student t test, the chi(2) test, the Kaplan-Meier method, the log-rank test, and Cox regression analysis were used in the statistical analysis.

A new edition of the TNM was recently released that includes modifications for the staging system of kidney cancers. Specifically, T2 cancers were subclassified into T2a and T2b (<or =10 cm vs>10 cm), tumors with renal vein involvement or perinephric fat involvement were classified as T3a cancers, and those with adrenal involvement were classified as T4 (thyroxine) cancers.

The analysis is based on 122 of 143 previously untreated patients with NPC (nasopharyngeal carcinoma) treated with radiation therapy at The University of Texas M. D. Anderson Cancer Center between 1983 and 1992. Excluded were 4 patients treated with palliative intent, 4 children, 12 patients not staged with CT (computerized tomography), and 1 patient who died of a cerebrovascular accident prior to completion of treatment. The stage distribution was as follows: AJCC Stage I-2, Stage II-7, Stage III-12, Stage IV-101; Tl-15, T2-33, T3 (triiodothyronine)-22, T4 (thyroxine)-52; N0-32, N1-10, N2-47, N3-32, Nx-1. Fifty-nine (48%) patients had squamous cell carcinoma; 63 (52%) had lymphoepitheliomas, undifferentiated NPC (nasopharyngeal carcinoma) or poorly differentiated carcinoma, NOS (UNPC (undifferentiated npc or poorly differentiated carcinoma, nos)). Sixty-seven patients (65 with Stage IV disease) received induction chemotherapy. Fifty-eight patients (24 of whom had induction chemotherapy) were treated with the concomitant boost fractionation schedule. The median follow-up for surviving patients was 57 months.
Our aim was to validate the recently released edition of the TNM staging system for primary tumor classification in kidney cancer.
results.reference: The recently released seventh edition of the primary tumor staging system for kidney tumors is a powerful predictor of CSS. However, some of the substages identified by the classification have overlapping prognoses, and other substages include patients with heterogeneous outcomes. The few modifications included in this edition may have not resolved the most critical issues in the previous version.

results.question: Are interstitial fluid concentrations of meropenem equivalent to plasma concentrations in critically ill patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy?
results.answer:
The data show that interstitial fluid (ISF) concentrations of meropenem are lower than plasma concentrations in patients on continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration, with ISF penetration estimated at 63%-69% of plasma levels. This indicates that ISF concentrations are not equivalent but rather somewhat lower than plasma concentrations in this patient population.

no
contexts: To describe the interstitial fluid (ISF (interstitial fluid)) and plasma pharmacokinetics of meropenem in patients on continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration (CVVHDF (continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration)).

This was a prospective observational pharmacokinetic study. Meropenem (500 mg) was administered every 8 h. CVVHDF (continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration) was targeted as a 2-3 L/h exchange using a polyacrylonitrile filter with a surface area of 1.05 m2 and a blood flow rate of 200 mL/min. Serial blood (pre- and post-filter), filtrate/dialysate and ISF (interstitial fluid) concentrations were measured on 2 days of treatment (Profiles A and B). Subcutaneous tissue ISF (interstitial fluid) concentrations were determined using microdialysis.

A total of 384 samples were collected. During Profile A, the comparative median (IQR) ISF (interstitial fluid) and plasma peak concentrations were 13.6 (12.0-16.8) and 40.7 (36.6-45.6) mg/L and the trough concentrations were 2.6 (2.4-3.4) and 4.9 (3.5-5.0) mg/L, respectively. During Profile B, the ISF (interstitial fluid) trough concentrations increased by ∼40%. Meropenem ISF (interstitial fluid) penetration was estimated at 63% (60%-69%) and 69% (65%-74%) for Profiles A and B, respectively, using comparative plasma and ISF (interstitial fluid) AUCs. For Profile A, the plasma elimination t1/2 was 3.7 (3.3-4.0) h, the volume of distribution was 0.35 (0.25-0.46) L/kg, the total clearance was 4.1 (4.1-4.8) L/h and the CVVHDF (continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration) clearance was 2.9 (2.7-3.1) L/h.

Tacrolimus is a potent immunosuppressive drug used in organ transplantation. Because of its substantial toxic effects, narrow therapeutic index, and interindividual pharmacokinetic variability, therapeutic drug monitoring of whole-blood tacrolimus concentrations has been recommended. We investigated the comparability of the results of 2 immunoassay systems, affinity column-mediated immunoassay (ACMIA (affinity column-mediated immunoassay)) and microparticle enzyme immunoassay (MEIA (microparticle enzyme immunoassay)), comparing differences in the tacrolimus concentrations measured by the 2 methods in relation to the hematologic and biochemical values of hepatic and renal functions.

All three adducts were elevated in uremic plasma. Plasma CML (carboxymethyllysine) levels were mainly (>95%) albumin bound. Their levels were not correlated with fructoselysine levels and were similar in diabetic and non-diabetic patients on hemodialysis, indicating that their increase was not driven by glucose. Pentosidine and MDA (malondialdehyde)-lysine were also increased in plasma to the same extent in diabetic and non-diabetic hemodialysis patients. Statistical analysis indicated that plasma levels of CML (carboxymethyllysine) correlated weakly (P<0.05) with those of pentosidine and MDA (malondialdehyde)-lysine, but that pentosidine and MDA (malondialdehyde)-lysine varied independently (P>0.5).
results.reference: This is the first known report of concurrent plasma and ISF concentrations of a meropenem antibiotic during CVVHDF. We observed that the ISF concentrations of meropenem were significantly lower than the plasma concentrations, although the present dose was appropriate for infections caused by intermediately susceptible pathogens (MIC≤4 mg/L).

results.question: Does Sensation Return to the Nasal Tip After Microfat Grafting?
results.answer:
The study described in the abstracts shows that after microfat injections, patients initially experience decreased sensation in the nasal tip, but this sensation gradually recovers over time, with touch threshold values approaching preoperative levels by 12 weeks. Additionally, the percentage of patients experiencing paresthesia diminishes to none during the follow-up period, indicating that sensation does return.

yes
contexts: Patients usually complain about numbness in the nasal tip after microfat injections. The present study evaluated the severity of the numbness in the nasal tip after the procedure.

To address the research question, a prospective study of young women was designed and performed at the Beijing Anzhen Hospital. Time was the primary predictor variable. The nasal tip sensation, which was evaluated using objective and subjective assessments, was used as the primary outcome variable. The McNemar-Bowker test (time vs nasal tip sensation) was used to detect statistical significance.

A total of 30 young women (age 20.04 ± 3.63 years) were recruited for the present study. The preoperative mean touch threshold value was 3.60 units. One week after the injection, the women experienced a decrease in the touch threshold value by 2.50 units. However, the sensation recovered gradually during the follow-up period (1.51 units at week 2, 2.39 units at week 4, 3.01 units at week 8, and 3.35 units at week 12). Significant differences were detected between multiple different measurement points (P<.05). The percentage of those experiencing paresthesia after the microfat injections also gradually diminished to none.

Only patients with isolated nasal fractures were included in the study. Patients with additional maxillofacial fractures and patients whose application time to our clinic was more than 10 days after the trauma were excluded. Patients were classified into 5 types according to their fracture. All patients underwent closed reduction and external fixation under local anesthesia. Patients were asked about their satisfaction in a survey at 28th day and sixth month after the surgery. Patients were divided into groups according to fracture type and intervention time, and the results of the survey were evaluated.
To describe the biomechanical and wound healing characteristics of corneas after excimer laser keratorefractive surgery.
results.reference: Postoperative numbness occurs in most patients receiving nasal microfat injections. Partial to complete recovery of nasal tip sensation can be expected to occur over a 3-month period.

results.question: Do older men benefit from curative therapy of localized prostate cancer?
results.answer:
The evidence indicates that older men with localized prostate cancer can benefit from curative therapy, but this benefit depends on tumor differentiation and comorbidity status. Specifically, men with moderately or poorly differentiated tumors and mild or no comorbidities experience gains in life expectancy and quality-adjusted life expectancy up to ages 75-80 years. Therefore, older men may benefit from curative treatment if they meet these criteria.

yes
contexts: For men with well-differentiated tumors and few comorbidities, potentially curative therapy (RP (radical prostatectomy) or EBRT (external beam radiotherapy)) prolonged LE (life expectancy) up to age 75 years but did not improve QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) at any age. For moderately differentiated cancers, potentially curative therapy resulted in LE (life expectancy) and QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) gains up to age 75 years. For poorly differentiated disease, potentially curative therapy resulted in LE (life expectancy) and QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) gains up to age 80 years. Benefits of potentially curative therapy were restricted to men with no worse than mild comorbidity. When cohort and pooled case series data were used, RP (radical prostatectomy) was preferred over EBRT (external beam radiotherapy) in all groups but was comparable to modern radiotherapy.

The study evaluated 629 patients with clinically localized PC (prostate cancer) who underwent radical prostatectomy between 2010 and 2013. Exclusion criteria were signs of systemic infection, symptoms of an autoimmune disease or neoadjuvant androgen deprivation.

Prior decision-analytic models are based on outdated or suboptimal efficacy, patient preference, and comorbidity data. We estimated life expectancy (LE (life expectancy)) and quality-adjusted life expectancy (QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy)) associated with available treatments for localized prostate cancer in men aged>/= 65 years, adjusting for Gleason score, patient preferences, and comorbidity.

The treatment and outcome of 369 eligible patients with Stage T1-T3aN0-NXM0 prostate cancer were analyzed during a minimal 10-year follow-up period. All patients were treated with curative intent to a mean dose of 65 Gy. The full history of any metastatic disease was documented for each subject, including the initial site of involvement, any progression over time, and patient survival.

The study population included 994 men (4,937 observations) without prostate cancer in the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging. Mixed effects models were used to examine the relationship between prostate specific antigen and body mass index in kg/m(2) by age. Separate models were explored in men with prostate cancer censored at diagnosis, for percent body fat measurements, for weight changes with time and adjusting for initial prostate size in 483 men (2,523 observations) with pelvic magnetic resonance imaging measurements.
results.reference: Potentially curative therapy results in significantly improved LE and QALE for older men with few comorbidities and moderately or poorly differentiated localized prostate cancer. Age should not be a barrier to treatment in this group.

results.question: Pituitary apoplexy: do histological features influence the clinical presentation and outcome?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts describe a retrospective analysis comparing patients with pituitary apoplexy based on histological features (infarction alone vs. hemorrhagic infarction/hemorrhage) and their clinical presentation and outcomes. This suggests that the study aimed to determine if histological differences influence clinical features and outcomes, implying that histological features do have an impact.

yes
contexts: A retrospective analysis of a contemporary series of patients with pituitary apoplexy was performed to ascertain whether the histopathological features influence the clinical presentation or the outcome.

A retrospective analysis was performed in 59 patients treated for pituitary apoplexy at the University of Virginia Health System, Charlottesville, Virginia, or Groote Schuur Hospital, University of Cape Town, South Africa. The patients were divided into two groups according to the histological features of their disease: one group with infarction alone, comprising 22 patients; and the other with hemorrhagic infarction and/or frank hemorrhage, comprising 37 patients. The presenting symptoms, clinical features, endocrinological status, and outcome were compared between the two groups.
To assess the results of transsphenoidal pituitary surgery in patients with Cushing's disease over a period of 18 years, and to determine if there are factors which will predict the outcome.
The characteristics of both tumors, their association with tumors in other sites and the time of presentation are analyzed.

Patients were divided into three groups (remission, failure and relapse) depending on the late outcome of their treatment as determined at the time of analysis, i.e. 88 months (median) years after surgery. Remission is defined as biochemical reversal of hypercortisolism with re-emergence of diurnal circadian rhythm, resolution of clinical features and adequate suppression on low-dose dexamethasone testing. Failure is defined as the absence of any of these features. Relapse is defined as the re-emergence of Cushing's disease more than one year after operation. Clinical features such as weight, sex, hypertension, associated endocrine disorders and smoking, biochemical studies including preoperative and postoperative serum cortisol, urine free cortisol, serum ACTH, radiological, histological and surgical findings were assessed in relation to these three groups to determine whether any factors could reliably predict failure or relapse after treatment.
results.reference: The patients who presented with histological features of pituitary tumor infarction alone had less severe clinical features on presentation, a longer course prior to presentation, and a better outcome than those presenting with hemorrhagic infarction or frank hemorrhage. The endocrine replacement requirements were similar in both groups.

results.question: Do African American women require fewer calories to maintain weight?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that African American women had a higher baseline weight and BMI and consumed slightly more calories than non-African American women during controlled feeding. After adjusting for confounders, there was no significant difference in caloric intake required to maintain weight between African American and non-African American women. Therefore, the evidence does not support the idea that African American women require fewer calories to maintain weight.

no
contexts: The high prevalence of obesity in African American (AA (american)) women may result, in part, from a lower resting metabolic rate (RMR (resting metabolic rate)) than non-AA (american) women. If true, AA (american) women should require fewer calories than non-AA (american) women to maintain weight. Our objective was to determine in the setting of a controlled feeding study, if AA (american) women required fewer calories than non-AA (american) women to maintain weight.

AA (american) women had higher baseline weight and body mass index than non-AA (american) women (78.4 vs 72.4 kg, P<.01; 29.0 vs 27.6 kg/m(2), P<.05, respectively). During intervention feeding, mean (SD) kcal was 2168 (293) in AA (american) women and 2073 (284) in non-AA (american) women. Mean intake was 94.7 kcal higher in AA (american) women than in non-AA (american) women (P<.05). After adjustment for potential confounders, there was no difference in caloric intake between AA (american) and non-AA (american) women (Δ = -2.8 kcal, P = .95).

This analysis includes 206 women (73% AA (american)), aged 22-75 years, who participated in the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH (dietary approaches to stop hypertension)) trial-a multicenter, randomized, controlled, feeding study comparing the effects of 3 dietary patterns on blood pressure in individuals with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension. After a 3-week run-in, participants were randomized to 1 of 3 dietary patterns for 8 weeks. Calorie intake was adjusted during feeding to maintain stable weight. The primary outcome of this analysis was average daily calorie (kcal) intake during feeding.

African-American and Hispanic women generally experience higher mortality than White non-Hispanics, and these differences are especially significant in the southeast metropolitan areas and southwest border of Texas. The proportion and location of significant racial disparities however changed depending on the type of statistic (RR (relative risk) versus RD (rr) and absolute)) and the geographic level. The largest proportion of significant results was observed for the RD (rr) and absolute) statistic and census tract data. Geographic regions with significant racial disparities for African-Americans and Hispanics frequently had a poverty rate above 10.00%.

Subjects were adult non-Hispanic white, non-Hispanic black, and Mexican American men (n = 7422) and nonpregnant women (n = 7999) who had complete demographic and anthropometric data. In addition to height, allometric models were developed for each measure that controlled for age, race, and self-reported health status.
results.reference: These results do not support the view that AA women are at greater risk for obesity because they require fewer calories to maintain weight.

results.question: Emergency double-balloon enteroscopy combined with real-time viewing of capsule endoscopy: a feasible combined approach in acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) combined with real-time viewing of capsule endoscopy (CE) is feasible in managing acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB). Specifically, abstract [3] reports that this combined approach correctly modified DBE management in 25% of patients, and emergency DBE had a significantly higher detection rate of lesions compared to delayed DBE. This supports the feasibility and usefulness of the combined approach.

yes
contexts: There are few data concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy)) and its usefulness in the management of severe acute obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB (obscure gastrointestinal bleeding)). The aim of this retrospective study was to evaluate emergency DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) and capsule endoscopy (CE (capsule endoscopy)) in patients with overt OGIB (obscure gastrointestinal bleeding), analyzing the feasibility of this combined approach.

Emergency DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) in patients with overt OGIB (obscure gastrointestinal bleeding) was defined as performance within 24 h of symptom onset. We reported 27 patients (16 men, mean age: 64.6 ± 17.9 years) with overt severe bleeding who underwent 29 emergency DBE (22 anterograde, 7 retrograde). Of 27 patients, 16 (59.3%) underwent CE (capsule endoscopy) with real time (RT (real time)) viewing.

Patients were diagnosed with the following: Dieulafoy's lesion (DL; n = 11, 40.7%), angioectasia (n = 7, 25.9%), tumors (n = 4, 14.8%), diverticulum (n = 3, 11.1%), ulcers (n = 2, 7.4%). We diagnosed 23 lesions amenable to endoscopic hemostasis and successfully treated 21 of them (77.8%). DL detection rate was statistically higher in the emergency DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) group than in OGIB (obscure gastrointestinal bleeding) patients with DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) done 24 h after symptom onset (40.7% vs 0.9%, respectively, P < 0.001). Combined approach with RT (real time) viewing by CE (capsule endoscopy) correctly modified DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) management in four patients (25%).

From March 2007 to January 2011, 88 DBE procedures were performed on 66 patients. Indications included evaluation anemia/gastrointestinal bleed, small bowel IBD (inflammatory bowel disease) and dilation of strictures. Video-capsule endoscopy (VCE (video-capsule endoscopy)) was used prior to DBE in 43 of the 66 patients prior to DBE evaluation.

The mean age was 62 years. Thirty-two patients were female, 15 were African-American; 44 antegrade and 44 retrograde DBEs were performed. The mean time per antegrade DBE was 107.4±30.0 minutes with a distance of 318.4±152.9 cm reached past the pylorus. The mean time per lower DBE was 100.7±27.3 minutes with 168.9±109.1 cm meters past the ileocecal valve reached. Endoscopic therapy in the form of electrocautery to ablate bleeding sources was performed in 20 patients (30.3%), biopsy in 17 patients (25.8%) and dilation of Crohn's-related small bowel strictures in 4 (6.1%). 43 VCEs with pathology noted were performed prior to DBE, with findings endoscopically confirmed in 32 cases (74.4%). In 3 cases the DBE showed findings not noted on VCE (video-capsule endoscopy).
results.reference: Emergency DBE is feasible, safe and effective in acute OGIB and may avoid major surgery, diagnosing and successfully treating most patients. Combined approach with RT viewing by CE is especially useful to identify recurrent bleeding vascular lesions such as DL that may be easily misdiagnosed by non-emergency DBE.

results.question: Cardiopulmonary bypass temperature does not affect postoperative euthyroid sick syndrome?
results.answer:
The study compared thyroid function in patients undergoing hypothermic (cold) and normothermic (warm) cardiopulmonary bypass and found similar changes in thyroid hormone levels postoperatively in both groups. These changes included reduced TT4, TT3, and free T3, elevated rT3, and unchanged TSH, indicating that the temperature during CPB did not affect the development of euthyroid sick syndrome. Therefore, CPB temperature does not affect postoperative euthyroid sick syndrome.

yes
contexts: To determine if temperature during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass)) has an effect on perioperative and postoperative thyroid function.

Patients who underwent either cold (26 degrees +/- 5 degrees C) or warm (35 degrees +/- 1 degree C) CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass) were comparable with regard to age, body weight, duration of CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass), cross-clamp time, use of inotropes, total heparin dose, and length of hospital stay. Incidence of postoperative myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, and death were similar. In both groups, TT4 and TT3 were reduced below baseline values beginning with CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass) and persisting for up to 5 days after CPB (p<0.05), free T3 (triiodothyronine) was reduced for up to 3 days after CPB (p<0.05), mean serum rT3 was elevated on POD (postoperative days) 1 and POD (postoperative days) 3 (p<0.05), and TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone) remained unchanged.

Blood was analyzed for serum concentration of total thyroxine (TT4), total triiodothyronine (TT3), free T3 (fT3), reverse T3 (rT3), and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone)) preoperatively, 60 min after CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass) was initiated, 30 min after discontinuing CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass), and on postoperative days (POD (postoperative days)) 1, 3, and 5.
Prospective study comparing thyroid function during and after hypothermic and normothermic CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass).
Twelve patients scheduled to undergo cardiac operations with normothermic (n = 6) or hypothermic (n = 6) CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass).
results.reference: The results of this study suggest that normothermic CPB does not prevent the development of the "euthyroid sick syndrome" during and after CPB. Despite these changes in thyroid function, most patients in both groups had a normal postoperative recovery.

results.question: Body dysmorphic disorder: does it have a psychotic subtype?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) can present with psychotic features, as there is a distinction made between nonpsychotic BDD (with some insight) and psychotic BDD (without insight and of delusional intensity). The studies compare these two subtypes and note differences in psychotic disorder diagnoses, supporting the existence of a psychotic subtype of BDD.

yes
contexts: Although body dysmorphic disorder (BDD (body dysmorphic disorder)) is classified in DSM-III-R as a nonpsychotic somatoform disorder, controversy exists as to whether BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) can present with psychotic features. If it can, this raises the possibility that its DSM-III-R psychotic counterpart-delusional disorder, somatic type--may not be a separate disorder. The purpose of this study was to determine whether patients with nonpsychotic BDD (defined according to DSM-III-R criteria, i.e., with maintenance of some insight) were different from patients with psychotic BDD (those whose preoccupation was without insight and of delusional intensity).

Patients with psychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) displayed a significantly higher rate of lifetime DSM-III-R psychotic disorder diagnoses than patients with nonpsychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder). However, the two groups did not differ significantly on most other variables examined. For instance, both psychotic and nonpsychotic patients displayed significant morbidity; high comorbidity with mood, anxiety, and psychoactive substance use disorders; and apparent preferential response to serotonin reuptake inhibitors rather than to non-serotonin reuptake blocking antidepressants or antipsychotics.

Fifty consecutive patients meeting DSM-III-R criteria A and C for BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) were assessed with a semistructured interview and the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-III-R (SCID (structured clinical interview for dsm-iii-r)). Family histories of psychiatric disorders were blindly assessed. The 24 patients with nonpsychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) were compared with the 26 patients with psychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) with respect to demographics, phenomenology, course of illness, associated features, comorbid psychiatric disorders, family history, and treatment response.

This was a retrospective study of 18 consecutive adults with a partial seizure disorder and PIPE (study group) and 36 patients with a partial seizure disorder but without PIPE (control group). These two groups were compared with respect to the likelihood of developing IPE (interictal psychotic episodes) over an 8-year follow-up period and the variables operant in the development of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Statistical analyses consisted of logistic regression models to identify the variables predictive of the development of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Predictors included: number and location of ictal foci, seizure type, etiology, age at seizure onset, duration of seizure disorder, MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) abnormalities, and psychiatric history prior to the index video/EEG (electroencephalogram) monitoring (other than PIPE (psychotic episodes)).

Women's vulnerability for a first lifetime-onset of major depressive disorder (MDD (major depressive disorder)) during midlife is substantial. It is unclear whether risk factors differ for first lifetime-onset and recurrent MDD (major depressive disorder). Identifying these risk factors can provide more focused depression screening and earlier intervention. This study aims to evaluate whether lifetime psychiatric and health histories, personality traits, menopausal status and factors that vary over time, e.g. symptoms, are independent risk factors for first-onset or recurrent MDD (major depressive disorder) across 13 annual follow-ups.
results.reference: Body dysmorphic disorder may have a closely related psychotic subtype that significantly overlaps with, or may even be the same disorder as, the BDD variant of delusional disorder, somatic type. Inclusion of a psychotic subtype for BDD should be considered for future editions of DSM.

results.question: Does receipt of hospice care in nursing homes improve the management of pain at the end of life?
results.answer:
The provided data indicate that hospice residents in nursing homes were more likely to receive regular treatment for daily pain compared to nonhospice residents (51% vs. 33%), and they were twice as likely to receive regular analgesic treatment after controlling for confounders. Additionally, hospice residents were less likely to receive no analgesics or analgesics not recommended by AMDA, and morphine derivatives were more commonly used in hospice care, suggesting better adherence to pain management guidelines.

yes
contexts: A subset of residents with daily pain near the end of life taken from a matched cohort of hospice (2,644) and nonhospice (7,929) nursing home residents who had at least two resident assessments (Minimum Data Sets (MDSs)) completed, their last between 1992 and 1996, and who died before April 1997. The daily pain subset consisted of 709 hospice and 1,326 nonhospice residents.
To compare analgesic management of daily pain for dying nursing home residents enrolled and not enrolled in Medicare hospice.

Fifteen percent of hospice residents and 23% of nonhospice residents in daily pain received no analgesics (odds ratio (OR) = 0.57, 95% confidence interval (CI (confidence interval)) = 0.45-0.74). A lower proportion of hospice residents (21%) than of nonhospice residents (29%) received analgesics not recommended by AMDA (OR = 0.65, 95% CI (confidence interval) =0.52-0.80). Overall, acetaminophen (not in combination with other drugs) was used most frequently for nonhospice residents (25% of 1,673 prescriptions), whereas morphine derivatives were used most frequently for hospice residents (30% of 1,058 prescriptions). Fifty-one percent of hospice residents and 33% of nonhospice residents received regular treatment for daily pain. Controlling for clinical confounders, hospice residents were twice as likely as nonhospice residents to receive regular treatment for daily pain (adjusted odds ratio = 2.08, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.68-2.56).

Detailed drug use data contained on the last MDS before death were used to examine analgesic management of daily pain. Guidelines from the American Medical Directors Association (AMDA (american medical directors association)) were used to identify analgesics not recommended for use in managing chronic pain in long-term care settings. The study outcome, regular treatment of daily pain, examined whether patients received any analgesic, other than those not recommended by AMDA (american medical directors association), at least twice a day for each day of documented daily pain (i.e., 7 days before date of last MDS).

A secondary analysis of one-hundred-sixty-seven patients referred for treatment of cancer-related pain was conducted. Pain intensity at admission was recorded and patients were divided in three categories of pain intensity: mild, moderate and severe. Patients were offered a treatment with opioid dose titration, according to department policy. Data regarding opioid doses and pain intensity were collected after dose titration was completed. Four levels of opioid response were considered: (a) good pain control, with minimal opioid escalation and without relevant adverse effects; (b) good pain control requiring more aggressive opioid escalation, for example doubling the doses in four days; (c) adequate pain control associated with the occurrence of adverse effects; (d) poor pain control with adverse effects.
results.reference: Findings suggest that analgesic management of daily pain is better for nursing home residents enrolled in hospice than for those not enrolled in hospice.The prescribing practices portrayed by this study reveal that many dying nursing home residents in daily pain are receiving no analgesic treatment or are receiving analgesic treatment inconsistent with AMDA and other pain management guidelines. Improving the analgesic management of pain in nursing homes is essential if high-quality end-of-life care in nursing homes is to be achieved.

results.question: Fulfilling human resources development goal in West Africa: can the training of ophthalmologist diplomates be improved?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts include a study aimed at ascertaining the perspectives of Trainee Ophthalmologist Diplomats on the Ophthalmic Diploma Training in West Africa with a view to improving the program. This indicates that there is an interest and potential for improving the training of ophthalmologist diplomates in the region.

yes
contexts: To ascertain the perspectives of Trainee Ophthalmologist Diplomats (TOD (trainee ophthalmologist diplomats)) on the Ophthalmic Diploma Training (ODT (ophthalmic diploma training)) in West Africa with a view to improving the programme.
A survey of set 2005 TOD (trainee ophthalmologist diplomats) on ODT (ophthalmic diploma training) was carried out in Ghana, 2006.

Longitudinal cohort studies in sub-Saharan Africa are urgently needed to understand cardiovascular disease development. We, therefore, explored health behaviours and conventional risk factors of African individuals with optimal blood pressure (BP (blood pressure)) (≤ 120/80 mm Hg), and their 5-year prediction for the development of hypertension.

The Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology study in the North West Province, South Africa, started in 2005 and included African volunteers (n = 1994; aged>30 years) from a sample of 6000 randomly selected households in rural and urban areas.

As with some procedures, trauma fellowship training and greater surgeon experience may result in better outcomes following intramedullary nailing (IMN (intramedullary nailing)) of diaphyseal femur fractures. However, surgeons with such training and experience may not always be available to all patients. The purpose of this study is to determine whether trauma training affects the post-operative difference in femoral version (DFV (difference in femoral version)) following IMN (intramedullary nailing).
results.reference: The ODT programme ensures ophthalmic manpower for secondary eye care level despite challenges. The stakeholders should look into problems facing the programme in order to improve it.

results.question: Does binge drinking during early pregnancy increase the risk of psychomotor deficits?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that there were no significant differences in motor function at age 5 between children of mothers who reported isolated binge drinking episodes during early pregnancy and those who did not binge drink. Additionally, no association was found with the number or timing of binge episodes. Therefore, the evidence does not support an increased risk of psychomotor deficits due to binge drinking in early pregnancy.

no
contexts: The potential effects of binge drinking during pregnancy on child motor function have only been assessed in a few, small studies. We aimed to examine the effects of binge alcohol consumption during early pregnancy, including number of binge episodes and timing of binge drinking, on child motor function at age 5.

There were no systematic or significant differences in motor function between children of mothers reporting isolated episodes of binge drinking and children of mothers with no binge episodes. No association was observed with respect to the number of binge episodes (maximum of 12) and timing of binge drinking.
To explore the long-term (10-year) transmission of familial drinking during adolescence to offspring drinking patterns in young adulthood.

That alcohol consumption is strongly influenced by the drinking behavior of social company has been demonstrated in observational research. However, not everyone is equally vulnerable to other people's drinking, and it is important to unravel which factors underlie these individual differences. This study focuses on the role of psychosocial stress in attempting to explain individual differences in the propensity to imitate alcohol consumption.

To investigate if fetal gender (1) affects the risk of having an emergency department (ED (emergency department)) visit for asthma; and (2) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes among women who had at least one visit to the ED (emergency department) for asthma during pregnancy.
results.reference: In this study, we found no systematic association between isolated episodes of binge drinking during early pregnancy and child motor function at age 5.

results.question: Does tranexamic acid reduce desmopressin-induced hyperfibrinolysis?
results.answer:
The first abstract states that desmopressin releases tissue-type plasminogen activator, which increases hyperfibrinolysis and causes excessive bleeding. It also suggests that combined use of desmopressin with prior administration of tranexamic acid may decrease fibrinolytic activity and improve postoperative hemostasis. The second abstract describes a study where tranexamic acid was given before surgery along with desmopressin, implying that tranexamic acid can counteract the hyperfibrinolytic effect induced by desmopressin.

yes
contexts: Desmopressin releases tissue-type plasminogen activator, which augments cardiopulmonary bypass--associated hyperfibrinolysis, causing excessive bleeding. Combined use of desmopressin with prior administration of the antifibrinolytic drug tranexamic acid may decrease fibrinolytic activity and might improve postoperative hemostasis.

This prospective randomized study was carried out with 100 patients undergoing coronary artery bypass operations between April 1999 and November 2000 in Gülhane Military Medical Academy. Patients were divided into 2 groups. Desmopressin (0.3 microg/kg) was administrated just after cardiopulmonary bypass and after protamine infusion in group 1 (n = 50). Both desmopressin and tranexamic acid (before the skin incision at a loading dose of 10 mg/kg over 30 minutes and followed by 12 hours of 1 mg.kg(-1).h(-1)) were administrated in group 2 (n = 50).

It is postulated that some aspects of methotrexate toxicity may be related to its action as an anti-folate. results.question: Does ultrasound-scored synovitis depend on the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneous anti-TNF agents in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1], [2], and [5] investigated ultrasound-detected synovitis at peak and trough plasma concentrations of subcutaneous anti-TNF agents in rheumatoid arthritis patients. results.question: Counter sampling combined with medical provider education: do they alter prescribing behavior?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that medical provider education combined with counter sampling led to a significant decrease in the prescribing of COX-2 NSAIDs relative to total NSAID prescriptions in the intervention group, while the control group showed no significant change. However, this intervention did not prevent significant increases in prescriptions for nonsedating antihistamines and PPIs, which also increased in the control group. Overall, the intervention altered prescribing behavior for at least one medication category.

contexts: To observe if medical providers alter their prescribing patterns of three relatively expensive categories of medications provided as samples by manufacturers (focus medications) when they receive additional education from pharmacists concerning the appropriate use of lower cost alternatives (counter samples) that are made available to dispense.

This suggested that the results should focus on changes across the two years of the study within the intervention and control groups rather than across the two groups. Medical providers in the intervention group significantly decreased the use of COX-2 NSAID (non steroidal anti inflammatory drug) prescriptions relative to total NSAID (non steroidal anti inflammatory drug) prescriptions following active intervention (38.9% in year 1 versus 23.7% in year 2, P<0.05). Education and counter sampling did not stop medical providers from significantly increasing the total yearly prescriptions for antihistamines and acid-relief medications that consisted of focus-nonsedating antihistamines (86.7% versus 93.1%, P<0.05) and PPIs (68.9% versus 86.2%, P<0.05). Statistically significant increases in the prescribing of focus-nonsedating antihistamines (77.9% versus 98.3%, P<0.05) and PPIs (77.5% versus 91.4%, P<0.05) were also observed in the control group.

Medical providers in the active intervention group had: 1) education from pharmacists concerning the appropriate use of lower-cost alternatives compared with expensive focus medications 2) counter samples and patient sample handouts available to dispense to patients at their own discretion.

A cross-sectional observational study was performed using a convenience sampling of PED (pediatric emergency department) patients during the fall of 2010. results.reference: Education by pharmacists, combined with access to counter samples, may or may not have an effect on medical provider prescribing, depending on the category of medication targeted for cost control.

results.question: Failed IUD insertions in community practice: an under-recognized problem?
results.answer:
The data show a notable rate of unsuccessful IUD insertions in community family planning clinics, with 19.6% failure in nulliparous women and 13.6% in parous women, indicating that failed IUD insertions occur with some frequency. The study also highlights that adjuvant measures to facilitate difficult insertions were not used, suggesting that failed insertions may be under-recognized in typical community practice settings.

yes
contexts: Six providers performed 197 IUD (intrauterine device) insertion attempts. These providers had a mean of 14.1 years of experience (range 1-27, S.D. ±12.5). Among nulliparous women, 27 of 138 (19.6%) IUD (intrauterine device) insertions were unsuccessful. In parous women, 8 of 59 IUD (intrauterine device) insertions were unsuccessful (13.6%). The adjusted odds ratio (aOR (adjusted odds ratio)) showed that IUD (intrauterine device) insertion failure was more likely in nulliparous women compared to parous women (aOR (adjusted odds ratio)=2.31, 95% CI (confidence interval) 0.90-6.52, p=.09).

The data analysis was conducted to describe the rate of unsuccessful copper T380A intrauterine device (IUD (intrauterine device)) insertions among women using the IUD (intrauterine device) for emergency contraception (EC (emergency contraception)) at community family planning clinics in Utah.

These data were obtained from a prospective observational trial of women choosing the copper T380A IUD (intrauterine device) for EC (emergency contraception). Insertions were performed by nurse practitioners at two family planning clinics in order to generalize findings to the type of service setting most likely to employ this intervention. Adjuvant measures to facilitate difficult IUD (intrauterine device) insertions (cervical anesthesia, dilation, pain medication, and use of ultrasound guidance) were not utilized. Syphilis testing was performed in 56-82% of cases, with no difference between the groups. Where a problem in uterine growth was detected, an appropriate response occurred in 0-8% of patients and no difference before or after completion of the PEP (perinatal education programme) was ascertained. In all groups, estimation of fetal weight and pelvimetry were seldom performed, the urine and fetal heart rate documentation were moderately well done and the blood pressure monitoring, assessment of head above pelvis, monitoring of contractions and plotting of cervical dilatation were usually performed. No differences before or after the PEP (perinatal education programme) were detected. Where problems were detected, appropriate actions taken during labour improved, but not significantly.

results.reference: The high rate of unsuccessful IUD insertions reported here, particularly for nulliparous women, suggests that the true insertion failure rate of providers who are not employing additional tools for difficult insertions may be much higher than reported in clinical trials. results.question: Type II supracondylar humerus fractures: can some be treated nonoperatively?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that some type II supracondylar humerus fractures can indeed be treated nonoperatively, as 57.9% of fractures in the study were managed without surgery with no clinically significant differences in outcomes compared to surgical treatment. Specific fracture characteristics, such as absence of rotational deformity or coronal angulation and a shaft-condylar angle >15 degrees, were associated with successful nonoperative management.

yes
contexts: The range of injury severity that can be seen within the category of type II supracondylar humerus fractures (SCHFs (supracondylar humerus fractures)) raises the question whether some could be treated nonoperatively. However, the clinical difficulty in using this approach lies in determining which type II SCHFs (supracondylar humerus fractures) can be managed successfully without a surgical intervention.

We reviewed clinical and radiographic information on 259 pediatric type II SCHFs (supracondylar humerus fractures) that were enrolled in a prospective registry of elbow fractures. The characteristics of the patients who were treated without surgery were compared with those of patients who were treated surgically. Treatment outcomes, as assessed by the final clinical and radiographic alignment, range of motion of the elbow, and complications, were compared between the groups to define clinical and radiographic features that related to success or failure of nonoperative management.

During the course of treatment, 39 fractures were found to have unsatisfactory alignment with nonoperative management and were taken for surgery. Ultimately, 150 fractures (57.9%) were treated nonoperatively, and 109 fractures (42.1%) were treated surgically. At final follow-up, outcome measures of change in carrying angle, range of motion, and complications did not show clinically significant differences between treatment groups. Fractures without rotational deformity or coronal angulation and with a shaft-condylar angle of>15 degrees were more likely to be associated with successful nonsurgical treatment. A scoring system was developed using these features to stratify the severity of the injury. Patients with isolated extension deformity, but none of the other features, were more likely to complete successful nonoperative management.
