This difference was not statistically significant when accounting for other factors in a multivariate model (p>0.05). The same statistical trend was true when analyzing outcomes of only the more severe Winquist type III and IV fractures. Additionally, surgeon experience was not significantly predictive of post-operative version for either trauma or non-trauma surgeons (p>0.05 for both).
results.reference: This study suggests that some of the less severe pediatric type II SCHFs can be successfully treated without surgery if close follow-up is achieved. Fractures with initial rotational deformity, coronal malalignment, and significant extension of the distal fragment are likely to fail a nonoperative approach. An algorithm using the initial radiographic characteristics can aid in distinguishing groups.

results.question: The promise of specialty pharmaceuticals: are they worth the price?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that specialty pharmaceuticals offer significant benefits such as increased life expectancy, improved quality of life, and reduced healthcare spending, but these come at a high cost and require complex management. While payers demand evidence of value and cost control is challenging, sophisticated pharmacoeconomic models can help manage these costs appropriately, suggesting that the benefits may justify the price.

yes
contexts: The promise of specialty pharmaceuticals: increased life expectancy, improved quality of life, enhanced workplace productivity, decreased burden of disease, and reduced health care spending comes at a significant cost. These agents require special handling, administration, patient education, clinical support, and risk mitigation. Additionally, specialty drugs require distribution systems that ensure appropriate patient selection and data collection. With the specialty pharmaceutical pipeline overflowing with new medicines and an aging population increasingly relying on these novel treatments to treat common diseases, the challenge of managing the costs associated with these agents can be daunting. Aided by sophisticated pharmacoeconomic models to assess value, the cost impacts of these specialty drugs can be appropriately controlled.

results.reference: Current evidence suggests that when used in targeted patient populations, specialty pharmaceuticals may represent a good health care value.

results.question: Does invasive diagnosis of nosocomial pneumonia during off-hours delay treatment?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that for ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), the time from bronchoalveolar lavage (an invasive diagnostic procedure) to antibiotic administration was actually shorter during off-hours compared to day shifts, due to faster specimen collection-to-antibiotic prescription times. contexts: Of the 152 VAP (ventilator-associated pneumonia) episodes 66 were diagnosed during off-hours. results.reference: An invasive strategy based on bronchoscopy to diagnose VAP was not associated with a longer time to first appropriate antibiotic administration when clinical suspicion of VAP occurs during off-hours.

results.question: Undescended testes: does age at orchiopexy affect survival of the testis?
results.answer:
The study found that testicular atrophy rates varied with age at orchiopexy, being highest in the 13-24 month group compared to younger or older groups. contexts: The optimal age at which to perform orchiopexy for cryptorchidism has long been debated. The aim of this study was to determine if age at orchiopexy affected testicular atrophy.

results.question: Do lipids, blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking confer equal risk of myocardial infarction in women as in men?
results.answer:

results.question: Does family practice at residency teaching sites reflect community practice?
results.answer:

results.question: Midwives' competence: is it affected by working in a rural location?
results.answer:
The evidence indicates that midwives' competence varies depending on whether they work in rural or urban locations, with rural midwives reporting higher competence in specific skills like breech delivery, while urban midwives report higher competence in other skills such as intravenous fluid replacement and newborn examinations. This suggests that working in a rural location does affect the type of competencies midwives feel confident in, reflecting differences in practice settings and training opportunities.

contexts: The response rate from midwives in rural settings was considerably higher (85%) than from midwives in the urban areas (60%). A key consideration is that midwives have the skills to competently and confidently provide maternity services in rural areas, which may be geographically isolated and where the midwife may only see a small number of pregnant women each year. Our objective was to compare the views of midwives in rural and urban settings, regarding their competence and confidence with respect to 'competencies' identified as being those which all professionals should have in order to provide effective and safe care for low-risk women.

results.reference: It is often assumed that midwives in rural areas where there are fewer deliveries, will be less competent and confident in their practice. Our exploratory study suggests that the issue of competence is far more complex and deserves further attention.

results.question: The effective orifice area/patient aortic annulus area ratio: a better way to compare different bioprostheses?
results.answer:
The study compared the effective orifice area (EOA) indexed to patient aortic annulus area between two bioprostheses and found no significant difference between them when using this ratio. This suggests that the EOA/patient aortic annulus area ratio is a useful method to adjust for patient anatomy and valve dimensions when comparing different bioprostheses.

contexts: Between August 2000 and September 2002, 139 patients underwent isolated aortic valve replacement (AVR (aortic valve replacement)) with the Mosaic (n = 67) or Perimount (n = 72) bioprosthesis. Upsizing (using a prosthesis larger in labeled valve size than the patient's measured internal aortic annulus diameter) was possible in 28.4% of Mosaic patients and 8.3% of Perimount patients. The postoperative mean systolic pressure gradient ranged from 10.5 to 22.2 mmHg in the Mosaic group, and from 9.4 to 12.6 mmHg in the Perimount group; it was significantly lower for 21 and 23 Perimount valves than for 21 and 23 Mosaic valves. The EOA (effective orifice area) ranged from 0.78 to 2.37 cm2 in Mosaic patients, and from 0.95 to 2.12 cm2 in Perimount patients. When indexing EOA (effective orifice area) by calculating the ratio of EOA (effective orifice area) to patient aortic annulus area to adjust for variables such as patient anatomy and valve dimensions, there was no significant difference between the two bioprostheses.

The aim of this prospective, randomized study was to compare the hemodynamic performance of the Medtronic Mosaic and Edwards Perimount bioprostheses in the aortic position, and to evaluate prosthesis-specific differences in valve sizing and valve-size labeling.

The progression rate of aortic valve obstruction was found to be dependent on the degree of valvar calcification ([VC] scoring 0 to III) and to be exponentially correlated with the aortic valve opening area (AVA (aortic valve opening area)) at initial catheterization. Neither age nor sex of the patient nor etiology of the valvar obstruction significantly influence the progression of aortic stenosis. If AVA (aortic valve opening area) decreases below 0.75 cm(2) with a present degree of VC = 0, or AVA (aortic valve opening area) of 0.8 with VC of I, AVA (aortic valve opening area) of 0.9 with VC of II, or AVA (aortic valve opening area) of 1.0 with VC of III, it is probable that aortic stenosis will have to be operated upon in the following years.

Of the 55 potential heart donors, 20 exhibited an FAC (fractional area change) of less than 50%. Forty hearts were harvested, 36 of which were successfully transplanted. Nine patients had an FAC (fractional area change) below 50% (group H2) and 27 had an FAC (fractional area change) over 50% (group H1). Four patients died: 2 from hemorrhage (FAC (fractional area change)>50% in donors); 1 from right and one from left ventricular dysfunction (FAC (fractional area change)<50% in donors). The FAC (fractional area change) increased significantly from 51 +/- 15% to 57 +/- 11% in 18 hearts that underwent TEE (transesophageal echocardiography) in donors and afterwards in recipients. Overall actuarial survival was 86.2% versus 64.6% at 1 and 2 years in group H1 and group H2, respectively (p = NS).
context_sections: BACKGROUND AND AIM OF THE STUDY
results.reference: Comparisons of absolute EOA values grouped by the manufacturers' valve sizes are misleading because of specific differences in geometric dimensions. The EOA:patient aortic annulus area ratio provides a new hemodynamic index which may facilitate objective comparisons between different valve types.

results.question: Evaluation of pediatric VCUG at an academic children's hospital: is the radiographic scout image necessary?
results.answer:
The study found that radiographic scout images did not provide any clinically significant or management-changing information during pediatric VCUG exams, despite contributing a measurable radiation dose. Therefore, the scout image does not appear necessary for the evaluation process at an academic children's hospital.

no
contexts: There is heterogeneity in how pediatric voiding cystourethrography (VCUG (voiding cystourethrography)) is performed. Some institutions, including our own, obtain a radiographic scout image prior to contrast agent instillation.

To demonstrate that the radiographic scout image does not augment VCUG (voiding cystourethrography) interpretation or contribute management-changing information but nonetheless carries a non-negligible effective dose.

We evaluated 181 children who underwent VCUG (voiding cystourethrography) in 2012, with an age breakdown of less than 1 year (56 children), 1-5 years (66 children), 6-10 years (43 children) and 11-18 years (16 children), with a mean age of 4.0 years. We investigated patient demographics, clinical indication for the examination, scout image findings and estimated effective radiation dose, as well as overall exam findings and impression.

No clinically significant or management-changing findings were present on scout images, and no radiopaque urinary tract calculi or concerning incidental finding was identified. Scout image estimated effective radiation dose averaged 0.09 mSv in children younger than 1 y, 0.09 mSv in children age 1-5, 0.13 mSv in children age 6-10 and 0.18 mSv in children age 11-18. Total fluoroscopy time per examination averaged 36.7 s (range 34.8-39.6 s for all age group averages). Evaluation of known or suspected vesicoureteral reflux (VUR (vesicoureteral reflux)) and urinary tract infection (UTI (urinary tract infection)) were the most common clinical indications, stated in 40.9% and 37.0% of exams, respectively.

The correlation between radiographic transition zone on contrast enema in Hirschsprung's disease and the total length of aganglionosis is known to be inaccurate. The aim of our study was to analyse this correlation more precisely to improve preoperative planning of the corrective surgery.
results.reference: Although the estimated effective dose is low for VCUG radiographic scout images, this step did not augment VCUG interpretation or contribute management-changing information. This step should be omitted or substituted to further reduce dose in pediatric VCUG.

results.question: Are endometrial polyps from pre-menopausal women similar to post-menopausal women?
results.answer:
The endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women show significant differences in the expression of hormone receptors and Ki67, indicating they are not similar in these aspects. However, both groups have similarly increased levels of Bcl-2. Overall, the differences in key markers suggest they are not similar.

no
contexts: Do endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women have similar immunohistochemical expression of oestrogen and progesterone receptors (ER (emergency room), PR) and markers of cellular proliferation/apoptosis (Ki67 and Bcl-2).
Fourteen pre-menopausal and 16 post-menopausal women who presented with abnormal bleeding with endometrial polyps.

Endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women had significant differences in their expression of hormone receptors and Ki67. However, polyps from both groups of women had similarly increased levels of Bcl-2, an inhibitor of apoptosis.
Polyps recruited from women attending an out-patient hysteroscopy clinic in a UK district general hospital.
Immunohistochemical staining was performed on endometrial polyps.
results.reference: Pre- and post-menopausal polyps exhibit differing hormone receptor and proliferation markers, presumably a result of their hormonal milieu. However, both groups appear to have lost the usual control mechanisms for apoptotic regulation, this appears to be responsible for their growth.

results.question: Does accompanying metabolic syndrome contribute to heart dimensions in hypertensive patients?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that hypertensive patients with metabolic syndrome have a significantly greater left atrial diameter compared to those without metabolic syndrome, and this diameter correlates with the number of metabolic syndrome criteria. Other heart dimensions were increased in hypertensive patients regardless of metabolic syndrome, but the presence of metabolic syndrome specifically contributed to changes in left atrial size.

yes
contexts: Metabolic syndrome (MetS (metabolic syndrome)) is associated with increased risk for cardiovascular events. We evaluated heart dimensions in hypertensive patients with MetS (metabolic syndrome).

Metabolic syndrome was present in 32 hypertensive patients (42.7%; 18 males, 14 females). The mean number of MetS (metabolic syndrome) criteria was 2.6+/-1.0 in the hypertensive group. Compared to the control group, patients with or without MetS (metabolic syndrome) exhibited significantly increased interventricular septum and posterior wall thickness, left atrial diameter, relative wall thickness, and left ventricular mass (p<0.05). The only significant difference between the two patient groups was that MetS (metabolic syndrome) was associated with a greater left atrial diameter (p=0.019). Left atrial diameter was correlated with the number of MetS (metabolic syndrome) criteria (r=0.51; p<0.001).

The study included 75 hypertensive patients (34 males, 41 females; mean age 51+/-9 years) without coronary artery disease. Patients were evaluated in two groups depending on the presence or absence of MetS (metabolic syndrome). Age- and gender-matched 20 healthy subjects (9 males, 11 females; mean age 50+/-5 years) comprised the control group. The diagnosis of MetS (metabolic syndrome) was based on the presence of at least three of five MetS (metabolic syndrome) criteria. Hypertension was defined as arterial blood pressure exceeding 140/85 mmHg on three consecutive measurements or the use of antihypertensive drugs. Echocardiographic measurements included interventricular septal thickness, left ventricular internal diameter, posterior wall thickness, aortic diameter, left atrial diameter, relative wall thickness, and left ventricular mass.
To determine whether anginal episodes might be related to extremes of hypotension in patients with ischaemic heart disease taking drugs to treat angina and heart failure.

Hypertension is one of the important contributing factors linked with both causation and development of kidney disease. It is a multifactorial, polygenic, and complex disorder due to interaction of several risk genes with environmental factors. The present study was aimed to explore genetic polymorphism in ACE-1 gene as a risk factor for CKD (chronic kidney disease) among hypertensive patients.
results.reference: Left ventricular dimensions are not influenced by MetS. Rather than MetS, hypertension is primarily responsible for changes in left ventricular dimensions. However, left atrial enlargement is more prominent in patients with MetS, suggesting that each MetS criterion contributes to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction.

results.question: The Prevalence of Incidentally Detected Idiopathic Misty Mesentery on Multidetector Computed Tomography: Can Obesity Be the Triggering Cause?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that among patients with incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on CT, a high proportion were classified as obese (67.5%) or overweight (17.5%). This suggests a possible association between obesity and the presence of idiopathic misty mesentery, implying that obesity could be a triggering factor.

yes
contexts: Misty mesentery appearance is commonly reported in daily practice, usually as a secondary finding of various pathological entities, but sometimes it is encountered as an isolated finding that cannot be attributed to any other disease entity. We aimed to assess the prevalence of cases with incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) and to summarize the pathologies leading to this appearance.

There were a total of 561 patients in whom misty mesentery appearance was depicted on abdominopelvic CT (computed tomography) scans. A total of 80 cases were found to have isolated incidental idiopathic misty mesentery, giving a prevalence of 7%. The common indication for CT (computed tomography) examination was abdominal pain. There was a slight female predominance (51.3%). 67.5% of all patients were classified as obese and 17.5% as overweight.

Medical records and initial and follow-up CT (computed tomography) features of patients with misty mesentery appearance between January 2011 and January 2013 were analysed. The study included cases with no known cause of misty mesentery according to associated CT (computed tomography) findings, clinical history, or biochemical manifestations, and excluded patients with diseases known to cause misty mesentery, lymph nodes greater than a short-axis diameter of 5 mm, discrete mesenteric masses, or bowel wall thickening.

To investigate the effect of obesity at the start of adolescence on the prevalence, incidence and maintenance of chest wheezing among individuals aged 11-15 years in a birth cohort in a developing country.

The aim of this study was to prospectively compare the diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)), multidetector computed tomography (MDCT (multidetector computed tomography)) and endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS (endoscopic ultrasonography)) in the preoperative locoregional staging of gastric cancer.
results.reference: The results of the present study show that idiopathic incidental misty mesentery appearance has a significant prevalence. Also, the high body mass index of these patients and the growing evidence of obesity-induced inflammatory changes in adipose tissue are suggestive of an association between obesity and misty mesentery appearance on CT.

results.question: Are pediatric concussion patients compliant with discharge instructions?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that standardized discharge instructions were given to pediatric concussion patients, and the involvement of a discharge coordinator improved the discharge planning process and reduced problems experienced by patients after discharge. This suggests that patients were generally compliant with discharge instructions, as improvements in outcomes imply adherence to the guidance provided.

yes
contexts: Concussions are commonly diagnosed in pediatric patients presenting to the emergency department (ED (emergency department)). The primary objective of this study was to evaluate compliance with ED (emergency department) discharge instructions for concussion management.

A prospective cohort study was conducted from November 2011 to November 2012 in a pediatric ED (emergency department) at a regional Level 1 trauma center, serving 35,000 pediatric patients per year. Subjects were aged 8 years to 17 years and were discharged from the ED (emergency department) with a diagnosis of concussion. Exclusion criteria included recent (past 3 months) diagnosis of head injury, hospital admission, intracranial injury, skull fracture, suspected nonaccidental trauma, or preexisting neurologic condition. Subjects were administered a baseline survey in the ED (emergency department) and were given standardized discharge instructions for concussion by the treating physician. Telephone follow-up surveys were conducted at 2 weeks and 4 weeks after ED (emergency department) visit.

The discharge coordinator resulted in an improved discharge planning process, and there was a reduction in problems experienced by patients after discharge, and in perceived need for medical and healthcare services. There was no evidence that the discharge coordinator resulted in a more timely or effective provision of community services after discharge, or that the appropriateness or efficiency of bed use was improved.
To examine the attitudes of players and coaches to the use of protective headgear, particularly with respect to the prevention of concussion.

To characterize the use and delivery of cough and cold medicines in children younger than 6 presenting to an inner-city pediatric emergency department (PED (pediatric emergency department)) following 2007 FDA (Food and Drug Administration) warnings.
results.reference: Pediatric patients discharged from the ED are mostly compliant with concussion instructions. However, a significant number of patients RTP on the day of injury, while experiencing symptoms or without medical clearance.

results.question: Is the zeolite hemostatic agent beneficial in reducing blood loss during arterial injury?
results.answer:
The studies involving swine models show that application of the zeolite hemostatic agent (QuikClot - Advanced Clotting Sponge) led to decreased total blood loss and a slower drop in blood pressure after arterial injury. Additionally, the QC group had higher hematocrit levels and better physiological parameters compared to controls, indicating a beneficial effect in reducing blood loss.

yes
contexts: Uncontrolled hemorrhage is the leading cause of fatality. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of zeolite mineral (QuikClot - Advanced Clotting Sponge [QC-ACS]) on blood loss and physiological variables in a swine extremity arterial injury model.

Arterial catheters are routinely used to sample blood for clotting studies in most cardiothoracic intensive care units. The clotting profile in surgical bleeding after cardiac surgery influences further management. Aspiration and discard of a certain amount of blood from the line, prior to sampling, are assumed to clear heparin contamination. We have investigated this assumption through analysis of the clotting profile by simultaneous arterial line and peripheral venous samples.

Sixteen swine were used. Oblique groin incision was created and a 5 mm incision was made. The animals were allocated to: control group (n: 6): Pressure dressing was applied with manual pressure over gauze sponge; or QC group (n: 10): QC was directly applied over lacerated femoral artery. Mean arterial pressure, blood loss and physiological parameters were measured during the study period.

Application of QC led to a slower drop in blood pressure. The control group had a significantly higher increase in lactate within 60 minutes. The mean prothrombin time in the control group was significantly increased at 60 minutes. The application of QC led to decreased total blood loss. The QC group had significantly higher hematocrit levels. QC application generated a significant heat production. There were mild edematous and vacuolar changes in nerve samples.

Use of the modified lithotomy position was not associated with any demonstrable decrease in lower limb perfusion. The addition of 15 degrees head-down tilt, however, during pelvic dissection, led to an immediate and significant drop in lower limb perfusion (P<0.05; Mann-Whitney U test). The subgroup of patients analyzed postoperatively showed a ten-fold increase (P<0.01) in perfusion that was confined to the muscle compartment with no demonstrable increase in skin perfusion or intra-arterial pedal blood pressure.
results.reference: According to the physiological parameters, we observed that zeolite tends to reduce blood loss, however could not stop bleeding completely. We believe that further clinical trials are needed to conclude that zeolite could be used in the routine practice.

results.question: Treatment as prevention in resource-limited settings: is it feasible to maintain HIV viral load suppression over time?
results.answer:
The study reports that among patients on long-term HAART in a resource-limited setting, 87.3% had undetectable viral loads, with many maintaining viral suppression over a median of 14 years. Although some patients experienced virologic failure, the majority were able to sustain viral load suppression, indicating that treatment as prevention is feasible in such settings.

yes
contexts: Recently, there has been increasing interest in the role of "treatment as prevention" (TasP (the role of "treatment as prevention")). Some of the questions regarding TasP (the role of "treatment as prevention") strategies arise from the perceived difficulties in achieving and maintaining viral load (VL (viral load)) suppression over time and the risk of emergence of viral resistance that could compromise future treatment options. This study was conducted to assess these questions in a resource-limited setting.
To evaluate whether reported unsafe sexual behaviour among HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)- infected individuals is changing over time.

Of 619 patients on follow-up, 82 (13.2%) were diagnosed in the pre-HAART era. At the time of our study, 79 (96.3%) patients were on HAART, with a median duration of 14 years (IQR 12-15) of therapy, and exposure to mono or dual nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors regimens in 47.8% of cases. Sixty-nine patients (87.3%) had undetectable VL (viral load), 37 (46.8%) never presented virologic failure, and 19 (24.1%) experienced only one failure. Thirteen patients (16.5%) were receiving third-line ART (assisted reproductive technology) regimens, with an average of 2.7-fold more virologic failures than those on first- or second-line regimens (p = 0.007).

The number of new diagnoses of HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) infection is rising in the northwestern hemisphere and it is becoming increasingly important to understand the mechanisms behind this trend.

At least one sexual behaviour questionnaire was obtained for 6545 HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-infected individuals and the median number of questionnaires completed per individual was five. There was no evidence of an increase in reported unsafe sex over time in this population [odds ratio (OR (odds ratio)), 1.0; 95% confidence interval (CI (confidence interval)), 0.96-1.05]. Females (OR (odds ratio), 1.38; 95% CI (confidence interval), 1.19-1.60), 15-30 year olds (OR (odds ratio), 1.26; 95% CI (confidence interval), 1.09-1.47), those with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-positive partners (OR (odds ratio), 12.58; 95% CI (confidence interval), 10.84-14.07) and those with occasional partners (OR (odds ratio), 3.25; 95% CI (confidence interval), 2.87-3.67) were more likely to report unsafe sex. There was no evidence of a response bias over time, but individuals were less willing to leave questions about their sexual behaviour unanswered or ambiguous (OR (odds ratio), 0.93; 95% CI (confidence interval), 0.90-0.97).
results.reference: Maintaining viral load suppression over time in resource-limited-settings is feasible.

results.question: Are octogenarians at high risk for carotid endarterectomy?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that carotid endarterectomy has been proven safe and effective in patients younger than 80, but octogenarians (patients aged 80-89) are considered high-risk for carotid artery stenting, implying a higher risk category. However, a study of 95 octogenarians undergoing carotid endarterectomy showed low perioperative neurologic complications and no deaths, suggesting that while octogenarians may be high-risk, carotid endarterectomy can still be performed safely in this group. Overall, octogenarians are considered high-risk patients for carotid interventions.

yes
contexts: Several prospective randomized trials have proved carotid endarterectomy to be safe and effective for both symptomatic and asymptomatic patients younger than 80 years of age. Recently, carotid artery stenting (CAS (carotid artery stenting)) has been approved for use in selected high-risk patients. It has been proposed that being an octogenarian places patients in this high-risk category.

A total of 103 carotid endarterectomies were performed in 95 octogenarians. Procedures were performed on 59 men and 36 women. Indications for operation included symptomatic carotid stenosis in 44 patients (43%) and asymptomatic carotid stenosis in 59 (57%). Associated risk factors included diabetes mellitus (17%), hypertension (76%), coronary artery disease (28%), hyperlipidemia (39%), and history of smoking (42%). There were 4 perioperative neurologic complications, which included 1 transient ischemic attack (0.97%), 2 minor strokes (1.94%), and 1 major stroke (0.97%). There were no deaths.

All patients between the ages of 80 to 89 years undergoing carotid endarterectomy during a 12-year period were included in the study. Information included indications for carotid endarterectomy, associated risk factors, length of stay, and hospital course. Perioperative morbidity and mortality, including neurologic events and myocardial infarction, were recorded.

Overall, 205 consecutive patients underwent preoperative carotid screening. The prevalence of significant carotid stenosis was 5.8%. Univariate analysis confirmed that PVD (P=0.005), carotid bruit (P=0.003) and diabetes mellitus (P=0.05) were significant risk factors for stenosis. Carotid stenosis was a risk factor for stroke (P=0.03). Prevalence of carotid stenosis was higher in the high-risk group (9.1%) than the low-risk group (1.2%) (P<0.05). All concomitant or staged carotid endarterectomies/CAB (5/205) and all patients who had perioperative strokes (5/205) were in the high-risk group (P=0.01).

The case records of patients consecutively undergoing CAB (coronary artery bypass surgery) were reviewed. Patients were stratified retrospectively into high- or low-risk groups according to risk factors for significant carotid stenosis and perioperative stroke: peripheral vascular disease (PVD (peripheral vascular disease)), carotid bruit, diabetes mellitus, age>70 years and/or history of cerebrovascular disease. Prevalence of carotid stenosis detected by ultrasonography, surgical management and perioperative stroke rates were determined in each group.
results.reference: Combined end points for adverse events are acceptable in the octogenarian. Carotid endarterectomy remains the gold standard for treatment of extracranial carotid disease in all age groups. Age alone should not place patients in the high-risk category for carotid endarterectomy.

results.question: Has the mammography quality standards act affected the mammography quality in North Carolina?
results.answer:
The data from inspections before and after the implementation of the Mammography Quality Standards Act (MQSA) in North Carolina show a clear improvement in mammography quality measures, such as phantom scores, darkroom fog, and temperature difference passing rates. This indicates that the MQSA positively affected mammography quality in the state.

yes
contexts: The United States Food and Drug Administration implemented federal regulations governing mammography under the Mammography Quality Standards Act (MQSA (mammography quality standards act)) of 1992. During 1995, its first year in implementation, we examined the impact of the MQSA (mammography quality standards act) on the quality of mammography in North Carolina.

All mammography facilities were inspected during 1993-1994, and again in 1995. Both inspections evaluated mean glandular radiation dose, phantom image evaluation, darkroom fog, and developer temperature. Two mammography health specialists employed by the North Carolina Division of Radiation Protection performed all inspections and collected and codified data.

Telephone counseling and tailored print communications have emerged as promising methods for promoting mammography screening. However, there has been little research testing, within the same randomized field trial, of the efficacy of these two methods compared to a high-quality usual care system for enhancing screening. This study addressed the question: Compared to usual care, is tailored telephone counseling more effective than tailored print materials for promoting mammography screening?

The percentage of facilities that met quality standards increased from the first inspection to the second inspection. Phantom scores passing rate was 31.6% versus 78.2%; darkroom fog passing rate was 74.3% versus 88.5%; and temperature difference passing rate was 62.4% versus 86.9%.

The identification of the most suspect enhancing part of a lesion is regarded as a major diagnostic criterion in dynamic magnetic resonance mammography. Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD (computer-aided diagnosis)) software allows the semi-automatic analysis of the kinetic characteristics of complete enhancing lesions, providing additional information about lesion vasculature. The diagnostic value of this information has not yet been quantified.
results.reference: In 1995, the first year that the MQSA was in effect, there was a significant improvement in the quality of mammography in North Carolina. This improvement probably resulted from facilities' compliance with federal regulations.

results.question: Do hospitals provide lower quality care on weekends?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts do not directly address the quality of hospital care on weekends. Abstract [4] discusses differences in invasive lung-specimen collection-to-treatment times during different work shifts, including weekends, but does not provide information on the overall quality of care. Therefore, there is no evidence here to support or refute the claim that hospitals provide lower quality care on weekends.

no
contexts: Health care delivery has undertaken a major shift from inpatient management to ambulatory surgical care with increasing emphasis on quality assurance (QA (quality assurance)) processes. Educational opportunities for medical undergraduate programmes are being sought in the day surgery environment. Our study was undertaken to explore ways in which senior medical students can actively contribute to QA (quality assurance) processes as part of an undergraduate day surgery educational programme.

Health care delivery has undertaken a major shift from inpatient management to ambulatory surgical care with increasing emphasis on quality assurance (QA (quality assurance)) processes. Educational opportunities for medical undergraduate programmes are being sought in the day surgery environment. Our study was undertaken to explore ways in which senior medical students can actively contribute to the QA (quality assurance) processes as part of an undergraduate day surgery educational programme.

Swedish hospital mergers seem to stem from a conviction among policy makers that bigger hospitals lead to lower average costs and improved clinical outcomes. The effects of mergers in the form of multisited hospitals have not been systematically evaluated. The purpose of this article is to contribute to this area of knowledge by exploring responses to the merger of Blekinge Hospital.

We examined whether invasive lung-specimen collection-to-treatment times for intensive care unit patients with suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP (ventilator-associated pneumonia)) differ with to the work shift during which specimens were collected. We compared weekday day shifts and off-hours (from 6:30 p.m. to 8:29 a.m. the next day for night shifts, from Saturday 1:00 p.m. to Monday 8:29 a.m. for weekends, and from 8:30 a.m. to 8:29 a.m. the following morning for public holidays).

Governments are urged to determine methods to control the use of medical resources and curb the rise of healthcare costs. The question is, do health behaviors have an impact on the use of medical resources? This study aims to identify and understand the difference in the number of outpatient visits and health examinations based on various health behaviors and to determine whether patients seek medical care for illness from the same physicians.
results.reference: Weekend hospitalization leads to delayed provision of intensive procedures and elevated 1-year mortality for elderly AMI patients. The existence of measurable differences in treatments raises questions regarding the efficacy of a single input regulation (e.g., mandated nurse staffing ratios) in enhancing the quality of weekend care. My results suggest that targeted financial incentives might be a more cost-effective policy response than broad regulation aimed at improving quality.

results.question: Screening History Among Women with Invasive Cervical Cancer in an Academic Medical Center: Will We Miss Cancers Following Updated Guidelines?
results.answer:
The data show that among women younger than 30 with invasive cervical cancer, the time from a normal Pap test to diagnosis was significantly shorter than in older women, suggesting that less frequent screening as per updated guidelines might delay detection in this group. This implies that following the updated guidelines could lead to missed or delayed cancer diagnoses in younger women.

yes
contexts: Updated guidelines for the screening and management of cervical cancer in the United States recommend starting Papanicolaou (Pap) testing at age 21 and screening less frequently with less aggressive management for abnormalities. We sought to examine updated Pap test screening guidelines and how they may affect the detection of invasive cervical cancer, especially among women<30 years of age.

Patients diagnosed at Brigham and Women's Hospital with invasive cervical cancer between 2002 and 2012 were retrospectively identified. Prior screening history was obtained and patients were divided into two groups based on age<30 years or age ≥30 years. The two groups were then compared with respect to demographics, pathological findings, and time to diagnosis.

A total of 288 patients with invasive cervical carcinoma were identified. Among these patients, 109 had adequate information on prior screening history. Invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC (invasive adenocarcinoma)) was diagnosed in 37 (33.94%) patients, whereas 64 (58.72%) patients were diagnosed with invasive squamous cell carcinoma (ISCC (invasive squamous cell carcinoma)). The remaining eight patients were diagnosed with other types of cancers of the cervix. A total of 13 patients were younger than 30 while 96 patients were 30 or older. The mean time from normal Pap to diagnosis of IAC (invasive adenocarcinoma) was 15 months in patients younger than 30 years of age compared to 56 months in patients aged 30 and older (p < 0.001). The mean time from normal Pap to diagnosis of ISCC (invasive squamous cell carcinoma) was 38 months in patients younger than 30 years of age and 82 months in patients aged 30 and older (p = 0.018).

The records of 282 consecutive women with recurrent endometrial cancer treated from 1986 to 2005 were retrospectively collected in 8 Italian institutions. Primary disease, clinical history, and recurrence features and data were analyzed.

Coverage for breast cancer screening was 10.5% in South Africa, 19.3% in China, 33.8% in Russia and 43% in Mexico, and coverage for cervical cancer screening was 24% in South Africa, 27.2% in China, 63.7% in Mexico and 81.5% in Russia. Economic inequalities in screening participation were substantially lower or non-existent in countries with higher aggregate coverage, for both breast cancer screening (RII (relative index of inequality): 14.57 in South Africa, 4.90 in China, 2.01 in Mexico, 1.04 in Russia) and cervical cancer screening (RII (relative index of inequality): 3.60 in China, 2.47 in South Africa, 1.39 in Mexico, 1.12 in Russia).
results.reference: In this small retrospective study, updated Pap test screening guidelines would not have missed invasive cancer on average among screened women age 30 and older. However, young patients aged 21-29 years may be at increased risk of developing IAC of the cervix between the recommended screening intervals.

results.question: Oral mucocele/ranula: Another human immunodeficiency virus-related salivary gland disease?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate a strong association between oral mucoceles/ranulas and HIV infection, with a significant proportion of HIV-positive patients presenting with ranulas, especially plunging ranulas. This suggests that oral mucocele/ranula can be considered another HIV-related salivary gland disease.

yes
contexts: To describe clinical characteristics of oral mucoceles/ranulas, with a focus on human immunodeficiency virus (HIV (human immunodeficiency virus))-related salivary gland diseases.

There were 30 (26.5%) males and 83 (73.5%) females. Most patients were below 30 years of age, with the peak frequency in the first and second decade. Ranula (simple and plunging) represented 84.1% of the mucocele locations. Mucocele on the lips represented 10.6%. Seventy-two (63.7%) patients were HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) positive; and 97.2% of them had ranulas. Thirty-eight (33.6%) patients presented with plunging ranulas; and 92.1% of them were HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) positive, compared with two patients presenting with plunging ranulas in the HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-negative group. These results strongly suggest that an HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-positive patient is statistically (P<0.001) more at risk of presenting with not only a simple, but also a plunging ranula type.

We reviewed 113 referred cases of oral mucocele. The following anatomical sites were identified: lip, tongue, and floor of the mouth (simple ranulas), as well as plunging ranulas. The age and gender data of the patients with oral mucoceles were recorded. The HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) status of the patients and other information were reviewed.

In 136 patients, a primary parotid gland tumor was confirmed by histology. Among the observers, a high correlation was calculated (0.98). ADC values of pleomorphic adenomas were significantly higher than those of all other entities, except for myoepithelial adenomas (P = .054). ADC values of Warthin tumors were different from those of myoepithelial adenomas, lipomas, and salivary duct carcinomas (P<.001, 0.013, and .037, respectively). Mucoepidermoid carcinomas, acinic cell carcinomas, and basal cell adenocarcinomas were not differentiable from Warthin tumors (P = .094, .396, and .604, respectively).

A cross sectional study was carried out on sputa of patients diagnosed with tuberculosis. Sputa were tested for antibodies to HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) using OraQuick® HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-1/2 Assay (OraSure Technologies, Inc., Bethlehem, PA, USA). The results were compared with results of serum ELISA.
results.reference: This study presents a different clinical picture of oral mucoceles/ranulas, as observed in HIV-positive patients. Additionally, it suggests a possible clinical link between the two pathologies. The authors strongly support the suggestion that oral mucocele/ranula is an HIV-related salivary gland disease.

results.question: Is there an increase in the incidence of gbs carrier rates among pregnant women in northern Israel?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts report a 16% GBS colonization rate among parturients in the western Galilee, northern Israel, but do not provide previous data or trends over time to compare whether this represents an increase. Without historical prevalence data, it is not possible to determine if there has been an increase in GBS carrier rates.

no
contexts: Group B Streptococci (GBS (group b streptococci)) asymptomatically colonize the vaginal or rectal areas of about 20% of pregnant women (4-40%). About 50% of infants to mothers with GBS (group b streptococci) colonization also become colonized at rectal, umbilical or oral sites. GBS (group b streptococci) is a leading bacterial cause of neonatal illness and death. The present prevalence rate of GBS (group b streptococci) carriers among parturients in the western Galilee in Israel is unknown.AIM: A prospective study of the GBS (group b streptococci) carrier rate according to origin and gestational age in the western Galilee in Israel.

Sixteen percent of the parturients were found to be GBS (group b streptococci) colonized. The prevalence of GBS (group b streptococci) was 13.7% in Jewish women and 19% in Arab women, P=0.038. The women were also divided into two groups according to the gestational age one group included 414 women in 24-37 weeks gestation, and the other group included 286 women in term pregnancy. No difference was found in the rate of GBS (group b streptococci) carriers between the two gestational age groups.
A prospective study including 700 pregnant women. All women were screened for carriage of GBS (group b streptococci) by vaginal and rectal cultures.

Fifteen patients were included in the analysis as they became pregnant after ICSI procedure. Four of 47 selected genes were excluded from the analysis. Of the 43 genes analyzed, only 6 genes (VEGFA, PLA2G2A, ALPL, LIF, NNMT and STC1) showed a statistically uniform expression among patients who subsequently became pregnant. For all the other genes analyzed there were considerable differences in their expression levels amongst women who subsequently became pregnant.

Resistance rates for ofloxacin were calculated for all cases of uncomplicated UTI (urinary tract infection) diagnosed during the first 5 months of 2005 in a managed care organization (MCO (managed care organization)) in Israel, in community-dwelling women aged 41-75 years. The women were without risk factors for fluoroquinolone resistance. Uncomplicated UTI (urinary tract infection) was diagnosed with a urine culture positive for E. coli. The data set was stratified for age, using 5 year intervals, and stratum-specific resistance rates (% and 95% CI (confidence interval)) were calculated. These data were analyzed to identify age groups in which resistance rates have surpassed 10%.
results.reference: In the present study we found a significant increase in the incidence of GBS colonization in pregnant women in northern Israel. We also found an increased rate of GBS carriers in Arab women relative to Jewish women.

results.question: Does a dedicated discharge coordinator improve the quality of hospital discharge?
results.answer:
The introduction of a discharge coordinator improved the discharge planning process and reduced problems experienced by patients after discharge, indicating an improvement in the quality of hospital discharge. However, there was no evidence that it led to more timely or effective provision of community services or improved bed use efficiency. Overall, the quality of discharge planning was enhanced.

yes
contexts: The discharge coordinator resulted in an improved discharge planning process, and there was a reduction in problems experienced by patients after discharge, and in perceived need for medical and healthcare services. There was no evidence that the discharge coordinator resulted in a more timely or effective provision of community services after discharge, or that the appropriateness or efficiency of bed use was improved.

An intervention study in which the quality of discharge planning was assessed before and after the introduction of a discharge coordinator. Patients were interviewed on the ward before discharge and seven to 10 days after being discharged home.
To evaluate the effectiveness of the role of a discharge coordinator whose sole responsibility was to plan and coordinate the discharge of patients from medical wards.

Phase I comprised base line data collection; in phase II data were collected after the introduction of the district discharge planning policy and a discharge form (checklist) for all patients; in phase III data were collected after the introduction of the discharge coordinator.

The quality and out come of discharge planning. Readmission rates, duration of stay, appropriateness of days of care, patients' health and satisfaction, problems after discharge, and receipt of services.
results.reference: The introduction of a discharge coordinator improved the quality of discharge planning, but at additional cost.

results.question: Can dobutamine stress echocardiography induce cardiac troponin elevation?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that in a study of 57 patients undergoing dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), none showed elevated cardiac troponin I (cTnI) 18-24 hours after the test, even among those with ischemia detected by DSE. This suggests that DSE does not induce cardiac troponin elevation.

no
contexts: Elevation of cardiac troponin (cTn) is considered specific for myocardial damage. Elevated cTn and echocardiogrpahic documentation of wall motion abnormalities (WMAs (wall motion abnormalities)) that were recorded after extreme physical effort raise the question whether dobutamine stress echo (DSE (dobutamine stress echo)), can also induce elevation of troponin.

Fifty-seven consecutive patients were included. The average age was 64.4 ± 10.7, 73% of the patients were males, and nearly half of the patients were known to have ischemic heart disease. Two of the patients were excluded due to technical difficulty. No signs of ischemia were recorded in 25 (45.4%). Among the patients with established ischemia on DSE (dobutamine stress echo), 12 (22%) had mild ischemia, 13 (23.6%) had moderate and 5 (9%) had severe ischemia. Angiography was performed in 13 (26%) of the patients, of which 7 had PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) and one was referred to bypass surgery. None of the patients had elevated cTnI 18-24 hours after the DSE (dobutamine stress echo).

we prospective enrolled stable patients (age>18 years) referred to DSE (dobutamine stress echo). The exam was performed under standardized conditions. Blood samples for cTnI were obtained at baseline and 18-24 hours after the test. We aimed to compare between the clinical and echocardiographic features of patients with elevated cTnI and those without cTnI elevations.

Myocardial damage that is associated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention)) partially affects the results of the procedure, and is related to medium-term cardiovascular death. Remote postischemic conditioning might reduce the myocardial lesions that are associated with PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention), but perhaps less so in diabetics. The aim of this study was to evaluate the protective effect of remote postischemic conditioning in patients undergoing elective PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) for stable angina or non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome with troponin<1 ng/ml at the time of randomization.

In 14 healthy pigs, blood flow was measured in the ascending aorta, left anterior descending (LAD (left anterior descending)), circumflex (Cx), right coronary artery (RCA (right coronary artery)), right common carotid artery (RCCA (right common carotid artery)), and left internal mammary artery (LIMA (left internal mammary artery)), along with left-and right-ventricular pressures (LVP and RVP), aortic pressure (AoP (aortic pressure)), and pulmonary artery pressure (PAP (pulmonary artery pressure)). Cardiac Troponin (cTn), interleukin 6 and 10 (IL (interleukin)-6 and IL (interleukin)-10), and tumor necrosis factor A (TNF (tumor necrosis factor)-A) were measured in coronary sinus blood samples. The experimental (IR (ischemia-reperfusion)) group (n=10) underwent 60 min of lung ischemia followed by 60 min of reperfusion by clamping and releasing the left pulmonary hilum. Simultaneous measurements of all parameters were made at baseline and during IR (ischemia-reperfusion). The control group (n=4) had similar measurements without lung IR (ischemia-reperfusion).
results.reference: Our results indicate that there is no elevation of cTn despite the occurrence of significant WMAs on DSE. We conclude that cTnI cannot be used as an additional diagnostic tool during pharmacological stress test performed to evaluate the presence and severity of ischemia.

results.question: Cigarettes and cinema: does parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing reduce adolescent smoking susceptibility?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts show a strong negative correlation between parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing and adolescent smoking susceptibility, with higher odds of smoking susceptibility among those with partial or no restrictions compared to full restriction. This suggests that parental restriction of R-rated movies is associated with reduced smoking susceptibility in adolescents.

yes
contexts: To examine the relationship between exposure to pro-smoking messages in media and susceptibility to smoking adoption among middle school students. The hypothesis that parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing is associated with lower adolescent smoking susceptibility was tested.

An index of smoking susceptibility was created using measures of cigarette use and future intention to smoke. A zero-order correlation for parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing and smoking susceptibility showed a strong association (r = -.36, p<.001). A hierarchical logistic regression yielded odds ratios (ORs (odds ratios)) for being susceptible to or having tried smoking for three levels of parental R-rated movie restriction. Results show that compared to full restriction, respondents with partial or no restriction were more likely to be susceptible to smoking (partial restriction: OR = 2.1, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.5-2.8; no restriction: OR = 3.3, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 2.3-4.6), when controlling for demographic factors, and family and friend smoking. Analyses using a measure of smoking prevalence as the dependent variable yielded similar results (partial restriction: OR = 1.5, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.0-2.2; no restriction: OR = 2.5, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.7-3.7).

A sample of 1687 6th-, 7th-, and 8th-grade students from four Wisconsin middle schools were surveyed about their use of cigarettes, exposure to smoking in media, their views of smoking, and peer smoking behaviors.
To explore the extent to which parent-adolescent emotional closeness, family conflict, and parental permissiveness moderate the association of puberty and alcohol use in adolescents (aged 10-14).

Cross-sectional survey of 7631 adolescents from 231 Australian schools. Measures included pubertal status, recent (30day) alcohol use, parent-adolescent emotional closeness, family conflict, parental permissiveness of alcohol use and peer alcohol use. The analysis was based on a two-level (individuals nested within schools) logistic regression model, with main effects entered first, and interaction terms added second.
results.reference: Parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing is associated with both lower adolescent smoking susceptibility and lower smoking rates.

results.question: Are laboratories reporting serum quantitative hCG results correctly?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that there are errors in how laboratories report serum quantitative hCG results, specifically misreporting intact hCG as total beta hCG and vice versa. This suggests that laboratories are not consistently reporting hCG results correctly, which is clinically important for diagnosis and monitoring.

no
contexts: We identified errors in participant reporting of intact hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) results as total beta hCG (9.3%; 22 of 235 laboratories) and total beta hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) as intact hCG (13.1%; 8 of 61 laboratories).

Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin)) is a heterodimeric glycoprotein hormone that exists in multiple forms. Immunoassays commonly used in clinical laboratories measure intact hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin), total beta hCG (intact hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) + hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) free beta-subunit), and/or hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) free beta-subunit. Measurement of serum concentrations of hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) is useful for confirmation and monitoring of pregnancy, diagnosis of trophoblastic diseases and monitoring of the efficacy of treatment, and prenatal screening. Correctly reporting results for the various forms of hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) is clinically important.

We prepared samples by addition of intact hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) and hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) free beta-subunit to an essentially hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin)-free human serum matrix. The samples were analyzed by participant laboratories using various immunoassay methods.

As part of an MRC funded study into primary care oral anticoagulation management, INR (international normalized ratio) measurements obtained in general practice were validated against values on the same samples obtained in hospital laboratories. A prospective comparative trial was undertaken between three hospital laboratories and nine general practices. All patients attending general practice based anticoagulant clinics had parallel INR (international normalized ratio) estimations performed in general practice and in a hospital laboratory.

405 tests were performed. Comparison between results obtained in the practices and those in the reference hospital laboratory (gold standard), which used the same method of testing for INR (international normalized ratio), showed a correlation coefficient of 0.96. Correlation coefficients comparing the results with the various standard laboratory techniques ranged from 0.86 to 0.92. It was estimated that up to 53% of tests would have resulted in clinically significant differences (change in warfarin dose) depending upon the site and method of testing. The practice derived results showed a positive bias ranging from 0.28 to 1.55, depending upon the site and method of testing.
results.reference: Many factors contribute to the erroneous reporting of hCG results, including (a) the complexity of hCG molecule and confusion of nomenclature on the various forms of hCG; (b) laboratory personnel's lack of awareness of the distinctions of the forms of hCG and failure to recognize the specificity of assays for their measurement; (c) lack of clarity and uniformity in manufacturers' reagent labeling; and (d) most product inserts' lack of information on the specificity of each method to the various forms of hCG.

results.question: Steroids in aminoglycoside-containing ear drops: do they reduce cochlear toxicity?
results.answer:
The hypothesis in abstract [1] is to determine whether betamethasone reduces cochlear toxicity of gentamicin when given together. Abstract [3] describes a study where mice received intratympanic injections of betamethasone, gentamicin, or both, with auditory brainstem response thresholds assessed over time, implying investigation into cochlear toxicity. Although the results are not explicitly detailed in the provided excerpts, the study design suggests that the combination was tested for protective effects. No contradictory evidence is presented.

yes
contexts: To determine whether betamethasone (BM (betamethasone)) reduces the cochlear toxicity of otic gentamicin (GM (gentamicin)) if given together.

It is postulated that some aspects of methotrexate toxicity may be related to its action as an anti-folate. Folic acid (FA (folic acid)) is often given as an adjunct to methotrexate therapy, but there is no conclusive proof that it decreases the toxicity of methotrexate and there is a theoretical risk that it may decrease the efficacy of methotrexate.

Thirty-four mice were assigned at random to receive intratympanic injections of either 0.1 % BM (11 mice), 0.3% GM (13 mice), or a combination of both (GM (gentamicin)/BM (betamethasone)) with benzalkonium chloride (10 mice) in the left ear (treated) and saline on the right (untreated). Six injections were given on alternate days. Auditory brainstem response thresholds were assessed at 1 month, 2 months, and>2 months.

In the whole group only a slight difference was found between both training modalities concerning their writing abilities. However, children with a history of hearing loss, actual hearing loss or pathologic middle ear findings profited most from the specialized training program compared to the control in their reading abilities.

The subjects were seven healthy humans. The right ear was stimulated using ice-water. Each subject was kept in a left-ear-down position for 20 s and then repositioned to a prone position, a right-ear-down position and a supine position with 20 s intervals. Nystagmus was analysed using three-dimensional video-oculography.
results.reference: Our data suggest that hearing loss caused by GM otic drops may be reduced by the inclusion of BM and benzalkonium chloride. Our finding that BM alone was associated with hearing loss suggests that the benzalkonium chloride may be the protective agent in combination otic drops.

results.question: Does having a regular primary care clinician improve quality of preventive care for young children?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that having a regular clinician for preventive care is associated with slightly higher interpersonal quality ratings and slightly greater content of anticipatory guidance for young children. Multivariate analyses show that interpersonal quality is higher for children with a regular clinician, although anticipatory guidance content is not significantly different after controlling for other factors. Overall, this suggests an improvement in quality of preventive care with a regular primary care clinician.

yes
contexts: This study examines whether having a regular clinician for preventive care is associated with quality of care for young children, as measured by interpersonal quality ratings and content of anticipatory guidance.

In bivariate analysis, parents of children with a regular clinician for preventive care reported slightly higher interpersonal quality (69 vs. 65 on a 0-100 scale, P = 0.01). Content of anticipatory guidance received was slightly greater for children with a regular clinician (82 vs. 80 on a 0-100 scale, P = 0.03). In bivariate analysis, a regular clinician was associated with interpersonal quality only among African American and Hispanic children. In multivariate analyses, controlling for factors that could independently influence self-reports of experiences with care, interpersonal quality but not anticipatory guidance content was higher for children with a regular clinician.

Bivariate and multivariate analyses evaluate associations between having a regular clinician for well child care and interpersonal quality, the content of anticipatory guidance, and timely access to care.

(1) To examine the effects of managed care on the likelihood of low-income persons having a usual source of care and a usual physician, and; (2) To examine the association between usual source of care and access.

Electronic health records have the potential to facilitate family history use by primary care physicians (PCPs (primary care physicians)) to provide personalized care. The objective of this study was to determine whether automated, at-the-visit tailored prompts about family history risk change PCP (primary care physician) behavior.
results.reference: Having a regular primary care clinician is embraced in pediatrics, although team care among physicians is also widely practiced. For young children, having a regular clinician is associated with modest gains in interpersonal quality and no differences in content of anticipatory guidance. The benefit of having a regular clinician may primarily occur in interpersonal quality for subgroups of young children.

results.question: Does performance in selection processes predict performance as a dental student?
results.answer:
The evidence is mixed. Abstract [1] states that pre-admission academic average, UMAT scores, and interview performance did not predict dental student performance, while abstract [5] reports a statistically significant correlation between overall selection performance and examination performance. This suggests some predictive value of selection processes, but not consistently across all measures.

maybe
contexts: After controlling for variables, pre-admission academic average, UMAT (undergraduate medicine and health sciences admission test) scores and interview performance did not predict performance as a dental student. Class place in second year, however, was a strong predictor of class place in final year. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that the best predictors of higher class placement in the final year were New Zealand European ethnicity and domestic (rather than international) student status. Other socio-demographic characteristics were not associated with performance. These interim findings provide a sound base for the ongoing study.

This study investigated associations between the performance of dental students in each of the three components of the selection procedure [academic average, Undergraduate Medicine and Health Sciences Admission Test (UMAT (undergraduate medicine and health sciences admission test)) and structured interview], socio-demographic characteristics and their academic success in an undergraduate dental surgery programme.

Do preresidency selection factors serve as predictors of success in residency? Specifically, we asked which preresidency selection factors are associated or correlated with (1) objective measures of resident knowledge and performance; and (2) subjective ratings by faculty.

Longitudinal review of admissions data relating to students entering dental education at the University of Otago, New Zealand, between 2004 and 2009 was compared with academic performance throughout the dental programme.

The score for overall performance at selection achieved statistically significant correlation  with examination performance (r = 0.491 for the AKT (applied knowledge test) and r = 0.526 for the CSA (clinical skills assessment), P<0.01).
results.reference: The study found important socio-demographic differences in pre-admission test scores, but those scores did not predict performance in the dental programme, whether measured in second year or in final year.

results.question: Is it time to reconsider lobectomy in low-risk paediatric thyroid cancer?
results.answer:
The provided data indicate that a subset of children with well-differentiated thyroid cancer (WDTC) classified as 'very-low-risk' based on specific histopathological criteria had excellent outcomes with no recurrence after initial therapy, suggesting that less extensive surgery like lobectomy might be sufficient. Since current guidelines recommend total thyroidectomy for nearly all children but this study identifies a group that may do well with less aggressive treatment, it supports reconsidering lobectomy in low-risk pediatric thyroid cancer.

yes
contexts: Current guidelines recommend total thyroidectomy for nearly all children with well-differentiated thyroid cancer (WDTC (well-differentiated thyroid cancer)). These guidelines, however, derive from older data accrued prior to current high-resolution imaging. We speculate that there is a subpopulation of children who may be adequately treated with lobectomy.

We applied two different risk-stratification criteria to this population. First, we determined the number of patients meeting American Thyroid Association (ATA (american thyroid association)) 'low-risk' criteria, defined as disease grossly confined to the thyroid with either N0/Nx or incidental microscopic N1a disease. Second, we defined a set of 'very-low-risk' histopathological criteria, comprising unifocal tumours ≤4 cm without predefined high-risk factors, and determined the proportion of patients that met these criteria.

Twenty-seven (37%) males and 46 (63%) females were included in this study, with a mean age of 13·4 years. Ipsilateral- and contralateral multifocality were identified in 27 (37·0%) and 19 (26·0%) of specimens. Thirty-seven (51%) patients had lymph node metastasis (N1a = 18/N1b = 19). Pre-operative ultrasound identified all cases with clinically significant nodal disease. Of the 73 patients, 39 (53·4%) met ATA (american thyroid association) low-risk criteria and 16 (21·9%) met 'very-low-risk' criteria. All 'very-low-risk' patients demonstrated excellent response to initial therapy without persistence/recurrence after a mean follow-up of 36·4 months.
Seventy-three children with WDTC (well-differentiated thyroid cancer) treated between 2004 and 2015.
It remains controversial whether there is a gender difference in survival of patients with resected non-small cell lung cancer.
results.reference: Ultrasound and histopathology identify a substantial population that may be candidates for lobectomy, avoiding the risks and potential medical and psychosocial morbidity associated with total thyroidectomy. We propose a clinical framework to stimulate discussion of lobectomy as an option for low-risk patients.

results.question: Is an advance care planning model feasible in community palliative care?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that embedding an advance care planning model into community palliative care services is feasible. The studies describe successful implementation in Victorian community palliative care services, highlighting the importance of organizational adaptation and quality audit processes to integrate the model into routine practice.

yes
contexts: The services demonstrated that it was feasible to embed the Model into their organizational structures. Advance care planning conversations and involvement of family was an important outcome measure rather than completion rate of advance care planning documents in community settings. Services adapted and applied their own concept of community, which widened the impact of the model. Changes to quality audit processes were essential to consolidate the model into routine palliative care practice.

An effective advance care planning programme involves an organizational wide commitment and preparedness for health service reform to embed advance care planning into routine practice. Internationally, such programmes have been implemented predominantly in aged and acute care with more recent work in primary care.

A multi-site action research was conducted over a 16-month period in 2007-2009 with three Victorian community palliative care services. Using mixed method data collection strategies to assess feasibility, we conducted a baseline audit of staff and clients; analysed relevant documents (client records, policies, procedures and quality improvement strategies) pre-implementation and post-implementation and conducted key informant interviews (n = 9).
Three community palliative care services: one regional and two metropolitan services in Victoria, Australia.

Family medicine has aspired to train residents and conduct research in settings that closely resemble community practice. The purpose of this study was to compare the patient characteristics of the ambulatory teaching centers of a consortium of seven community-based university-affiliated family practice residency programs in northeast Ohio with the National Ambulatory Medical Care Survey (NAMCS (national ambulatory medical care survey)) results for family physicians (FPs (family physicians)) and general practitioners (GPs (general practitioners)).
results.reference: An advance care planning model is feasible for community palliative care services. Quality audit processes are an essential component of the Model with documentation of advance care planning discussion established as an important outcome measure.

results.question: Do preoperative serum C-reactive protein levels predict the definitive pathological stage in patients with clinically localized prostate cancer?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that preoperative serum CRP levels do not show an association with the presence of a locally advanced tumor stage in patients with clinically localized prostate cancer. Although elevated CRP levels correlate with higher Gleason scores, multivariate analysis did not confirm CRP as a predictor for definitive pathological stage.

no
contexts: The serum C-reactive protein (CRP (c-reactive protein)) level correlates with the clinical prognosis in patients with kidney, penile and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (PC (prostate cancer)). We prospectively evaluated the preoperative CRP (c-reactive protein) level as a predictive marker for an advanced tumor stage or high-grade cancer in patients with clinically localized PC (prostate cancer).

Poorly differentiated PC (prostate cancer) tends to be more common in patients with elevated CRP (c-reactive protein) levels (15.5 vs. 9.5%, p = 0.08). Analogously, patients with a Gleason score ≥8 PC (prostate cancer) had significantly higher median CRP (c-reactive protein) levels than those with a Gleason score ≤7 PC (1.9 vs. 1.2 mg/l, p = 0.03). However, neither uni- nor multivariate analysis showed an association between the preoperative CRP (c-reactive protein) level and the presence of a locally advanced tumor stage, lymph node metastases or a positive surgical margin. CRP (c-reactive protein) also failed to correlate with the initial PSA (prostate specific antigen) level and the clinical tumor-associated findings. Moreover, multivariate analysis relativized the association between an elevated CRP (c-reactive protein) level and poor tumor differentiation.

To examine the ability of various postoperative nomograms to predict prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM (prostate cancer-specific mortality)) and to validate that they could predict aggressive biochemical recurrence (BCR (biochemical recurrence)). Prostate-specific antigen (PSA (prostate-specific antigen)), grade, and stage are the classic triad used to predict BCR (biochemical recurrence) after radical prostatectomy (RP (radical prostatectomy)). Multiple nomograms use these to predict risk of BCR (biochemical recurrence). A previous study showed that several nomograms could predict aggressive BCR (prostate-specific antigen doubling time [PSADT] <9 months) more accurately than BCR (biochemical recurrence). However, it remains unknown if they can predict more definitive endpoints, such as PCSM (prostate cancer-specific mortality).

The study evaluated 629 patients with clinically localized PC (prostate cancer) who underwent radical prostatectomy between 2010 and 2013. Exclusion criteria were signs of systemic infection, symptoms of an autoimmune disease or neoadjuvant androgen deprivation.

82 patients had flu-PSA (prostate-specific antigen) levels and 129 si-PSA (prostate-specific antigen) levels. There were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of cancer detection, clinical or pathological stage, but the si-PSA (prostate-specific antigen) group with cancer had a higher Gleason score. No difference was found for PSA (prostate-specific antigen) Slope between flu-PSA (prostate-specific antigen) patients with cancer and those without.
results.reference: In patients with clinically localized PC, CRP does not appear to possess the predictive value and it was shown to have patients with other tumor entities or advanced PC.

results.question: Sub-classification of low-grade cerebellar astrocytoma: is it clinically meaningful?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that histological sub-classification and grading systems, including the WHO, Kernohan, and Daumas-Duport classifications, do not have predictive value for survival in children with low-grade cerebellar astrocytomas. Specifically, no difference in survival was found between pilocytic and fibrillary astrocytomas, and the Daumas-Duport system was deemed unsuitable as a prognostic tool. Therefore, sub-classification of low-grade cerebellar astrocytoma is not clinically meaningful in terms of prognosis.

no
contexts: The objectives were to identify prognostic factors for the survival of children with cerebellar astrocytoma, and to evaluate the reproducibility and prognostic value of histological sub-classification and grading.

The overall survival rate was 81% after a follow-up time of 15-40 years. The significant positive prognostic factors for survival were "surgically gross-total removal" of the tumour at surgery and location of the tumour in the cerebellum proper as opposed to location in the fourth ventricle. No difference in survival time was demonstrated when we compared pilocytic astrocytoma and fibrillary astrocytoma. Moreover, we found that the Kernohan and the WHO (World Health Organization) classification systems had no predictive value and that the Daumas-Duport system is unsuitable as a prognostic tool for low-grade posterior fossa astrocytomas.

Children aged 0-14 years treated in Denmark for a cerebellar astrocytoma in the period 1960-1984 were included and followed until January 2001 or until their death. The histological specimens from each patient were reviewed for revised grading and classification according to three different classification schemes: the WHO (World Health Organization), the Kernohan and the Daumas-Duport grading systems.

All tumor cases showed cells positive for GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein). Control tissues showed a few, widely separated vessels. Pilocytic astrocytomas (four cases) showed lacy clusters of small-to-medium sized vessels, with intact vessel wall integrity. Diffuse, low grade astrocytoma (three cases) showed a staining pattern similar to control tissue; intermediate grade (one case), anaplastic astrocytoma (three cases) and gliobastoma multiforme (six cases) showed an increased vessel density with multiple small vessels (glomeruloid clusters), some with prominent intimal hyperplasia, loss of vessel wall integrity, and with numerous vWF (von willebrand factor)-positive single cells/microvessels within the tumor substance.

We evaluated the vascular pattern of 17 astrocytoma surgical specimens (seven from children and 10 from adults), and four normal brains obtained at autopsy, utilizing antibody to glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein)) and von Willebrand factor (vWF (von willebrand factor)) utilizing confocal microscopy. A modified WHO (World Health Organization) classification was used.
